verdict.summary: All dangerous operations in njs_array_prototype_splice are protected by shown in-fragment guards: start is clamped to [0,length] (line 26), delete is clamped to [0,length-start] (lines 32/42), and the deleted allocation is NULL-checked (line 55). verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is constrained by a shown protective statement: delete is clamped to [0, length-start] (line 42), the final length is capped at NJS_MAX_LENGTH (line 47), the deleted-copy loops are strictly bounded by i < delete against arrays allocated with capacity delete (lines 54, 61, 68), and the new-items memcpy (lines 121-122) is gated by items > 0 (line 120) with its write span bounded by the line 42 clamp and the line 103 njs_array_expand capacity growth. verdict.summary: ReadPCLImage writes FormatLocaleString output into heap buffers allocated as AcquireString("") with 1-byte capacity (L186 density, L187 options). Every reachable path overflows them: '%gx%g' always emits at least 4 bytes ('0x0\0'), '2.0x2.0' emits 8 bytes, and '-g%.20gx%.20g ' emits at least 7 bytes, so the writes land past a 1-byte heap allocation (heap-based out-of-bounds write, CWE-787). The command accumulation loop (L115-119) is bounded by the check at L116-117 and is not the finding.

evidence.reason: Sink: FormatLocaleString writes into density, whose capacity is 1 byte because density=AcquireString("") at L186 allocates exactly strlen("")+1 bytes (named callee semantics). The length argument MaxTextExtent only caps output at 4096 bytes and does not match the real capacity; with any two doubles the format '%gx%g' emits at least 4 bytes ('0x0\0'), so the write overflows the 1-byte allocation by at least 3 bytes on every path that reaches L188 (all paths past the delegate_info NULL check at L177). No guard on the straight-line path L186->L189 bounds it (the L116-117 guard governs only command accumulation); absent fix: allocate density with at least MaxTextExtent bytes (e.g. AcquireQuantumMemory) before formatting. Primary CWE-787 heap OOB write.

Sink: FormatLocaleString writes into options, whose capacity is 1 byte because options=AcquireString("") at L187 allocates strlen("")+1 bytes. The format '-g%.20gx%.20g ' always emits at least 7 bytes ('-g0x0 \0'), and page.width/page.height derive from attacker-controlled %lf doubles (L131-146) scaled at L192-195, so the write is a guaranteed heap OOB write (CWE-787) with no protective statement on the straight-line path L187->L197. Same buffer is overwritten again at L204-205 and L207-209. Absent fix: allocate options with at least MaxTextExtent bytes before formatting.

Sink: in ping mode this writes '2.0x2.0\0' (8 bytes) into the same 1-byte density allocation made at L186 (AcquireString("") -> 1 byte), another unguarded heap OOB write (CWE-787). Absent fix: allocate density with adequate capacity before the FormatLocaleString call.

assumptions: AcquireString(src) returns a heap copy of exactly strlen(src)+1 bytes (standard name-implied callee semantics), so AcquireString("") at L186 and L187 yields a 1-byte allocation; this is the object-capacity evidence for the OOB claims.

FormatLocaleString(buf, length, ...) is a length-bounded (vsnprintf-style) formatter whose length argument is the caller-claimed buffer capacity; with length=MaxTextExtent it permits writes of up to 4096 bytes, far exceeding the actual 1-byte capacity.
command, geometry, filename, input_filename are declared char[MaxTextExtent] at L9, L11, L12, L14.
limitations: The double->size_t conversions at L153-154 and L192-195 are undefined for huge attacker-supplied %lf values but feed only arithmetic and formatting inside the fragment, with no memory sink, so they are demoted.
Discarded statuses (AcquireUniqueFilename at L215, RelinquishUniqueFileResource at L226-227) show no in-fragment failing-value consumption path, so no status-handling finding is claimed.
The command accumulation loop (L115-119) resolves PRESENT via the L116-117 '< (MaxTextExtent-1)' bound including the NUL slot, so it is not part of the vulnerability.
Overflow extent per sink is on the order of 3-45 bytes and occurs on any PCL render path, not only on crafted inputs; magnitude scales with page dimensions converted from attacker-controlled doubles.

verdict.summary: RTCP RPSI length field values 0 or 1 make rpsi_len wrap to SIZE_MAX in unsigned arithmetic, so the guard 'length < rpsi_len + 12' wraps back to a tiny bound (4 or 8) and admits a minimal 8-byte buffer; the parser then reads padlen/pt bytes at offsets 8/9 past the validated buffer, an out-of-bounds read.

evidence.reason: Capacity evidence: line 12 only guarantees length >= sizeof(pjmedia_rtcp_common) (8 bytes), so p = hdr+8 (line 22) is the first out-of-range position for an 8-byte buffer. With hdr->length == 0, line 18 assigns (0-2)*4 = -8 to unsigned pj_size_t rpsi_len, wrapping to SIZE_MAX-7; line 19 then evaluates length < (SIZE_MAX-7)+12 == 4, admitting length == 8. The read at hdr+8 is therefore one byte past the validated buffer, and no shown statement excludes the witness (line 12 passes at exactly 8, line 15 passes for compliant pt/count). Absent one-statement fix: enforce a minimum on hdr->length/rpsi_len (e.g. reject rpsi_len < 12) before the line-19 comparison so the wrap cannot subvert it. Primary mechanism: attacker-controlled RTCP header length field drives an unchecked OOB read (CWE-125).

Same wrapped-rpsi_len path admits a minimal buffer: for hdr->length == 0 with length == 8, line 19 passes and this statement dereferences hdr+9, a second out-of-bounds read caused by the absent minimum check on the RTCP length field (CWE-125).

assumptions: pj_size_t is unsigned and pj_ntohs returns pj_uint16_t/promoted int, so (0-2)*4 = -8 converts to a huge unsigned rpsi_len whose +12 wraps to a small value (4 on both 32- and 64-bit builds).
sizeof(pjmedia_rtcp_common) == 8, matching the line-12 minimum length accepted by the fragment.
PJ_ASSERT_RETURN is an active runtime check, not a debug-only assertion.
limitations: The computed size at line 26 is only stored via pj_strset; any downstream dereference/read of rpsi->rpsi is in an unshown caller and is not claimed as an in-fragment finding.
For hdr->length >= 2 the line-19 check is sound for the padlen/pt reads; the confirmed failure is confined to length-field values 0 and 1 where the guard boundary wraps.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected: ca_cert_ is NULL-checked before use, every crypto rc is RELEASE_ASSERTed before outputs are consumed, and hash_length is assertion-constrained to SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH (32) before EVP_DigestUpdate reads hash_buffer (capacity EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE, 64). verdict.summary: xml_parse_node strips the two quote characters from an attribute value without validating the token length returned by pj_scan_get_quotes: line 62 executes 'attr->value.slen -= 2' with no preceding slen>=2 check, so a truncated or unquoted attacker-supplied attribute value (token length 0 or 1) wraps the unsigned length to a near-SIZE_MAX value that is stored in the parse tree and later consumed as a string length, enabling memory corruption.

evidence.reason: Entry-point XML drives pj_scan_get_quotes (line 59), whose returned token length is unconstrained in the fragment (residual range 0..buffer length); the '=' branch guard (line 57) and attribute-loop condition (line 53) admit the path, and no statement binds attr->value.slen >= 2 before the sink. For input ending at an opening attribute quote, slen is 0 or 1, so 'slen -= 2' wraps (pj_str_t.slen is the unsigned size type per library semantics) to a huge length stored via pj_list_push_back (line 65). Absent one-statement fix: 'if (attr->value.slen < 2) on_syntax_error(scanner);' before the quote removal. This is an integer wraparound (CWE-190) on an attacker-influenced length at the confirmed in-fragment sink; downstream heap OOB is not shown in-fragment and is not claimed.

assumptions: pj_str_t.slen is an unsigned length field (pj_size_t), which makes 'slen -= 2' on a 0/1 value wrap to a huge size (standard library type semantics; the definition is not re-declared in the fragment).

pj_scan_get_quotes returns a token that covers the quote characters actually present in the input, so a value whose closing quote is absent (or an unquoted value) yields a token shorter than 2; on_syntax_error is a returning handler because every shown call site continues executing past it.
limitations: OOB reads via '*(scanner->curptr+1)' (lines 12, 17, 80-81, 93) and reads of '*scanner->curptr' at EOF (lines 53, 68, 93) cannot be confirmed because no scanner-buffer end/capacity expression appears in the fragment (capacity-evidence rule).

Unbounded recursion at lines 24/40/83 could enable stack exhaustion on deeply nested XML, but it is not the one-statement difference and is not decisive.
The downstream consumption of the wrapped attr->value.slen (heap OOB read/write) occurs in pj_xml consumers outside this fragment and is therefore not independently confirmed.

verdict.summary: QuantizeV2-style op validates neither the axis_ attribute against the input rank nor the min/max range element count against num_slices. An entry-point input whose axis dimension exceeds the min/max range tensor size drives per-slice indices i in [0, num_slices) into min_ranges/max_ranges and output_min/max_tensor buffers allocated with minmax_shape, producing heap out-of-bounds reads and writes; an out-of-range axis_ (including 0 and values >= rank) also reads past the TensorShape dims array.

evidence.reason: Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). num_slices = input.dim_size(axis_) (line 8) is an entry-point-derived count with no shown minimum or relation to minmax_shape, whose element count bounds both min_ranges (lines 11, 47) and the output buffers allocated with minmax_shape (lines 31-34). Loop 'for (int i = 0; i < num_slices; ++i)' (line 49) admits i = NumElements when num_slices > NumElements(minmax_shape), and this line writes float index i into that 1-element buffer. No shown guard ties minmax_size to num_slices; the missing one-statement fix is 'OP_REQUIRES(ctx, minmax_shape.num_elements() == num_slices, ...)'. Witness survives the BLOCK test: scalar minmax (1 element) with axis_ dim > 1 passes lines 18 and 28 and reaches line 53 with i >= 1.

Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). axis_ is an op attribute with only the 'if (axis_ > -1)' guard (line 7) shown, which admits every axis_ >= 0 with no upper bound. The input dims array has exactly output->dims() entries (input.shape() allocated to output at line 13; output->dims() used at line 42), so axis_ >= rank makes dim_size(axis_) read past the dims array. The absent one-statement fix is a bound check 'OP_REQUIRES(ctx, axis_ < input.dims(), ...)' before this use. Witness: axis_ = 2 with a 1-D input; no shown statement excludes it.

Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) of min_ranges(i) where vec<float>() (line 47) has NumElements(minmax_shape) elements (line 11). With num_slices > NumElements(minmax_shape), i reaches an index beyond the tensor's element count, same missing equality fix as the primary write: 'OP_REQUIRES(ctx, minmax_shape.num_elements() == num_slices, ...)'. The scalar branch (line 18) does not cover this path, and no other guard constrains the sizes.

assumptions: output is allocated with input.shape() (line 13), so input rank equals output->dims() (line 42) and bounds the TensorShape dims array.
axis_ is the op's user-supplied attribute and the input/min/max tensors are entry-point data; the fragment shows no validation of axis_ beyond 'axis_ > -1' (line 7).
output_min_tensor and output_max_tensor capacity is NumElements(minmax_shape) via allocation at lines 31-34.
limitations: flat_inner_outer_dims (line 37) body is unshown; the OOB there is inferred from the standard reshape-at-outer_dim semantics and the in-fragment argument axis_ - 1, which is -1 when axis_ == 0.
Exploitation/corruption downstream of the OOB Write is not demonstrated; the unguarded entry-point value reaching the failing operation is the confirmed failure.
The path with axis_ == -1 / num_slices == 1 is safe and was not used as a witness.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write in GetEXIFProperty: when property[5]=='*' (all=1 mode), key is allocated as strlen(property)+1 bytes (e.g., 7 bytes for "abcde*"), but the case-1 branch calls FormatLocaleString(key,MaxTextExtent,"%s",description), writing a static tag description ("exif:ImageWidth", 16 bytes incl. NUL; at least "unknown", 8 bytes) with MaxTextExtent as the size bound instead of the key buffer's capacity. Reachable with any EXIF profile containing a single directory entry; no shown statement ties the write size to the key allocation (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: property is admitted with any length >5 (line 446 rejects only strlen<=5) and property[5]=='*' sets all=1 (lines 450-458); key=AcquireString(property) (line 762) allocates exactly strlen(property)+1 bytes (7 bytes for "abcde*"). The case-1 FormatLocaleString writes the full static description found in EXIFTag (lines 774-783), e.g. "exif:ImageWidth" (16 bytes incl. NUL) or "unknown" (8 bytes), using MaxTextExtent (4096) as the size bound rather than the 7-byte allocation, so bytes past key[6] are written into the heap (CWE-787). The only guards on the path are the non-empty check (line 442), the lower-bound strlen>5 (line 446), and value!=NULL (line 754); none constrains the write to the key's actual capacity (wrong-bound drift / guard-identity failure for 446). Absent one-statement fix: pass the key buffer's real capacity (strlen(property)+1) as the FormatLocaleString size argument, or allocate key with MaxTextExtent capacity. Witness "abcde*" with an EXIF profile containing one BYTE entry (components=1) survives the BLOCK test.

assumptions: MaxTextExtent is the ImageMagick constant 4096, larger than every EXIFTag description.
FormatLocaleString behaves like vsnprintf, writing at most size-1 chars plus a NUL into the destination.
AcquireString allocates exactly strlen(source)+1 bytes (standard semantics).
EXIF profile contents (profile/GetStringInfoDatum) are attacker-controlled file data; only the shown length/offset/format checks constrain them.
EXIFTag table (lines 99-394) supplies static bounded description strings.
limitations: ReadPropertyByte's empty-length behavior is in the unshown callee; the signature scan (lines 532-547) is not used as a finding.
OOM in AcquireQuantumMemory would set value=NULL and skip the key block; the witness relies on the normal successful small allocation.
OOB reads through multiple-value/byte paths were examined and are guarded by q bounds (lines 608-610), dir_offset span checks (lines 636-643), and p guards (lines 651, 732); demoted.
The case-2 'unknown' FormatLocaleString is unreachable because tag_value <= 0x1FFFF, so only the <=7-byte '#%04lx'/'@%04lx' forms execute there; demoted.
Default-case SubstituteString growth comes from callee standard semantics and was not needed for the verdict.
Verdict rests solely on the shown statements and the BLOCK/BREAK tests; no membership-identity inference was used.

verdict.summary: The PORT command handler formats attacker-controlled integers into a 16-byte stack buffer with sprintf without any range check, allowing a stack buffer overflow via components large enough (e.g., 2147483647); the sscanf return value is also discarded, permitting use of uninitialized ints.

evidence.reason: addr is declared as char addr[INET_ADDRSTRLEN] on line 4 (16 bytes including NUL per standard semantics); a-d are entry-point-derived ints from sscanf's %d at line 14 with full INT_MIN..INT_MAX residual range and no shown bound. Named absent fix: per-component 0-255 check or snprintf(addr, sizeof(addr), ...) before the sink. Primary CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow.

sscanf's return value is discarded at line 14; when the attacker sends a PORT argument that yields fewer than 6 %d conversions, e and f are uninitialized and are read here (and a-d at line 15) with no initialization or status check shown. This independently confirmed use of uninitialized data classifies as CWE-457.

assumptions: char addr[INET_ADDRSTRLEN] on line 4 has capacity 16 bytes including the NUL terminator (standard POSIX INET_ADDRSTRLEN semantics).
sscanf %d conversions admit the full int domain INT_MIN..INT_MAX, so each parsed component can be up to 10-11 characters.
limitations: Downstream corruption/exploitation from the overflow is not modeled; the overflow itself is the confirmed failure.
The e*256+f port computation (possible int wrap) is a logic concern only and is not used as a finding.
str is assumed to be network-supplied PORT command data per the handler name and its parsing context, but the caller is not shown.

verdict.summary: No confirmed dangerous operation admits a failing value: the only sink with an in-fragment failure set (consuming tmp after a failed digest_final) is protected by `if (ret) goto end;`, which excludes every nonzero status before memcmp. Negative-len and md-capacity/NULL candidates are demoted because their failing values have no in-fragment producer or shown capacity.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the only sink with a confirmable failure set: tmp allocated by xmalloc(len) (line 7) is consumed by memcmp (line 13) only after digest_final (line 9). The guard evaluates the exact returned status with no intervening modification, admits only ret==0 (success), and executes on every path reaching line 13, so a digest_final failure can never reach the uninitialized tmp compare. All other candidates (negative len from digest_length, md NULL/short buffer) are demoted: digest_length's name-implied semantics return a non-negative length and no in-fragment statement can produce a negative value or constrain/prove md's capacity.

assumptions: xmalloc has standard semantics: it never returns NULL and aborts on allocation failure (line 7).
digest_length returns the digest's byte length, a non-negative value, per name-implied standard semantics (line 4).
digest_final returning 0 means the digest was written into tmp (lines 9-10).
limitations: A negative len reaching xmalloc/memcmp as a huge size_t is not confirmable: the only producer is the unshown callee digest_length, and a negative return is non-standard; additionally, standard xmalloc aborts on the resulting huge allocation unless the environment overcommits.
md's buffer capacity is never shown, so an out-of-bounds read of len bytes from md cannot be established (capacity-evidence rule).
A NULL md dereference by memcmp is not confirmable: no shown statement can make md NULL.

If digest_length could legitimately return 0, memcmp(md,tmp,0) would always compare equal and verify would pass without comparing bytes; this depends on unshown digest_length semantics and is not demonstrated in-fragment.

verdict.summary: restore_index (int, fully unconstrained entry-point value) is used directly to element-index the flat views of entry-point input tensors: tensor_name_t at line 16, and context->input(2) at line 53 when restore_slice is true. No statement ties restore_index to either tensor's element count, so indices equal to NumElements, greater, or negative reach the flat-view operator() unguarded, causing an out-of-bounds heap read (CWE-125). The absent one-statement fix is OP_REQUIRES(context, restore_index >= 0 && restore_index < tensor_name_t.NumElements(), ...) before line 16, with an analogous bound against input(2).NumElements() before line 53.

evidence.reason: restore_index retains its full int domain (no shown constraint anywhere in the fragment; only input(0)'s size is checked at lines 7-8, purely for file_pattern). It reaches tensor_name_t.flat<tstring>()(restore_index) on every path, and the flat view's extent (the tensor's NumElements) is likewise unconstrained entry-point data, so any index >= element count or negative is admitted by every guard on the path (there are none). Reverse scan confirms no excluding statement; the absent fix is OP_REQUIRES(context, restore_index >= 0 && restore_index < tensor_name_t.NumElements(), ...) inserted before line 16. This is an attacker-controlled out-of-bounds heap read, CWE-125.

On the restore_slice==true path the same unconstrained restore_index indexes context->input(2)'s flat view; the only preceding gate (line 51) is the restore_slice flag itself, which cannot bound the index, and the shape_spec.empty() test (line 54) executes after the read, so it cannot block the OOB. CWE-125.

Tensor::flat<T>() exposes an extent equal to the tensor's own NumElements (standard Tensor API semantics); that extent is the object capacity for the indexings at lines 16 and 53.
new checkpoint::TensorSliceReader never returns NULL, so reader is non-NULL on both branches (line 27's if replaces any NULL cache result).
limitations: The exact element counts of input(1)/input(2) are not quoted as literals in-fragment; the flat-view extent is the only capacity evidence, so the witness is stated as index-vs-NumElements rather than against a fixed constant.
reader->CopySliceData (lines 77-79) is bounded internally by reader/slice metadata; no in-fragment producer of an oversized copy is shown, so it was not counted as a finding.
The dtype error message at line 44 prints expected_output_dtype(0) while comparing expected_output_dtype(restore_index) at line 42; this is a display inconsistency with no memory-safety impact.

Protective statement for the input-counting write: the guard excludes kEllipsisLabel (-1) on every path reaching the sink, and MapToLabels' standard semantics assign only consecutive integers in [0, num_labels-1] as real labels, whose max equals the capacity at line 30 minus one. BREAK test survives (identity: same label, no intervening modification; boundary: max admitted = capacity-1; degenerate: -1 excluded; reach: guard precedes sink unconditionally).

Protective statement for the output-counting write: guard excludes kEllipsisLabel (-1) on every path; admitted labels are in [0, num_labels-1] against the vector resized to num_labels at line 38, so the largest admitted index is capacity-1. BREAK test survives by the same four checks as the input-counting sink.

A successful ParseEinsumEquation call yields at least one input subscript (splitting any left side yields >=1 piece, or the call fails and line 11 returns early), so num_inputs >= 1 on the reaching paths; capacities for the [0]/[1] accesses derive from the shown resizes at lines 27 and 30.

The Status of MapToLabels at lines 21 and 23 is unchecked, but any labels pushed on a partially failing parse still fall in [0, num_labels) or equal kEllipsisLabel, so the ignored status cannot create an OOB index at the shown sinks (robustness concern only).

The redundant check at line 49 (label == kEllipsisLabel with label >= 0) was not credited as protective; the actual protection for lines 50-53 is the strict loop bound at line 48 against the shown resizes.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in Compute is protected by an in-fragment guard: dims are required non-negative (line 18) and equal (line 14), zero output/inner dims early-return (lines 26, 30), the transposed-tensor path rejects zero dims (lines 85-88), and the output allocation is status-checked (line 23), so no admitted value reaches an unguarded sink.

OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK return from Compute on failure, so output is non-null after line 23.
k2's only use is the k == k2 equality (line 14); with k >= 0 enforced, k2 is non-negative on all surviving paths.
m*n with m,n <= INT_MAX is at most 2^62 and does not overflow the int64 element count.

DoMatMul's body is not shown; it is assessed only via its shown arguments (2-D matrices, dims >= 1, consistent inner dim, m x n output), and no in-fragment producer of a failing value reaches it.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is guarded: the sparse-path transpose/shuffle/DoMatMul of `right` is protected by the `right->dim_size(0) != 0` and `right->dim_size(1) != 0` checks (L75/L77), which pass the BREAK test (identity, boundary, degenerate, reach); the dense-path Eigen contract is protected by `k == k2` (L14) plus the `k == 0` early return (L21); bfloat16 conversions and the zero-fill are bounded by same-shape allocations. No operation admits an unconstrained failing value.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statements for the transpose sink (L85-89) and the subsequent DoMatMul (L95-103). Entry-point-controlled `right` dims would otherwise be able to be 0, causing a degenerate shuffle/transpose. The guards constrain the same `right->dim_size` int64 values consumed by `TensorShape({right->dim_size(1), right->dim_size(0)})` (L81) and by the matrix views, with no intervening reassignment (L91 executes only after the shuffle), on every path inside `if (transpose_b)` (L72). Admitted set {1..2^63-1} intersects the failure set {0} in the empty set; BREAK identity/boundary/degenerate/reach all pass.

evidence.snippet:
OP_REQUIRES(ctx, k == k2,
                errors::InvalidArgument(
                    "Matrix size incompatible: a: ", a.shape().DebugString(),
                    ", b: ", b.shape().DebugString()));
evidence.reason: Protective statement for the dense-path Eigen contract (L51-52), whose `dim_pair` contracts exactly a's k-axis against b's k2-axis (L48-49). `k == k2` admits only equal inner dimensions, and `if (k == 0)` (L21) returns before the contract, excluding the zero-size contraction. The `if (transpose_b)` branch and the DoMatMul calls are reached only in the sparse path (the dense path returns at L53).
`new Tensor` does not have a NULL-failure standard outcome, and `OP_REQUIRES_OK` (L19) aborts the op on allocation failure, making `output` non-null at every subsequent use.

The transpose branch's zero checks reject legitimate empty-output matmuls when the dense operand must be transposed; that is a fail-closed error, not a security finding.

verdict.summary: In IsConstantFoldable, the loop over the shape_map entry for node n (line 26) bounds i only by the shape-vector length, then passes i to n->output_type(i) at line 29. No shown guard ties i to the node's output count, so a shape-map vector longer than the node's number of outputs admits i >= num_outputs and reads past the node's output-type array (out-of-bounds read).

The absent one-statement fix is adding 'i < n->num_outputs()' to the loop condition. A shape_map entry whose vector length L exceeds the node's output count k admits i = k on line 29, an out-of-bounds read of the node's output types (CWE-125); the line-26 guard constrains only the shape vector and admits the failing index.

The product out_shape.num_elements() * DataTypeSize(n->output_type(i)) could overflow for extreme shapes, but there is no in-fragment memory sink consuming that product, so it is recorded as a defensive-hardening concern, not a confirmed finding.

verdict.summary: afra_box_read reads global_entry_count (line 35) from the bitstream with no bound check against the remaining box size and feeds it directly to the loop at line 36, which allocates a GF_GlobalAfraEntry and inserts it into a list each iteration (lines 37-39). A crafted box with the global_entries flag set and global_entry_count=0xFFFFFFFF drives ~2^32 heap allocations and list insertions, causing uncontrolled memory consumption. The analogous entry_count loop is capped by the guard at line 14, but that guard constrains only entry_count, leaving the global loop unguarded.

evidence.reason: global_entry_count is an entry-point u32 read at line 35 (gf_bs_read_u32) with no shown constraint after the line 33 flag check; the loop head consumes it directly as the iteration bound, so it keeps its full [0, 2^32-1] domain. The forward scan shows no protecting statement: line 14's guard (if (ptr->size / ( (ptr->long_offsets ? 16 : 12) ) < ptr->entry_count) return GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE;) constrains only entry_count (wrong-object drift, class 2), and the ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE calls are macros whose expansion is unshown and therefore not credited. Witness: global_entries=1 with global_entry_count=0xFFFFFFFF yields ~4.29e9 iterations, each executing gf_malloc (line 37) and gf_list_insert (line 39), i.e. uncontrolled memory consumption (CWE-400). The absent one-statement fix is a size-vs-count bound check before line 36, e.g. if (ptr->size / (8 + (ptr->long_ids ? 8 : 4) + (ptr->long_offsets ? 16 : 8)) < ptr->global_entry_count) return GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE;.

The per-iteration heap allocation is the resource-exhaustion sink: with the unconstrained global_entry_count from line 35/36, this statement runs once per attacker-chosen iteration count, each also growing the list at line 39, so total allocations scale with the unconstrained count rather than with the byte payload the box actually contains, confirming CWE-400. The line 38 NULL check protects against malloc failure but does not bound the count.

assumptions: ptr->size is the box's remaining payload size, consistent with its use at line 14 and its decrement by the ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE macro calls (lines 6, 22, 25, 28, 34, 41, 44, 48, 53, 57).
First-loop per-entry payload is exactly 12 bytes (long_offsets=0) or 16 bytes (long_offsets=1), matching the line 14 divisor, so that guard's boundary aligns with the first loop.
Global-loop per-entry payload is 20-32 bytes (lines 41-60), so any equivalent fix must use that divisor.
limitations: ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE is a macro whose expansion is not shown; per the analysis rules it is not credited as a protective statement, so a real build that aborts early on a short box is not considered here.
gf_bs_read_* EOF behavior is assumed safe internally; no out-of-bounds bitstream read is claimed at fragment level.
No fixed-capacity array is indexed by i (lists grow dynamically), so no CWE-787-style OOB candidate is asserted; the confirmed failure is uncontrolled resource consumption.
Practical impact (host OOM behavior) depends on the execution environment.

verdict.summary: The bitstream-derived element count nbFields (line 20, range 0..2^31-1) reaches gf_sg_vrml_mf_alloc and both decode loops with no upper-bound check, so a small crafted BIFS file forces an uncontrolled multi-gigabyte allocation and/or up to 2^31-1 node allocations/iterations (CWE-400).

evidence.reason: nbFields is read directly from the entry-point bitstream at line 20 with residual range [0, 2^31-1]; no shown statement caps it before this allocation, so a 36-bit crafted vector header forces allocation for up to 2^31-1 elements. The absent one-statement fix is a bound check limiting nbFields (e.g. 'if (nbFields > MAX) return GF_NON_COMPLIANT_BITSTREAM;') before the alloc; the status check at line 30 constrains the callee result, not the count (wrong-object drift). CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption.

In the MFNODE branch the same uncapped attacker-controlled nbFields drives up to 2^31-1 iterations, each allocating and registering a GF_Node and appending it to the child list (lines 41-75), with no pre-loop size cap; the same absent nbFields bound check would neutralize this. CWE-400.

assumptions: gf_bs_read_int returns the field value within the requested bit width, so NbBits is in [0,31] and nbFields is in [0, 2^31-1].

gf_sg_vrml_mf_alloc standard semantics are to allocate storage for the given element count and return an error on failure (body unshown); gf_bifs_dec_node returns NULL on decode failure (handled at lines 42/77-78).
Both the MFNODE and non-MFNODE branches consume the same unconstrained nbFields; either branch path suffices for the finding.
limitations: Callee bodies (gf_sg_vrml_mf_alloc, gf_bs_read_int, gf_bifs_dec_node) are unshown, so an integer overflow inside the allocator's size computation is not used as evidence.
Practical impact depends on allocator/OS behavior; a failed allocation may be returned as a handled error. The finding is unbounded resource consumption / DoS, not demonstrated memory corruption.
get_item indexing (line 33) is contractually in-bounds (i < nbFields equals the line-29 allocation count) and is not flagged.

verdict.summary: When the axis attribute is 0, the guards admit it (L7-9 require only input.dims() > axis_), the fragment computes axis_ - 1 == -1, and line 80 passes this negative value as the dimension-index argument (begin) to flat_inner_outer_dims<float, 3>, which indexes the input shape with -1 (heap out-of-bounds read) and produces a 3-D extent for dim1 that no longer matches num_slices, leaving the subsequent chip<1>(i) access unconstrained. The absent one-statement fix is a check that axis_ > 0 (axis_ >= 1) before the call.

evidence.reason: axis_ is an entry-point op attribute whose residual range after the shown guards (L7 branch axis_ > -1, L8-9 input.dims() > axis_) is [0, dims-1], which includes 0; at L80 the fragment itself computes axis_ - 1 = -1 and passes it as the begin dimension index to flat_inner_outer_dims, whose standard contract requires 0 <= begin < ndims. A -1 index reads the input shape's dim array out of bounds (CWE-125) and yields a dim1 extent not equal to num_slices, so the loop index i at L94 is not constrained by the tensor's real extent. The absent fix is OP_REQUIRES(ctx, axis_ > 0, ...) (or axis_ >= 1) before this call; no shown statement on the reaching path excludes axis_ == 0.

Independent sink statement: input_tensor.template chip<1>(i) is executed with i in [0, num_slices) (L92), but when axis_ == 0 the tensor was built from shape[-1] at L80, so its dim1 capacity is not num_slices and the chip access can read past the input data (CWE-125). The guards L21-27/L34-40 bound only the min/max range tensors and do not restore the corrupted input_tensor extent; the absent fix is the same axis_ > 0 check before L80.

assumptions: flat_inner_outer_dims' begin parameter is a rank index into the input shape, with valid domain [0, ndims); -1 violates its standard, name-implied contract.
axis_ and mode_ are op attributes originating from the graph definition (entry-point user-config values), so axis_ = 0 is attacker-suppliable.
allocate_output results are non-null at use because every call is wrapped in OP_REQUIRES_OK (L56, L62-63, L74-77).
limitations: The exact bytes read inside the unshown flat_inner_outer_dims body are not displayed; the in-fragment evidence is the negative index -1 constructed at L80 and passed as a dimension index, with the downstream chip<1>(i) use showing the consequence.
int64 overflow of pre_dim/post_dim accumulation was considered but no in-fragment capacity evidence demonstrates a reachable overflow; not scored.
QuantizeSlice's internal behavior is not analyzed; its inputs are bounded as recorded except for the corrupted input_tensor path described above.

verdict.summary: The sscanf() return value at line 14 is discarded; when the attacker-controlled PORT argument does not match all six %d conversions, some of the uninitialized stack integers a-f are read at line 15 (snprintf) and line 25 (data_port computation). The inet_aton() check at line 18 is evaluated after line 15 and constrains only the formatted address, not the conversion count or e/f, so the uninitialized reads reach the sinks on every partial-match path.

evidence.snippet: snprintf(addr, sizeof(addr), "%d.%d.%d.%d", a, b, c, d);
evidence.reason: Entry-point attacker-controlled str is parsed by sscanf at line 14 with the result discarded; per standard semantics a failed/absent conversion stops and leaves later arguments untouched, so with str="1" only a is set while b, c, d remain uninitialized (declared at line 3 with no initializer) and are read here on every path. The reverse protection scan shows no prior check on the conversion count; the !inet_aton() guard at line 18 is after this read and constrains addr, not a-d, so the witness survives the BLOCK test. Absent fix: check sscanf(...) == 6 before use (or initialize a-f to 0). Primary mechanism: use of uninitialized variable (CWE-457), root cause being the unchecked sscanf return (CWE-754).

With str="1,2,3,4,5" sscanf at line 14 assigns a-e but not f, whose value is uninitialized (line 3, no initializer); inet_aton("1.2.3.4") at line 18 succeeds so this path is admitted by every guard in execution order, and the guard constrains only addr, not f (wrong-object drift), so the reading of uninitialized f (and the signed overflow of e*256+f) reaches this sink unprotected. Absent fix: reject sscanf results != 6 (or initialize a-f). Confirms CWE-457 with the same discarded-status root cause as the primary sink at line 15.

assumptions: sscanf standard semantics: conversion stops at the first failed/absent directive; unmatched output arguments are left unmodified and the return value is the number of assignments (line 14 call).
addr has capacity char[INET_ADDRSTRLEN] = 16 bytes (line 4); snprintf at line 15 writes at most 15 characters plus NUL, so addr is always NUL-terminated for inet_aton (line 18) and strlcpy (line 24).
str is treated as a NUL-terminated C string supplied by the FTP client (entry-point input).
limitations: Signed overflow of e*256+f at line 25 when e,f are fully initialized large ints is UB but secondary; it is not the deciding finding and is not counted as an independent sink.

Whether the continuing path past inet_aton (line 18) is reached depends on the uninitialized bytes forming a valid address; this is stack-layout-dependent UB, but the line 15 uninitialized read occurs on all partial-match inputs regardless, so the verdict does not depend on it.
Potential information disclosure via the DBG (line 27) and ERR (line 19) log formatting of uninitialized-derived data was not counted as a separate finding.

verdict.summary: The gf_bifs_dec_node result is NULL-checked at line 7 before any use on every reaching path, fully excluding the only provable failure set (node==NULL) for all node and ActiveQP dereferences. The dereferences of node->sgprivate, codec->scenegraph, and the un-checked com/inf results have no NULL producer inside the fragment, so they are demoted to limitations rather than confirmed vulnerabilities.

evidence.reason: First dereference of the gf_bifs_dec_node result (line 6). Its NULL-on-failure set is fully excluded by the guard at line 7 (`if (!node) return GF_NON_COMPLIANT_BITSTREAM;`), which executes on every path before this use, constrains the same unmodified `node` value, and leaves residual range node != NULL; BREAK test (identity, boundary, degenerate, reach) passes, so this sink resolves PRESENT; the same guard protects the subsequent node dereferences at lines 17, 22-24, and the node portion of line 27.

assumptions: gf_bifs_dec_node follows NULL-on-failure parse semantics, confirmed by the fragment's own `if (!node)` check at line 7.
`node` is not reassigned or modified between the line 7 check and its uses at lines 16, 17, 22-24, and 27.
limitations: A NULL `node->sgprivate` dereference at line 27 is not confirmable: no statement in the fragment assigns or produces sgprivate==NULL, and assuming the unshown gf_bifs_dec_node body can return a node with NULL sgprivate would attribute non-standard callee behavior, which is prohibited. The candidate would need a guard such as `if (node->sgprivate)`, but no witness survives the BLOCK test.
NULL `codec->scenegraph` (lines 10, 14, 24) has no in-fragment producer; framework member pointers are treated non-NULL absent a shown NULL assignment.
Unchecked NULL returns from gf_sg_command_new / gf_sg_command_field_new (lines 29-30) have no shown failure producer; allocation-failure behavior of these unshown helpers is not in-fragment evidence.
No OOB, injection, crypto, file/access-control, or loop candidates exist: the fragment performs no indexing, copies, or attacker-derived size arithmetic.

verdict.summary: The rank of input/rhs is read via dim_size(ndims - 1) at lines 5-6 before any rank validation executes. A rank-0 (scalar) input makes ndims == 0, so input.dim_size(-1) indexes the tensor's 0-element dimension array out of bounds; a lower-rank rhs likewise makes rhs.dim_size(ndims - 1) read past rhs's dims array. The guards at lines 9 and 12 are evaluated only after these reads, so they protect nothing on those paths; the fix is to move the ndims >= 2 and rhs.dims() == ndims validations ahead of lines 5-6.

evidence.reason: ndims = input.dims() (line 4) is an entry-point-derived value with no shown minimum before this read; a rank-0 input yields ndims == 0, so index ndims - 1 == -1 indexes the input's 0-element TensorShape dimension array (capacity == dims() == 0), an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The only candidate guard, OP_REQUIRES_ASYNC `ndims >= 2` (line 9), executes after this read and protects nothing on this path (guard-after-use). Absent fix: perform the `ndims >= 2` validation before line 5.

rhs's rank is unconstrained before this read; with input rank >= 2 and rhs a rank-0 tensor, index ndims - 1 >= 1 exceeds rhs.dims() == 0, so this reads past rhs's dimension array (CWE-125). The rank-equality guard `rhs.dims() == ndims` (line 12) is evaluated only afterwards and does not protect this path. Absent fix: validate `rhs.dims() == ndims` before line 6.

assumptions: context->input(0)/context->input(1) may carry tensors of any rank, including rank 0, because the fragment shows no rank constraint before the dim_size reads at lines 5-6.

TensorShape stores exactly dims() dimensions, so a valid dim_size index must satisfy 0 <= i < dims(); the fragment itself uses this convention at lines 18/22 where `ndims >= 2` is required before `dim_size(ndims - 2)`.
limitations: The garbage value produced by the OOB read at lines 5-6 is not consumed: the later `ndims >= 2`/rank checks abort before n/nrhs are used, so the demonstrated failure is the OOB access itself rather than downstream corruption.
Potential int overflow of the batch loop variable for batch_size > INT_MAX (CWE-190/835) is not claimed: no shown path produces such a value and the scratch allocation would fail first.
Failure behavior inside unshown callees (GetScratchSpace, CudaSolver construction) is not used as evidence in either direction.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous indexing operation is protected in-fragment: the ellipsis sentinel label is excluded before both counting sinks (L33, L42), and the single-input case is short-circuited before accessing input_label_counts[1] (L53). All remaining indices are bounded by sizes established in the fragment (L27, L30, L39, L49).

evidence.reason: Protective guard for the input-label counting sink: `if (label != kEllipsisLabel)` excludes the only out-of-range label value (the ellipsis sentinel) on every reaching path before `input_label_counts->at(i)[label] += 1`. Real labels are consecutive 0..num_labels-1 (in-fragment comment L13-14 with MapToLabels semantics), and the inner vector has capacity num_labels (L30), so the admitted set is fully in-bounds. BREAK test passes: identity (same label, no intervening write), boundary (admitted set [0, num_labels) vs capacity num_labels), degenerate (sentinel value blocked), reach (guard on every path to the sink).

Protective guard for the output-label counting sink: it excludes the ellipsis sentinel label before indexing `output_label_counts`, which was resized to num_labels (L39). BREAK test passes by the same identity/boundary/degenerate/reach analysis as the input counting sink.

Protective short-circuit for the `(*input_label_counts)[1]` access: `num_inputs == 1 ||` prevents evaluating the index-1 access for single-input equations, and when the expression is evaluated num_inputs is >= 2, so index 1 exists because `input_label_counts` was resized to num_inputs (L27). Index 0 is likewise valid for num_inputs >= 1. BREAK test passes: identity (same num_inputs value used for sizing), boundary (index 1 requires size >= 2, guaranteed by guard order), degenerate (num_inputs==1 is the excluded case), reach (short-circuit executes before the access).

assumptions: MapToLabels assigns consecutive integer labels 0..label_mapping.size()-1 for distinct characters (per the in-fragment comment at lines 13-14), and kEllipsisLabel is the only label sentinel outside that range; the guards `label != kEllipsisLabel` (L33/L42) and `label == kEllipsisLabel` (L51) therefore cover the entire out-of-range set.
ParseEinsumEquation returning Status::OK() (checked at L11) populates input_str with at least one operand token under the standard '->' / ',' einsum grammar, so num_inputs >= 1.

Capacities are established in-fragment: each input_label_counts[i] is resized to num_labels (L30), input_label_counts to num_inputs (L27), output_label_counts to num_labels (L39), and label_types to num_labels (L49).
limitations: The literal value of kEllipsisLabel is not shown; the analysis only requires it to be the unique non-consecutive label value, which L33/L42 exclude (and L51 skips); any in-range collision would be a logic issue, not a memory-safety failure.

A num_inputs==0 out-of-bounds read at `(*input_label_counts)[0]` (L53) was considered and rejected: it would require ParseEinsumEquation (unshown) to return OK with an empty operand list, which the standard einsum grammar cannot produce; if that callee contract existed, the absent fix would be a `num_inputs == 0` guard.
A >2GB equation that could wrap input_str.size() to a negative int (L16) is not derivable within the fragment and is out of scope.

verdict.summary: All in-fragment dangerous operations are protected by fail-closed OP_REQUIRES guards. input(0) is indexed at 0 only after `size == 1` (line 8), and input(1) is indexed at restore_index only after `size > restore_index` (line 18), which excludes every index >= size on the ordinal domain, leaving no surviving witness. The input(2) index (line 60) and expected_output_dtype(restore_index) (line 49) lack any quoted in-fragment capacity, and a negative restore_index has no in-fragment producer, so neither yields a BLOCK-test-surviving witness; both are demoted to limitations.

assumptions: tensor_name_t's element count is `size` (line 17), and flat<tstring>() exposes exactly that many elements, so the valid index domain is [0, size-1].

restore_index is used as an ordinal (0-based) in every shown use and in the guard's own error message 'at least restore_index + 1 elements'; the shown code bounds it above via `size > restore_index` (line 18) with no intervening modification.
All guards use OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK, which abort the kernel path on failure (fail-closed), so a failed check never falls through to the sink.
reader is provably non-NULL on every path: either set by GetReader or, when null, by allocated_reader.get() (lines 30-38), with CHECK_NOTNULL (line 39) as an added check.
limitations: A negative restore_index (e.g., -1) would pass `size > restore_index` (line 18) and underrun tensor_name_t.flat<tstring>() at line 23, but the fragment contains no producer of a negative value; the witness depends entirely on an unshown caller supplying a value outside the function's ordinal contract, so it is not fragment-derivable and cannot support a vulnerable verdict.

context->input(2).flat<tstring>()(restore_index) (line 60) is unguarded, but input(2)'s element count is never quoted in the fragment, so no OOB boundary can be established (CAPACITY-EVIDENCE RULE); demoted.
context->expected_output_dtype(restore_index) (line 49) has no in-fragment capacity for the output-dtype array; demoted for the same reason.

CopySliceData (lines 84-88) could fail inside the callee based on checkpoint-file content, but the fragment shows no concrete failing argument and does check its bool result with OP_REQUIRES; callee-internal behavior is not in-fragment evidence.
`restore_index + 1` (line 21) could overflow only on the abort path with a caller-supplied INT_MAX and requires a failing size; not fragment-derivable and not a security-relevant sink.
The `restore_slice` branch is reachable only when an unshown caller sets restore_slice true; its only index sink (line 60) is covered by the capacity limitation above.

verdict.summary: Signed 32-bit multiplication `memory_size * num_filters` in the state-shape validation can overflow (e.g., 65536*65536 wraps to 0), so the TF_LITE_ENSURE_EQ size check admits a state tensor far smaller than the op requires. Prepare returns kTfLiteOk with the inconsistent state, and the guarded bound is forged by arithmetic overflow; no statement constrains the operands or the product.

evidence.reason: memory_size (line 30, weights_time->dims->data[1]) and num_filters (line 26, weights_feature->dims->data[0]) are entry-point int32 dims with no in-fragment magnitude bound; their product at line 50 wraps on 32-bit int (65536 x 65536 -> 0), so a state with dim[1]==0 passes the validation even though the true product is 2^32. Guards line 27 (rank != 0, witness rank=1), line 28 (num_filters % rank == 0, 65536%1==0), lines 33 and 47-48 all admit the witness because they constrain divisibility/equality, not operand magnitude or product size (guard-identity drift class 2, wrong-object). The absent one-statement fix is a product/bound check before the equality (e.g., TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, num_filters <= INT_MAX / memory_size)). Mechanism: signed integer overflow corrupting the size used by a bounds-validation security decision, admitting an undersized persistent state (CWE-190).

assumptions: The witness assumes C++ int is 32-bit two's-complement, where 65536 * 65536 wraps to 0; the fragment declares memory_size and num_filters as int from int32 dims data.
rank, memory_size, num_filters, and batch_size are model-supplied entry-point values; the fragment imposes no minimum on them.
limitations: OOB reads of dims->data[0]/data[1] on input, weights_feature, weights_time without a NumDimensions check are demoted: the dims-array capacity (dims->size) is not shown in the fragment, failing the capacity-evidence rule.

The actual out-of-bounds consumption of the undersized state happens in the not-shown Eval stage; the confirmed in-fragment failure is the overflow-forged validation guard admitting the invalid state.
Dereferences of quantization.params scale arrays (lines ~184-188) have no shown NULL producer inside the fragment, so they are not findings.
TfLiteIntArrayCreate results are dereferenced without NULL checks; the NULL-on-OOM path is environmental and the sizes are small constants, so it is not verdict-bearing.
INT_MIN / -1 division overflow would require dims value INT_MIN with rank -1; exact-UB-boundary edge, demoted.

verdict.summary: Every inventoried dangerous operation carries a fully-covering protective statement. The only input-derived index reaching a register sink, lv_idx()'s return, reaches gen_move(s, idx, sp, val) only under `if (idx > 0)` (line 45), which excludes every non-positive producer outcome, including the -1 not-found sentinel that is routed to the upvar branch; the guard survives the BREAK test on identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach. The safe-call receiver index `recv = cursp()-1` (line 99) cannot be negative because every path to line 98 has already executed the `push()` at line 87 (when val or sp==cursp()) plus the `push()`/codegen at lines 91-96, so cursp() >= 1. The argument count n from gen_values is normalized (`n < 0` -> 15 with a matching push at lines 107-110) and every remaining outcome (0..14) is handled by the n==14, n<14, and n<15 branches before n is used as an opcode operand; the push/pop_n sequences in NODE_COLON2 and NODE_CALL are balanced by the shown pushes. No residual-range value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the register-index sink gen_move(s, idx, sp, val) at line 47. idx is produced by lv_idx(s, nsym(tree)) at line 44, whose standard semantics return a non-positive sentinel (-1) when the identifier is not a current-scope local; the fragment's own upvar branch (lines 51-53) corroborates that routing. The guard admits only idx >= 1 and excludes idx <= 0, so the not-found/zero outcomes never reach the sink. Guard-identity audit passes (same idx, unmodified, same precision); BREAK test passes: identity (no intervening modification between line 45 and line 47), boundary (smallest admitted value 1 is strictly above the failure boundary 0), degenerate (-1, 0, INT_MIN all fail `> 0`), and reach (gen_move executes only inside the if-block on the idx>0 path). The residual upper range of idx is bounded by lv_idx's internal table semantics; no in-fragment capacity contradicts it.

assumptions: lv_idx (line 44) returns the index of the identifier in the current scope's local-variable table, or a non-positive sentinel (-1) when absent; the fragment's own upvar branch (lines 51-53) corroborates this.

gen_values (line 106) caps its returned positional-argument count at the limit argument (13 or 14) per the call's name-implied semantics, or returns negative for split/variable-length arguments; the fragment explicitly handles n<0, n==14, n<14, and n<15.
codegen(..., VAL) emits exactly one stack value, making the push()/pop()/pop_n() bookkeeping in NODE_COLON2 (lines 68-75) and NODE_CALL (lines 86-161) self-consistent.
The push() at line 87 (when val or sp==cursp()) and the push()/codegen at lines 91-96 execute on every path reaching line 98, guaranteeing cursp() >= 1 and recv = cursp()-1 >= 0.
limitations: The upper bound of lv_idx's return (<= vlen) and the codegen register-pool capacity are not shown in the fragment, so an OOB via an over-large positive idx cannot be demonstrated (capacity-evidence rule); the not-found negative case is the demonstrable failure set and it is excluded.

A gen_values return greater than 14 (without splat) would perturb the n bookkeeping, but producing such a value would require attributing non-standard behavior to the callee despite the explicit limit argument; no in-fragment witness exists, so this is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.
tree and rhs are entry parameters dereferenced at line 4 and elsewhere, but no shown statement can make them NULL; a NULL supplied only by an unshown caller is out of scope.

Whether local index 0 should route to gen_move rather than gen_setupvar (idx > 0 vs idx >= 0) is a potential compile-behavior/correctness concern; both routes are memory-safe within the shown code, so it is not a security finding.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations in IsConstantFoldable resolve PRESENT or non-dangerous. The vector index `shape_it->second[i]` is strictly capped by the in-fragment loop bound `i < shape_it->second.size()` (admitted 0..size()-1, BREAK test passed); the `n->output_type(i)` OOB candidate lacks any in-fragment capacity evidence and is demoted; derefs of `n` have no in-fragment NULL producer; and the size-arithmetic has no surviving wrap-down witness.

evidence.reason: Decisive PRESENT guard for `shape_it->second[i]` at line 26: the strict `<` admits i in [0, size()-1], excluding i >= size(), where the vector capacity is the same in-fragment expression `shape_it->second.size()`. BREAK test passes on all four axes: identity (same `i`, unmodified between check and use), boundary (max admitted index size()-1 is strictly below capacity size()), degenerate (size()==0 gives zero iterations; `i` is int64_t starting at 0 with no negative/unsigned-underflow path), and reach (the condition is re-evaluated before every access on every path). The guard-identity audit shows no drift, so no failing index reaches the sink.

assumptions: Capacity of `shape_it->second` is `shape_it->second.size()`, derived from the verbatim loop condition at line 25.

`num_elements()` returns int64_t and `DataTypeSize` returns size_t per standard TensorFlow API semantics; with `IsFullyDefined()` the element count is non-negative and at most 2^63-1, so any unsigned product wrap leaves a huge residue that still trips the size cap (no bypass witness).
limitations: OOB on `n->output_type(i)` (line 28) is not confirmable: the node's output-type array capacity is not shown in the fragment, and the loop bound is tied to the shape-vector size rather than the node's output count (wrong-object drift, guard-identity class 2); demoted under the CAPACITY-EVIDENCE RULE.
NULL dereference of `n` (lines 9, 15, 18, 35, 43, 46, 49, 57, 64-65) has no NULL producer inside the fragment; a NULL supplied only by an unshown caller is out of scope.
Resource-limit bypass via overflow of `num_elements() * DataTypeSize(...)` is theoretical: no surviving wrap-down witness can be derived from the shown int64 element-count domain.
Log write of `n->DebugString()` (lines 65-66) is a disabled-by-default VLOG path and a low-impact debug-log concern, not the decisive difference.

verdict.summary: In BM_ParseGlobalQuantizer, the result of gf_sg_command_field_new(com) (line 36) is assigned to inf and immediately dereferenced at line 37 (inf->new_node = node) with no NULL check. By the codebase's allocation convention this creation helper returns NULL on allocation failure, so a NULL value admitted by the unchecked producer reaches a direct pointer dereference, causing a NULL-pointer crash (denial of service) on crafted input. The absent one-statement fix is a NULL check on inf before the dereference.

evidence.reason: inf is produced at line 36 by the unchecked creation/allocation call gf_sg_command_field_new(com), whose NULL-on-failure result (call-site evidence) retains the full domain including NULL; the very next statement dereferences it at line 37 with no guard on any reaching path. The only NULL check in the function (line 7) constrains node, not inf (Guard-Identity drift class 2, wrong object), so it admits the failing value. Absent fix: if (!inf) return GF_NON_COMPLIANT_BITSTREAM; inserted between lines 36 and 37. An admitted NULL inf reaching inf->new_node = node is a confirmed NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476), a crash/DoS on attacker-controlled bitstream input.

assumptions: node from gf_bifs_dec_node is non-NULL at all later uses because line 7 returns early on NULL and node is not reassigned in the fragment.

gf_sg_command_field_new is a GPAC creation/allocation helper whose result is NULL on allocation failure (codebase convention used for helper results such as the checked gf_bifs_dec_node result at line 7); its impossible-to-verify allocation failure is the in-fragment NULL producer by call-site evidence.

verdict.summary: In OP_JMPUW, the absolute jump target `a` is computed at line 302 as `(uint32_t)((pc - irep->iseq) + (int16_t)a)` with no runtime range check; the only bound `0 <= a < irep->ilen` is a debug-only mrb_assert (lines 306/308). A negative 16-bit operand (e.g., 0xFFFF) at pc == irep->iseq wraps to 0xFFFFFFFF, and line 322 forms `pc = irep->iseq + a`, causing an out-of-bounds instruction fetch. The absent one-statement fix is a runtime check of `a` against `irep->ilen` before the jump.

evidence.reason: The jump target `a` (uint32_t, full residual domain after line 302's `(uint32_t)((pc - irep->iseq) + (int16_t)a)` wrap) is consumed unbounded at line 322: `pc = irep->iseq + a`. The only capacity reference in the fragment is `irep->ilen` at line 308, but it appears inside `mrb_assert(a >= 0 && a < irep->ilen)` which does not execute in normal builds; line 314's `ch`-conditional constrains `a` only to the catch-handler `[begin,end)` range on one branch. Producer: operand low16 = 0xFFFF (int16 = -1) at pc == irep->iseq gives `a = 0xFFFFFFFF`, admitted by every guard on the path. Absent fix: runtime check `if (a >= irep->ilen)` (raise) before line 322. Mechanism: signed-to-unsigned conversion (CWE-195) yields a huge index that makes the dispatch fetch `irep->iseq + a` an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: irep->iseq capacity is irep->ilen, as named by the fragment itself at line 308.
Instruction operands are decoded from the bytecode stream without runtime validation; the only 0<=a<irep->ilen bound in the fragment is an assertion.
limitations: regs[]/nlocals-based indexing (OP_ARYPUSH 1437, OP_HASH 1562, OP_ENTER 717, OP_APOST 1501-1504, OP_ERR 1756-1760) is demoted because the stack/pool capacity or attacker provenance is not established in-fragment.

OP_JMP/JMPIF/JMPNOT/JMPNIL also lack target-range checks; they are subsumed by the same missing-bound pattern and not separately flagged.
The OOB witness requires a bytecode operand outside a compiler-valid range; it is treated as admitted because the fragment imposes no runtime bound.

assumptions: bin is a file-parsed object whose members are conditionally initialized: the fragment itself tests bin->segment_entries for NULL, establishing within the fragment that bin's member pointers may be NULL.
The loop condition executes before any use of bin->segment_entries on every path reaching the sink.
limitations: S2 (OOB read of bin->segment_entries[i]) is demoted: the fragment shows no verbatim capacity/allocation expression for segment_entries, so the CAPACITY-EVIDENCE RULE prevents an OOB claim in either direction.

S4 ((ut64)se->offset * bin->alignment) is demoted: no dangerous in-fragment consumer of bs->paddr, and a 32-bit x 32-bit product cannot wrap a ut64.

verdict.summary: Every in-fragment dangerous operation is protected. verdict.summary: ReadCINImage computes the per-scanline read size `length` (line 381/385) from attacker-controlled image->columns (343) and image->depth (342), while the only in-fragment capacity tied to the destination `pixels` buffer — `extent` from GetQuantumExtent (379) — is discarded by `(void) extent;` (380). No statement bounds length against extent before `ReadBlobStream(image,length,pixels,&count)` (397) writes up to `length` bytes into `pixels`, so a crafted CIN header (depth > 8, rows = 1, large columns, padded file) causes a heap buffer overflow; the post-write count check (398) and the dimension-product check (350) do not constrain this size.

evidence.reason: Heap-buffer-overflow write (CWE-787): `length` (GetBytesPerRow at 381/385) is derived from attacker-controlled `image->columns` (343, from channel[0].pixels_per_line at 140) and `image->depth` (342, from channel[0].bits_per_pixel at 136, 0..255 with no depth cap); for depth>8 it is ~2x the RGB-scanline extent while the destination `pixels` (388) capacity is the in-fragment `extent=GetQuantumExtent(image,quantum_info,quantum_type)` (379), which is discarded at 380 `(void) extent;`. Guards on the path — 75-76 (image_offset>=712), 350-351 (columns*rows/8 <= GetBlobSize, wrong-bound drift for this sink), 363-368 (SetImageExtent status), 394-396 (q non-NULL) — all admit the witness (rows=1, columns=C, file >= ~6C bytes, image_offset==offset), and the count==length check at 398 executes only after the write inside ReadBlobStream, so it cannot block the overflow. The absent one-statement fix is a length-vs-extent check, e.g. replacing 380 with `if (length > extent) ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"ImproperImageHeader");` before the y-loop.

assumptions: `extent=GetQuantumExtent(image,quantum_info,quantum_type)` (379) is the byte capacity of the scanline buffer returned by `GetQuantumPixels(quantum_info)` (388), per the standard ImageMagick coupling of these helpers.

`GetBytesPerRow(columns,channels,depth,MagickTrue)` returns channels*columns bytes scaled by 2 when depth > 8, plus padding, so with depth=16 (RGB) `length` is ~2x the ~3*columns extent; the padding constants are irrelevant to the asymptotic mismatch.
`ReadBlobStream` copies up to the requested `length` bytes into the supplied `pixels` buffer and then reports `count`, consistent with its name-implied semantics.
limitations: The exact body/constants of GetBytesPerRow, GetQuantumExtent, and ReadBlobStream are unshown; the overflow magnitude and exact boundary rely on their standard name-implied semantics, which the fragment itself demonstrates by computing `length` (read size) and `extent` (buffer size) from the same header values and then discarding `extent` (380).
32-bit integer-wrap variants of the size arithmetic and any depth<=8 padding edge cases were not pursued as independent findings.
The user-data allocation sink (334) is properly guarded by 332-333 and 335-336; the offset-skip loop by 358 and 361-362; those are NOT the vulnerable operations.

verdict.summary: drill_parse_T_code post-increments the gerb_file_t pointer in `tmps = get_line(fd++);` and then dereferences `fd->filename` immediately after, so `fd->filename` reads one struct past the single gerb_file_t object. Absent one-statement fix: replace `get_line(fd++)` with `get_line(fd)`.

No NULL-deref confirmed: g_new0 follows GLib semantics (aborts, never returns NULL), apert is NULL-checked at lines 110/129/186, and no shown producer makes image or stats NULL.

verdict.summary: Every inventoried dangerous operation in ex_retab resolves PRESENT: the rebuilt-line allocation (line 130) is exactly old_len - col + start_col + len + 1, i.e. prefix + new whitespace + tail including NUL, so the prefix memmove (134), tail memmove (135-136) and fill loop (138-139) write exactly the allocated capacity; new_line NULL from alloc or failed u_save is excluded by 131-132 and 161-162 before any dereference; ml_replace status is checked (140-142) before rebinding the line pointer; and the tabstop argument is range-validated (55-59). No failing witness survives the BLOCK test, and every decisive guard passes all four BREAK tests.

The rebuilt line's exact length is prefix (start_col) + new whitespace (len = num_spaces + num_tabs) + tail including NUL (old_len - col + 1); the shown allocation admits exactly that plus one, so the prefix memmove (line 134), tail memmove (135-136) and fill loop (138-139) never write past index capacity-1. The only other NULL producer (u_save FAIL at 122-123) also breaks and is re-caught at 161-162. Reverse protection scan found no reaching path that dereferences NULL.

Status-handling protection: a failed undo save cannot be followed by a line rewrite continuing on the same path; the FAIL branch flags new_line = NULL and both breaks (inner at 123, outer at 161-162) prevent any subsequent use of the buffer state on that path.

Return-status protection: new_line is rebound to curbuf->b_ml.ml_line_ptr only when ml_replace reports OK, keeping ptr consistent with live buffer memory; on non-OK, new_line remains this function's own allocation, which stays valid for lines 143-147, so no stale/freed pointer is consumed.

Entry-point input validation before new_ts reaches the arithmetic at lines 103-110: negative and over-TABSTOP_MAX values are rejected; the residual zero case is substituted with curbuf->b_p_ts (60-61). A zero b_p_ts has no in-fragment producer or constraint, so division-by-zero is recorded as a limitation, not a confirmed witness.

assumptions: ml_get line buffers are NUL-terminated with capacity STRLEN(ptr)+1, consistent with the line-129 STRLEN and line-153 NUL scan in the fragment.
len, num_spaces, num_tabs are non-negative longs: len = num_spaces + num_tabs, with num_spaces from non-negative vcol differences and tabstop_fromto outputs.
alloc and vim_strnsave return NULL on out-of-memory and their results are checked at lines 131 and 40-46.
limitations: curbuf->b_p_ts == 0 would divide by zero at lines 103/109-110 via the substitution at lines 60-61, but no shown statement constrains b_p_ts or produces 0, so it is a framework-invariant robustness concern, not an in-fragment witness.

When a single tabstop value is given, new_vts_array may be rebound to curbuf->b_p_vts_array (lines 40-44), which could be NULL; whether tabstop_fromto (98) and tabstop_count (171-176, 196) tolerate NULL is unshown callee behavior, so any dereference there is not in-fragment evidence.
ml_replace semantics on the copy=FALSE path beyond the call site are unshown; the == OK check protects the rebind in either outcome.
The one-statement pair difference cannot be inferred from this member's appearance; the verdict follows only from the per-sink PRESENT resolutions and BLOCK/BREAK tests above.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched member of the micro-ecc ECDSA signing pair (CVE-2020-27209, commit 'Fix for #168'). It contains the randomized initial-Z countermeasure: 'initial_Z = k2[carry];' inside the RNG branch (L34) and passes 'initial_Z' instead of the vulnerable literal 0 to EccPoint_mult (L36). On the RNG path L31-L33 guarantee a valid pointer; on the no-RNG path NULL initial_Z is the callee's standard Z=1 fallback (the pre-fix code always passed 0). All other candidates (hash_size at L70, s[num_n_words-1] at L66, caller-buffer copies) are demoted for lack of in-fragment capacity or producer. No dangerous operation resolves ABSENT.

evidence.snippet: EccPoint_mult(p, curve->G, k2[!carry], initial_Z, num_n_bits + 1, curve);
evidence.reason: The pair's missing fix is the hard-coded 0 passed as initial_Z (the CVE-2020-27209 SPA weakness); here initial_Z is the randomized projective-Z value. On the g_rng_function path, L31-L33 check uECC_generate_random_int and return 0 on failure, then L34 assigns the valid pointer k2[carry] into tmp/s (uECC_MAX_WORDS, L8-L9); nothing modifies initial_Z before L36, so the BREAK identity/reach tests pass. On the no-RNG path initial_Z stays NULL, which is the callee's standard semantics for Z=1 (the pre-fix member always passed literal 0, so EccPoint_mult must tolerate NULL), i.e. a designed fallback, not a NULL-deref failure. The operation therefore has no admitted failing value.

Decisive protective statement for the EccPoint_mult sink at L36: it supplies a non-NULL, valid pointer derived from a checked RNG result (L31-L33), excluding the failure set (NULL with RNG present) on every path that reaches the sink when randomization is available; combined with the L23 0<k<n check on the scalar, no dangerous operation remains unprotected.

assumptions: uECC_MAX_WORDS is at least BITS_TO_WORDS of every supported curve, so tmp/s/p indexing by num_words/num_n_words stays in-bounds (L8-L9, L15); this is a library-wide constant invariant used by the shown declarations.
EccPoint_mult accepts a NULL/0 initial_Z and falls back to Z=1, evidenced by the pre-fix member of the pair always passing the literal 0 (standard name-implied callee semantics).
g_rng_function is a library-configured global; when set, uECC_generate_random_int result is checked before use (L31-L33).
limitations: hash_size (L3) is passed unclamped to bits2int (L70); any OOB read would occur inside the unshown callee against an unshown message_hash buffer capacity, so it is not confirmable from the fragment alone.

s[num_n_words - 1] = 0 (L66) would underflow to s[(wordcount_t)-1] only if curve->num_n_bits == 0; the curve is an internal-helper parameter with no shown call site or producer of a degenerate value, so it is demoted.
Signature/private_key buffer capacities (L57, L61, L77) are caller-provided and not shown; no in-fragment capacity evidence exists for OOB claims.

The side-channel randomization applies only when an RNG is configured; without g_rng_function the library intentionally falls back to Z=1, which is a design trade-off of the fixed member rather than a confirmed vulnerability.
bcopy direction/argument semantics (L61, L77) write into caller-supplied buffers; no capacity or contract violation is demonstrable in-fragment.

verdict.summary: pipePath is copied into sun_path with strncpy without a length check or explicit NUL termination; a path of length >= sizeof(local.sun_path) leaves sun_path unterminated, and the subsequent C-string consumers unlink()/chmod() read past the stack array.

evidence.reason: pipePath (line 4) is an unconstrained entry-point string with no shown length cap. strncpy (line 15) bounds the write at sizeof(local.sun_path) but, when pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path) (108), appends no NUL, leaving sun_path without a terminator. unlink(local.sun_path) consumes it as a NUL-terminated C string and over-reads the stack array (CWE-170 root cause; CWE-125 over-read). The absent one-statement fix is a length rejection such as 'if (pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path)) throw...' before line 15; the reverse scan finds no guard on the path that excludes this witness.

Same failure as the unlink sink: sun_path is unterminated when pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path), and chmod() reads it as a NUL-terminated string past the 108-byte array. The missing length/NUL-termination guard (line 15 region) is absent, so this sink also resolves ABSENT with the same surviving witness.

bind() consumes the same unterminated sun_path produced when pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path), so the missing-NUL failure (CWE-170) applies to this consumer as well; the confirmed out-of-bounds reads are the unlink and chmod sinks, while bind's consumption is bounded by addrlen and fails as a non-terminated pathname.

assumptions: The capacity of local.sun_path is anchored in-fragment by sizeof(local.sun_path) used as the strncpy bound at line 15.
endpoint.name() has no shown minimum/maximum, so pipePath retains its full string domain.
limitations: The return value of ::listen() is discarded; no security consequence is identified from the shown code.
The return value of unlink() is discarded; this is consistent with intentional stale-socket cleanup and is not flagged.
bind() reads at most sizeof(sockaddr_un) bytes, so its failure is the non-terminated pathname (CWE-170 logic), not an out-of-bounds read.

verdict.summary: In create_cache_bins the dependent-image walk reads depArray[k] and then uses depArray[k]&0x7fff as dep_index to write deps[dep_index] and read img[dep_index]. The loop index k is never bounded against the shown capacity depListCount (line 41) and dep_index is never bounded against imagesCount (lines 19/32), while both arrays' contents are file-derived, enabling heap out-of-bounds reads and writes.

evidence.reason: depArray has exactly cache->accel->depListCount ut16 elements (allocation at line 41, filled from the file at line 46). k is a ut32 starting at the unconstrained file value extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex and increments with no upper bound; the condition only tests the array contents for 0xffff. When the attacker suppresses the terminator within the depListCount entries, or sets the start index >= depListCount, the condition reads depArray[k] with k >= depListCount — a heap out-of-bounds read. Every path to this line passes only non-NULL checks (42, 51, 77) and the fill-length check (46); none bounds k. Absent fix: add k < cache->accel->depListCount to the loop condition. Primary CWE-125.

dep_index = depArray[k] & 0x7fff has residual range 0..32767 and is never compared against the shown capacity of deps, cache->hdr->imagesCount ints (allocation at line 19). A file-supplied depArray entry with a large masked value and a small imagesCount yields dep_index >= imagesCount, so deps[dep_index]++ performs a heap out-of-bounds write (read-modify-write of the int). Absent fix: check dep_index < cache->hdr->imagesCount before the increment. Secondary CWE-787.

img is sized by hdr->imagesCount (read at line 32 and indexed with j < hdr->imagesCount at line 58), but dep_index is unconstrained up to 32767 and is used unchanged to form &img[dep_index], reading past the image array when dep_index >= hdr->imagesCount. Absent fix: the same dep_index < hdr->imagesCount bounds check before this use. Same root cause, CWE-125.

assumptions: depArray capacity is cache->accel->depListCount ut16 elements, established by the allocation at line 41 and the matching fill at line 46 (both in-fragment).
deps capacity is cache->hdr->imagesCount int elements per the allocation at line 19.
img contains hdr->imagesCount entries per the loop bound at line 58 using the same hdr->imagesCount used by read_cache_images at line 32.
depListCount, depArray contents, and extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex originate from the parsed dyld-cache file, i.e. entry-point input.
limitations: deps[j] at lines 59/65/75 is a secondary candidate: deps is sized only by the first header's imagesCount (line 19) while j is bounded by each hdr[i].imagesCount (line 58); it is not needed for the verdict.
cache->maps[maps_index] at line 107 is demoted: maps_index is unvalidated against cache->n_maps, but the dereference occurs inside the unshown va2pa.
A depListCount so large that the R_NEWS0 allocation fails is handled by goto next at line 43 and is not a finding.

verdict.summary: Malformed dyld-cache file data reaches dependency processing without index bounds checks: depArray contents (l.46) are masked to [0,0x7fff] (l.80) and used to index deps[] (capacity cache->hdr->imagesCount, l.19) at l.81 and img[] at l.83, and the sentinel loop at l.79 reads depArray past its depListCount-element allocation, enabling a heap out-of-bounds write plus out-of-bounds reads.

evidence.reason: Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). dep_index derives from attacker-controlled depArray[k] read from the file at l.46; the only constraint is the mask l.80 `dep_index = depArray[k] & 0x7fff`, admitting [0,0x7fff], while deps[] has capacity cache->hdr->imagesCount (allocation l.19). For any N = cache->hdr->imagesCount <= 0x7fff, dep_index = N is admitted by every guard in execution order (l.77 extras/depArray non-NULL, l.46 read-count check, l.79 sentinel, l.80 mask) and reaches `deps[dep_index]++` unmodified; no check bounds dep_index against the capacity. The absent one-statement fix is a bound check such as `if (dep_index >= hdr->imagesCount) continue;` before l.81.

Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). depArray[] is allocated with cache->accel->depListCount ut16 elements (l.41) and k starts at the unvalidated, file-supplied extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex (l.50/79) with no `k < depListCount` guard; a start index >= depListCount (or 0xFFFFFFFF) makes the first `depArray[k]` access read past the allocation, and the data-controlled 0xffff sentinel can be suppressed so k advances without bound. Missing one-statement fix: a `k < cache->accel->depListCount` bound in the loop condition.

Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The img[] array is consumed with extent hdr->imagesCount by the shown loops (l.58, l.102), but here it is indexed by the same unbounded dep_index (l.80, [0,0x7fff], no check vs hdr->imagesCount) produced by attacker-controlled depArray contents; the only subsequent guard, `if (!dep_name) break` at l.84, runs after the OOB indexing. Missing one-statement fix is the same dep_index bound check placed before l.83.

assumptions: depArray[] capacity is cache->accel->depListCount elements (l.41) and deps[] capacity is cache->hdr->imagesCount elements (l.19), both shown as in-fragment allocations.
img[] extent equals hdr->imagesCount, evidenced by the in-fragment consuming loops bounded by hdr->imagesCount at l.58 and l.102.

depArray contents and extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex are supplied by the parsed dyld-cache file (l.46, l.50) and are therefore attacker-controlled unless validated, and no content validation is shown.
limitations: No in-fragment capacity is shown for cache->maps[], cache->hdr_offset[], or cache->maps_index[], so the accesses at l.29-31 and l.106 are not claimable as OOB and were demoted.

deps[j] reads at l.59 and l.103 compare current-hdr imagesCount against the first header's imagesCount used for deps[] capacity; the equality/difference of the two header counts is not shown, so this mismatch was not promoted to a finding.
If r_buf_read_at at l.111 fails, magicbytes is read uninitialized at l.112; demoted because the value only selects a display branch and no security decision or additional memory access depends on it.
Unchecked strdup results at l.135-143 could append a bin with NULL file; demoted as no in-fragment consumer of bin->file is shown.
