The do-while body then writes mch_memmove(newp,oldp,col) plus zero insert copies (L536-540 iterates 0 times) plus STRMOVE(ptr, oldp+col) writing oldlen-col+1 bytes, totaling oldlen+1 bytes into the oldlen-byte allocation -> heap out-of-bounds write. Capacity is the in-fragment allocation L531; the absent one-statement fix is a lower-bound check on count (e.g. 'count <= 0' at L502 / 'count < 1'), which would exclude -1 and every negative; its absence lets the negative residual range of the entry-point 'long count' reach the copy. verdict.summary: The visual-range command-modifier rewrite memmoves are fully guarded: the path to mch_memmove(cmd_start-5, ...) and mch_memmove(eap->cmd-1, ":'<,'>", 6) requires `if (eap->cmd > cmd_start)` (line 328), which admits len = eap->cmd - cmd_start >= 1 and excludes the len==0 underflow that would write 6 bytes at orig_cmd-1; the use_plus_cmd memmove/STRCPY are bounded by STRLEN-to-NUL plus the fixed +5 prefix offset. No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: Write sink derived from eap->cmd -= 5 (line 348): dest = orig_cmd + len - 1 where len = eap->cmd - cmd_start. Capacity evidence: orig_cmd = eap->cmd (line 7), cmd_start = orig_cmd + 5 (lines 24-25), buffer NUL at index >= orig_cmd + 5 + len. Guard `if (eap->cmd > cmd_start)` (line 328) admits len >= 1 and excludes len == 0, so dest >= orig_cmd and the 6-byte write ends at index orig_cmd+len+4 < NUL; the would-be failure (len==0 writing 6 bytes at orig_cmd-1, CWE-787 via pointer underflow) is blocked on the only reaching path. Resolves PRESENT; BREAK test passes (identity, boundary, degenerate, reach).

Copy length eap->cmd - cmd_start is >= 1 only because of the same guard at line 328 (`eap->cmd > cmd_start`), which excludes length 0; dest = orig_cmd, and dest+len <= old eap->cmd - 5, strictly inside the NUL-terminated command buffer. Resolves PRESENT; BREAK test passes.

assumptions: eap->cmd points into a writable, NUL-terminated command buffer; string-traversal loops (lines 34, 92) stop at NUL, so every eap->cmd position used for memmove endpoint math is an in-buffer byte at or before the terminator.
mch_memmove and STRCPY follow standard C semantics (overlap-safe; NUL-terminated string copy).

limitations: `switch (*p)` (line 100) dereferences skip_range's return without a NULL check, but no in-fragment statement can make it NULL and skip_range's name-implied semantics do not document NULL-on-failure, so no NULL producer is demonstrated.
`atoi((char *)eap->cmd) + 1` (line 316) could overflow on very long digit runs, but atoi overflow is implementation-defined and cmod->cmod_verbose has no in-fragment memory sink.
`cmod->cmod_tab = tabnr + 1` (line 279) boundary vs LAST_TAB_NR depends on unshown tab-index capacity and an unshown consumer; no in-fragment OOB is demonstrated.
vim_regcomp on an attacker regex (line 190-191) is a potential ReDoS concern, but no concrete blow-up witness is present.
The use_plus_cmd rewrite (342-343) leaves eap->cmd pointing past the new NUL; the consumer is unshown and reads stay in-buffer, so this is logic-only, not a memory-safety finding.

Primary mechanism: out-of-bounds stack write of attacker-influenced extent (CWE-787).

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations in createRandomCursorExecutor are protected by in-fragment statements. The line 14 `numRecords <= 100` early return excludes zero/negative/≤100 record counts on every path to the sharded ratio division at line 67, leaving a denominator ≥ 5.05. The line 91 `!(bucketUnpacker && numRecords)` guard excludes empty record counts and a disengaged optional before the timeseries division at line 124 and the `*bucketUnpacker` dereferences at lines 131 and 143. The random-cursor null check (line 35), executor status check (line 162), and `trialStage` null short-circuit (line 170) also pass the BREAK test. No witness survives the BLOCK test.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the sharded ratio division at line 67. The `numRecords <= 100` clause returns before `sampleSize / (numRecords * kMaxSampleRatioForRandCursor)` executes on every path to it (the division is nested in the same non-timeseries branch), so the residual domain reaching the sink is numRecords >= 101 and the floating denominator is at least 101 * 0.05 = 5.05. Excluded set: {numRecords <= 100}, including the degenerate 0 and negative cases. BREAK test passes on identity (same numRecords, unmodified), boundary (guard boundary 100 is strictly below the first admitted safe denominator), degenerate (0/negative all returned), and reach (guard precedes the sink on all paths).

Decisive protective statement for the timeseries path. It executes before the division at line 124 and the `*bucketUnpacker` dereferences at lines 131 and 143, excluding numRecords == 0 (which would make `kCoefficient * numRecords * gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount` a zero NaN-producing denominator) and a disengaged `bucketUnpacker`. Excluded set: {numRecords == 0, bucketUnpacker disengaged}. BREAK test passes: no intervening modification of either value, degenerate zero count is returned, and the guard sits on every reaching path ahead of the sinks.

assumptions: sampleSize and numRecords are entry-point-derived (aggregation $sample size and collection record count), but the verdict relies only on the shown guard boundaries, not on any assumed caller contract.

gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount is a server-side parameter with no shown attacker-controlled producer; a zero value would only produce an IEEE floating-point non-finite result with no dangerous consumer inside the fragment.
limitations: The result of CollectionShardingState::get (lines 49-51) is dereferenced without a NULL check, but no in-fragment statement can produce a NULL from it, so a NULL-deref finding would require unshown producer behavior and is demoted.
A NaN/infinity ratio, if one were produced, would flow into the unshown TrialStage body; the harm is outside the fragment and is not treated as a confirmed failure.
invariant() on line 10 is debug-only and is not credited as a protective statement.

verdict.summary: sug_filltree drives the trie-walk depth from spell-file data (sl_fbyts/sl_fidxs) with no cap against MAXWLEN before writing to the MAXWLEN-sized stack arrays tword, arridx, curi and wordcount. A crafted spell file whose case-folded trie contains a path of MAXWLEN non-NUL bytes makes depth reach MAXWLEN, causing stack out-of-bounds writes at tword[depth] (line 58) and at arridx[depth]/curi[depth]/wordcount[depth] after the post-increment (lines 86-89).

evidence.reason: Write into tword[MAXWLEN] (capacity declared at line 8) at index depth. depth is incremented once per non-NUL byte of the entry-point spell-file trie (line 86) and no shown statement bounds it against MAXWLEN; the loop condition at line 35 only enforces depth >= 0, and the guards at lines 37/55/77 constrain node byte counts, c, and byts[n+1] respectively, not depth. Witness: a case-folded trie path of exactly MAXWLEN non-NUL bytes reaches depth == MAXWLEN with c == 0, admitted by every guard in execution order. The absent one-statement fix is a depth bound (e.g., 'if (depth >= MAXWLEN) return FAIL;') before the write. Mechanism is an out-of-bounds stack write -> CWE-787.

After the post-increment at line 86, this writes arridx[MAXWLEN] (capacity declared at line 6) when depth was MAXWLEN-1 and a non-NUL byte is consumed; curi[depth] (line 88) and wordcount[depth] (line 89) overflow identically. The same missing depth-vs-MAXWLEN bound that fails line 58 leaves these writes unprotected; the idxs[n] read side is not used as a finding because sl_fidxs capacity is not shown in the fragment. Same CWE-787 stack out-of-bounds write mechanism.

assumptions: Capacities of tword, arridx, curi and wordcount are MAXWLEN as declared at lines 6-9 and 13.
byts is paired with sl_fbyts_len, evidenced by the bound check at line 77.
sl_fbyts/sl_fidxs are spell-file-derived (entry-point) data, consumed with no shown content validation.
limitations: idxs capacity is not established in the fragment, so idxs[arridx[depth]] (line 40) and idxs[n] (line 87 read) OOB candidates are demoted rather than findings.
byts[arridx[depth]] (line 37) and byts[n] (line 54) reads would rely on a trie well-formedness invariant not fully visible in the fragment; not used as findings.

The depth witness assumes an attacker can supply a case-folded trie path of length >= MAXWLEN; any external word-length cap imposed by the unshown spell-file reader would block it, but no such cap appears in the fragment and is not credited in either direction.

verdict.summary: No dangerous operation in the fragment admits a failing value that reaches an in-fragment sink. The refill and delete of pkt are gated by the checked ipf_handle_frag status (L17) into mutually exclusive branches; the batch array capacity is not shown, no NULL producer is shown, and the freed-packet and double-ownership failure mechanisms are consumed only by unshown callers/callees. verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in esp_output_head is protected by an in-fragment guard: the skb_shared_info frag-array index is bounded by `skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS` (lines 30-31) before `__skb_fill_page_desc` (56-57); the tail writes/`pskb_put` are bounded by `tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)` (line 24) on the inplace path and by the `skb_cow_data(skb, tailen, &trailer)` contract with the `if (nfrags < 0) goto out;` failure check (80-81) on the cow path; and the page-frag path checks `skb_page_frag_refill` (42-45) before any page/offset use. evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the `__skb_fill_page_desc(skb, nfrags, page, pfrag->offset, tailen)` sink at lines 56-57. It bounds the frag-array index: line 54 reads the identical, unmodified `skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags` into `nfrags`, so the admitted index set is 0..MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1 against the `frags[]` capacity MAX_SKB_FRAGS (the guard literal is the capacity evidence). Boundary value MAX_SKB_FRAGS is excluded, degenerate 0/MAX-1 are in bounds, and this guard sits on the only path to the sink, so the BREAK test (identity, boundary, degenerate, reach) passes.

Decisive protective statement for `esp_output_fill_trailer(tail, ...)` (line 86) and `pskb_put(skb, trailer, tailen)` (line 87) on the inplace path. It admits exactly tailen in 0..skb_tailroom(skb); equality exactly fills the tailroom so the write region [tail, tail+tailen) stays inside capacity, `tailen` is not modified between the check and the uses, and a negative tailen promotes to a huge unsigned value and fails the guard. BREAK test passes.

Decisive protective statement for the page-frag path sinks `get_page(page)` (48), `page_address(page) + pfrag->offset` (50) and the line-52 trailer fill: refill success (standard callee semantics) guarantees a usable page with at least allocsize >= tailen bytes from pfrag->offset, and any failure is redirected to `cow` before the page/offset is consumed. BREAK test passes.

Decisive return-status check for the cow path: `skb_cow_data(skb, tailen, &trailer)` (line 79) contractually yields *trailer with >= tailen writable tailroom, and this check fails closed (`goto out`) before `tail`/`trailer` are consumed at lines 82, 86 and 87, so no error value reaches a sink. assumptions: MAX_SKB_FRAGS is the capacity of skb_shared_info->frags[], evidenced by the guard comparing nr_frags directly against it at line 30.
skb_cow_data(skb, tailen, &trailer) guarantees at least tailen bytes of writable tailroom in *trailer (standard kernel contract used with pskb_put).
skb_page_frag_refill success guarantees a usable page with at least allocsize bytes available at pfrag->offset (standard callee semantics).
esp_output_fill_trailer writes at most tailen bytes (trailer fill = plen + tfclen layout established by the unshown esp_output caller).
limitations: A negative or overflowing esp->tailen would defeat the tailroom/paging guards at the pskb_put/fill sinks, but no shown statement can produce it; producing it requires an out-of-fragment caller contract violation, so it is demoted.

esp->tfclen and esp->plen are unconstrained within the fragment; a caller violating plen+tfclen <= tailen could overrun the guarded tail region, but no in-fragment producer or constraint shows this, so it is not a finding.
allocsize = ALIGN(tailen, L1_CACHE_BGES) appears to be a transcription typo for L1_CACHE_BYTES; treated as a cache-line alignment whose expansion is unshown but preserves allocsize >= tailen.

Every path reaching this sink is guarded: fast path by line 19 `if (tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb))` where trailer == skb, admitting tailen in [0, tailroom] with the equality at tailroom being an exact fit (consumption is exactly tailen bytes; tailroom is the capacity, no +1/NUL), and negative tailen is excluded by the int-vs-unsigned comparison; cow path by lines 74-76 `nfrags = skb_cow_data(skb, tailen, &trailer); if (nfrags < 0) goto out;` whose standard semantics guarantee tailen bytes in trailer on success. PRESENT. The descriptor index nfrags (= skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags at line 49) is constrained by line 25 `(skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS)`, admitting 0..MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1 against the frags[MAX_SKB_FRAGS] array (indices 0..MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1 valid); no statement between the check and the use modifies nr_frags. skb_cow_data and skb_page_frag_refill behave per their standard kernel semantics: success guarantees tailen bytes of room in the trailer, and a page-frag available at pfrag->offset.

ConstrainColormapIndex has the name-implied standard semantics of constraining an index into the colormap range (returning a value < image->colors).

The comment-read count at 152 is discarded; a truncated id_length field could leave uninitialized heap bytes embedded in the 'comment' image property (robustness/information-disclosure only, no memory-safety sink in the fragment).

It admits only the exact configuration optlen == 4 + exportnamelen + 2 + 2*nrinfos, so the maximum read covers indices optlen-2..optlen-1, inside the buffer data[0..optlen] allocated at line 38 (optlen+1; filled 0..optlen-1). Without this check the loop would be an OOB read (CWE-125); the check is present and suffices.

The surviving witness rests on the degenerate boundary value colormap_index == 0 and on name-implied standard semantics of AcquireImageColormap/ConstrainColormapIndex with a 0-entry colormap; if AcquireImageColormap(image,0) instead returned failure, the throw at L191 would abort before the sink (DoS only, no memory-safety finding), which limits confidence to the sub-0.7 band.

verdict.summary: reserve_sfa_size() never constrains the entry-derived int attr_len, so a negative value (residual full int domain) makes NLA_ALIGN produce req_size = (size_t)-4; that value overflows the u32 actions_len at the out: increment (line 36), and a subsequent reservation then memcpy()s the wrapped length 0xFFFFFFFC into a newly allocated buffer whose actions capacity is only new_acts_size - offsetof (about 4092 bytes), causing a kernel heap out-of-bounds read/write at line 29.

A second call with attr_len=4096 then reaches this memcpy via the expand path: line 11 admits the path (4096 <= 256-20 is false), line 14 sets new_acts_size=max(20+4096,256*2)=4116, line 16's clamp is skipped (4116 <= MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE), line 26 passes, and memcpy copies 0xFFFFFFFC bytes while acts->actions has capacity only 4116 - offsetof(sw_flow_actions,actions) ≈ 4092 bytes (capacity from lines 14/25), so the write overruns the heap object and the source read overruns the 256-byte old buffer. The capacity guards constrain req_size/new_acts_size, not the copied actions_len (wrong-object drift), and none excludes 0xFFFFFFFC. Absent fix: a minimum validation on attr_len at entry, e.g. 'if (attr_len <= 0) return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);'. Primary mechanism: heap out-of-bounds write in memcpy (CWE-787).

actions_len is u32 while req_size is size_t; with the unconstrained attr_len=-5, req_size is (size_t)-4 (2^64-4), so the compound assignment wraps: 0 + (2^64-4) mod 2^32 = 0xFFFFFFFC, corrupting the length that line 29 later copies unchecked. This u32 overflow (CWE-190) is the in-fragment producer whose corrupted value reaches the memcpy sink, and it is the independently confirmed secondary mechanism.

assumptions: attr_len is entry-point-derived (netlink attribute length) with no shown minimum, so the full int domain is residual.
NLA_ALIGN semantics: ((len)+3)&~3 evaluated in size_t; implied 64-bit size_t and 32-bit int/u32 as in kernel builds.
Initial buffer is freshly allocated with actions_len=0 and ksize*2 <= MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE so the expand path is taken instead of the EMSGSIZE clamp on call 1.

params_len (data[aid_len+3]) is an unvalidated u8; with aid_len large and a short admitted frame, the source range skb->data[aid_len+4 .. aid_len+4+params_len) exceeds skb->len (CWE-125) and the params_len-byte write exceeds the L26 skb->len-2 allocation (CWE-787). The struct nfc_evt_transaction layout is not shown; the memcpy overflow claim relies only on the shown allocation capacity (skb->len - 2 at line 26) versus the shown copy length (transaction->aid_len), so it holds regardless of field offsets.

The vulnerability requires the gzip path (state->wrap & 2) and a caller that did not call inflateGetHeader; this precondition is consistent with the fragment treating state->head as nullable.

It compares the exact pointer pair (y_current_used vs y_current and y_current->y_array vs y_array) that the later read consumes, so a register swap cannot leave a freed y_array dereferenced. Protects the one-line insert path: with L504 excluding count==0 and yanklen==0, the admitted count is [1, INT_MAX/yanklen], so totlen=count*yanklen (L514) cannot overflow int, and alloc(totlen+oldlen+1) (L533) exactly covers the col + count*yanklen + (oldlen-col+1) bytes written at L536-543. BREAK test: identity (no intermediate modification), boundary (product bounded before alloc), reach (executes before the writes on every iteration) - survives.

The fragment shows no producer or path that drives a negative count to those sinks (the only count==-1 test at L59 returns before them), so this witness is not fragment-derivable and is demoted rather than confirmed.
Cursor-column invariants (col <= oldlen) underlying L159/536/543/591/608 come from unshown editor state, not from a shown in-fragment constraint; no shown statement violates them.

Callees whose bodies are unshown (u_save, ml_append, get_yank_register, changed_lines, alloc, vim_strchr) are analyzed only through their shown call sites and standard name-implied semantics.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations are protected in-fragment: the allocation is NULL-checked (L15), both r_buf_read_at calls are validated with `available != size` before any use of the buffer (L19, L56), the `size < 32` floor guarantees every memcmp/dereference of b stays in bounds (L11), and the write side of each read cannot exceed b's malloc'd capacity. Negative `off` (and the retry's `off - 8`) can underflow to huge ut64 addresses, but per standard bounded-read semantics that yields a short/error return which the `!= size` checks abort on; an OOB dereference inside the unshown callee is not demonstrated by the fragment and is not attributed.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the primary read sink. `b` has capacity exactly `size` (malloc at L14), so the callee cannot overflow the destination; any standard failure (out-of-range address from negative `off` promoted to a huge ut64, partial read, or int-len truncation when size > INT_MAX) yields `available` < size or -1, which L19 diverts to return NULL before `b`'s contents are consumed. BREAK test: identity — the check constrains the same call's return against the same requested size; boundary — the `!=` comparison admits only an exact full bounded read; degenerate — negative offsets, short reads, and truncations are all excluded; reach — the check executes on every path before the memcmp uses. PASS.

Same decisive status check for the retry read. For `off < 8`, `off - 8` underflows negative and is promoted to a huge ut64 address; under standard bounded-read semantics this returns -1/short, which L56 catches and aborts before `b` is used; the destination remains capped at the malloc'd `size` (L14). BREAK test: identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach all PASS as for L19.

Allocation failure set (NULL) is fully excluded: `if (!b) return NULL;` executes on every path before any dereference of `b`. Combined with the L11 `size < 32` floor (admitted values ≥ 32 while the largest in-fragment access is `b+8`..12 bytes), all subsequent reads of `b` are in bounds. BREAK test: identity (same pointer), boundary (NULL only), reach (all paths). PASS.

assumptions: `r_buf_size(buf)` (L3) returns the buffer extent N ≥ 0, and `r_buf_read_at` is a bounded read whose name-implied semantics return -1 or an actual short count for out-of-range addresses; the fragment's `available != size` checks rely on and enforce that contract.
The `D { ... }` debug block (L67-70) containing `r_read_le32 (b + 12)` is compiled out or at worst bounded, since `size >= 32` guarantees 16 readable bytes.
limitations: Negative `off` passes the L4 `off >= size` check and inflates `size` (L7) beyond the buffer extent, and `off - 8` underflows for `off < 8`; an OOB dereference inside the unshown `r_buf_read_at` body would be a vulnerability, but that requires attributing non-standard unbounded behavior to the callee, which the rules forbid — the shown status checks neutralize the standard failure outcomes.
A large allocation (up to N + 2^31 for `off = INT_MIN`) is a weak resource-amplification concern; `malloc` failure is handled and no confirmed exhaustion witness was shown, so it is demoted.
`off + 16` (L72) is passed to the unshown `r_coresym_cache_element_new`; no in-fragment failure set for that callee can be demonstrated, so it is not a finding.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected. The only memory-safety sink is the strlcat option-assembly chain into mnt_opts: line 79 allocates calloc(MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN, 1) (capacity MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN), line 80 ('if (mountent.mnt_opts)') excludes a NULL allocation result on every path into the block, and every strlcat passes MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN as its size, so all writes are confined to bytes 0..MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN-1; the mount_user append (98-99) is additionally guarded by 'if (mount_user)' at line 96. All status-bearing operations (setreuid, sigfillset, sigprocmask, toggle_dac_capability, lock_mtab, setmntent, fileno, fstat, addmntent, my_endmntent) are checked before their results are used, and discarded cleanup returns have no subsequent security-relevant consumer on the same path.

evidence.reason: Capacity evidence and NULL guard for the option buffer: calloc allocates exactly MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN bytes (line 79) and the guard at line 80 executes on every path that reaches the strlcat chain, excluding a NULL allocation result before any strlcat deref. Combined with the per-call size argument, the OOB failure set (write past byte MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN-1) has an empty intersection with the admitted set; BREAK test passes for identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach.

Representative bounded sink: every strlcat call passes the same size MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN as the allocation size at line 79, so writes are capped at MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN bytes (last index MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN-1) with the NUL terminator inside the buffer; any accumulated-options overflow truncates rather than writing out of bounds; same guard/bound on lines 84, 87, 89, 91, 93, 95, 97, and 98-99.

NULL guard for the getusername(uid) result (line 13): getusername can return NULL, and guard 96 on every path to the strlcat at lines 98-99 excludes that NULL before the deref, so no NULL-deref witness survives the BLOCK test.

Representative return-status check: addmntent's status is checked and, on failure, the partial write is rolled back via ftruncate (107) and EX_FILEIO propagated; the same check-then-use pattern covers setreuid (21), sigfillset (28), sigprocmask (34), toggle_dac_capability (40), lock_mtab (45), setmntent (52), fileno (60), fstat (68), and my_endmntent (111), so no unchecked status feeds a subsequent operation.

assumptions: Buffer capacity is established in-fragment by the calloc expression at line 79 (MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN bytes) and the identical size argument in every strlcat call.
strlcat standard semantics: writes at most size bytes including the terminating NUL, and requires dst capacity of size (satisfied by the calloc size).
callee standard semantics: setmntent/fileno/fstat/addmntent/my_endmntent return documented error indicators, all of which are checked before use.
limitations: The numeric value of MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN is not shown, but only the equality alloc-size == strlcat-bound is needed; any consistent value is safe.

addmntent serialization of devname/mountpoint/fstype (lines 76-78, 104) could in principle inject newline content into the plain-text advisory mtab file; there is no interpreter consumer inside this fragment and no in-fragment sanitization requirement demonstrated, so this is demoted, not a confirmed finding.
Cleanup return values (atexit at 43, ftruncate at 107, toggle_dac_capability(1,0) at 118, final sigprocmask at 119) are discarded, but no statement after them consumes their success on the same path.

A NULL mnt_opts reaching the unshown libc addmntent body on calloc failure is speculative: libc behavior for a NULL opts field is not a documented named failure mode, and the deref would occur inside the unshown callee.
devname/mountpoint/fstype provenance is caller-side; the fragment never dereferences them, so no NULL-deref witness can be constructed in-fragment for them.

verdict.summary: http_isfiltered reads the fixed-size hdf/hd header arrays with the fully unvalidated unsigned index u: the only shown range test (u < HTTP_HDR_FIRST, line 8) runs after the first access and imposes only a lower bound, so large values (e.g. u = UINT_MAX) reach out-of-bounds reads at lines 6, 10, and 13.

evidence.reason: u is an unsigned parameter with full domain 0..UINT_MAX and no shown producer constraint; no upper-bound check precedes this read (the line-8 test executes after it and admits every u >= HTTP_HDR_FIRST), so u = UINT_MAX values at or beyond the hdf array capacity reach the index and cause an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The absent one-statement fix is an upper-bound guard such as 'if (u >= HTTP_HDR_LAST) return (0);' placed before this line.

On the path reaching this line the line-8 guard admits exactly [HTTP_HDR_FIRST, UINT_MAX]; no upper bound is imposed, so the same witness (u = UINT_MAX, beyond the hd array size) reaches this second indexed read of the fixed-size array — an independent out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) that the same absent upper-bound guard would neutralize.

Argument evaluation re-reads fm->hd[u].b under the same admitted set [HTTP_HDR_FIRST, UINT_MAX] from the line-8 guard; u = UINT_MAX produces the same out-of-bounds read as the line-10 sink, and the returned f is separately and correctly NULL-checked at line 14, which does not protect this index.

assumptions: fm->hdf and fm->hd are fixed-size array members (accessed by an enum-like header index), so their element count is far below UINT_MAX and u = UINT_MAX is out of bounds for them.
fm is treated as non-NULL because the fragment shows no NULL producer for it.
limitations: The exact array sizes (e.g. HDRS/HTTP_HDR_LAST) are not quoted in this fragment, so the precise out-of-bounds threshold is inferred from the fixed-size indexed accesses and the missing upper-bound guard rather than a verbatim capacity literal.
Whether a caller can supply the offending u is not shown; the candidate stands on the fragment's own unguarded unbounded index.
strchr over-read on a non-NUL-terminated fm->hd[u].b and behavior inside the unshown http_hdr_flags were demoted for lack of in-fragment capacity/body evidence.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation with in-fragment capacity evidence is protected: the dire->name copy and NUL write (lines 86-88) are bounded by the guard `dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN` (line 81) against the SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN+1 bytes reserved for the name (line 5), and dir->dirs[] indexing (lines 107-111) is bounded by the shown realloc growth (lines 99-101). Read-side and destination-size claims lack in-fragment capacity evidence and are demoted.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the sink `memcpy(dire->name, directory_table + bytes, dire->size + 1)` (lines 86-87) and the NUL write at `dire->name[dire->size + 1]` (line 88). It excludes dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN; the admitted set 0..SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN-1 writes at most index SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN, within the SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN+1-byte name region reserved by the buffer at line 5. The guard executes on every reaching path before the sink with no intervening modification of dire->size; the BREAK identity, boundary, degenerate (size=0, size=255), and reach tests all pass, so the failure set (index LEN+1, i.e. size >= LEN) is empty in the admitted set.

Bounds protection for the dir->dirs[dir->dir_count] reads/writes at lines 107-111: the realloc triggers exactly when dir->dir_count is a multiple of DIR_ENT_SIZE, so the element capacity after the call is dir->dir_count + DIR_ENT_SIZE, strictly greater than the index being written; the index never exceeds the shown allocated count.

assumptions: SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN is one compile-time constant feeding both the guard (line 81) and the buffer reservation (line 5), so the guard's admitted maximum (size+1 == SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN) stays inside the 257-byte (LEN+1) name region.
squashfs_dir_entry_2.name is a trailing (zero-length/flexible) member, so dire->name begins at offset sizeof(squashfs_dir_entry_2) and the buffer leaves SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN+1 usable bytes for it.
DIR_ENT_SIZE is a small positive constant, so dir->dir_count + DIR_ENT_SIZE is always larger than the current index.
limitations: directory_table's allocation size is not shown, so the read-side overruns at lines 53, 56, 72-73, 76-77, and 86-87 (entry/header/name reads that can pass the logical `size` boundary inside the inner loop) cannot be confirmed out-of-bounds and are demoted under the capacity-evidence rule.
struct dir_ent.name capacity is not shown, so the destination size of strcpy at line 107 cannot be confirmed.
read_inode's failure semantics are not shown; no NULL producer for *i exists in the fragment.
SQUASHFS_SWAP_DIR_ENTRY_2 / SQUASHFS_SWAP_DIR_HEADER_2 macro bodies are not shown; only their fixed-width field swaps are relied on.
The computation `size = (*i)->data + bytes` (line 48) could wrap for extreme attacker values, but no in-fragment capacity links that size to an allocation, so it is not used as evidence.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations with a demonstrable failure set are protected: every strlcat into mountent.mnt_opts is guarded by the non-NULL check at line 62 and bounded by the same MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN capacity used by the calloc at line 61; the username append is NULL-guarded at line 78 and size-bounded; all security-relevant return statuses (setreuid, sigfillset, sigprocmask, toggle_dac_capability, lock_mtab, setmntent, addmntent) are checked before continued use. The only residual candidate, a NULL mnt_opts reaching addmntent on calloc failure, is OOM-only and addmntent's standard glibc behavior prints '(null)' rather than dereferencing it, so it is recorded as a limitation, not a vulnerability.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for all seven strlcat sinks (lines 64-81): the guard is evaluated after the calloc at line 61 (capacity MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN, NULL on failure) and excludes the NULL failure value on every reaching path; each strlcat size argument equals the allocation capacity, capping writes at capacity-1 characters plus NUL. BREAK test passes: identity (same pointer, no intervening modification), boundary (max write index MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN-1 within [0, MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN)), degenerate (NULL dst excluded, empty src harmless), reach (every strlcat executes only inside this block).

Protects the username append (lines 80-81) from a NULL lookup result of getusername(uid) at line 12; the append is also size-bounded by MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN so an arbitrarily long username is truncated, not overrun. BREAK test passes: identity (constrains the same value consumed), boundary (size argument equals capacity), degenerate (NULL excluded), reach (guard is on the only path to both strlcats).

assumptions: MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN is the same positive constant used for the calloc allocation (line 61) and as the size argument of every strlcat, tying the object capacity to the write bound in-fragment.
strlcat(dst, src, size) writes at most size-1 bytes plus a NUL terminator within dst[0..size-1]; a NULL dst is excluded by the line-62 guard.
getusername(uid) can return NULL under lookup semantics; it is consumed only under the line-78 guard.
calloc returns NULL on allocation failure; that NULL reaches addmntent only on the OOM path.
limitations: mountent.mnt_opts can be NULL at addmntent (line 86) when calloc fails, because the line-62 guard covers only the option-building branch; this is OOM-only and addmntent's standard glibc behavior prints '(null)' for a NULL %s argument rather than dereferencing it, so no in-fragment failure is demonstrated — a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
Ignored cleanup statuses (endmntent line 91, toggle_dac_capability line 95, sigprocmask line 96) have no shown security-relevant consumer.
devname/mountpoint/fstype contents are written verbatim to mtab; whitespace could corrupt entries, but this is inherent to the design and not a memory-safety or injection sink in the shown scope.
No attacker-controlled producer for allocation failure or for a NULL username is demonstrated inside the fragment.

verdict.summary: In mobi_parse_index_entry, the label length read from the entry (uint8, 0..255) is bounded only by entry_length (line 22), never by the stack buffer capacity INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX+1 declared at line 26. An entry whose entry_length >= label_length > INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX reaches the label-copy calls at lines 29/31, which write up to 255 bytes into the small stack array text, causing a stack-based buffer overflow before the NUL terminator.

evidence.snippet: label_length = mobi_indx_get_label((unsigned char*) text, buf, label_length, indx->ligt_entries_count);
evidence.reason: label_length from mobi_buffer_get8 (line 21) has residual range [0, min(entry_length,255)] after the line 22 check, with no bound against the in-fragment stack capacity INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX+1 (line 26). The line 16/22 guards constrain only buffer-remaining bytes and entry_length (wrong-bound drift), so any value in [INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX+1, min(entry_length,255)] reaches this call, which per its name-implied semantics writes label_length bytes plus NUL into text — a stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-121). The absent one-statement fix is an added check `if (label_length > INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX) return MOBI_DATA_CORRUPT;` after line 22.

evidence.snippet: label_length = mobi_getstring_ordt(ordt, buf, (unsigned char*) text, label_length);
evidence.reason: Same absent bound on the ordt2 branch: an admitted label_length in [INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX+1, min(entry_length,255)] is passed as the write length for the stack array text (capacity INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX+1, line 26), producing the same stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-121); the witness label_length=255/entry_length=255 passes lines 16 and 22 and survives the BLOCK test.

assumptions: INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX is a small compile-time constant (< 256) such that the stack array at line 26 has capacity INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX+1 smaller than the 8-bit maximum 255 of label_length; the fragment's own declaration is the quoted capacity expression.
indx->entries has at least total_entries_count elements, since line 10 is the only shown entries bound.
mobi_buffer_get8 yields the full uint8 range 0..255 with no in-fragment minimum.
limitations: The line 7 read idxt.offsets[curr_number + 1] is a potential OOB read, demoted: the offsets array capacity is not shown in the fragment.
entry_length computed as an unsigned difference could underflow if offsets are non-monotonic, demoted: the fragment shows no ordering guarantee and buffer-error paths cap downstream consumption.
Raw control_bytes[0] reads (lines 65-70) are demoted: the capacity of buf->data beyond the entry end is not shown.

The line 42 strncpy read of label_length+1 bytes from text is an additional OOB read (CWE-125) sharing the same missing bound; it is not counted as an independent finding because it depends on the same admitted label_length and on the absence of an early NUL in text.

verdict.summary: thread_call pushes the roottable and nparams-1 argument values onto the target thread's fixed-size stack with no capacity reservation or bound check (no sq_reservestack call). An attacker-controlled argument count (nparams = sq_gettop(v)) drives unchecked Push/sq_move writes past the thread's stack buffer, causing a heap-based buffer overflow (CVE-2022-30292).

evidence.reason: Sink: per-iteration unchecked write into the target thread's fixed-size _stack. nparams (line 5) is an entry-point-derived count (1 + number of script arguments to thread.call) with no shown minimum/maximum; the loop admits i = 2..nparams (line 7), so nparams values are pushed via sq_move (= dest->Push = _stack[_top++]=o, no bounds check) while the thread's stack capacity was fixed at creation and can be far smaller (e.g., 2*closure_stacksize+2). A script call t.call(a1..aK) with nparams > capacity writes past the buffer: heap-buffer-overflow (CWE-787). No capacity guard exists on any path to this sink (line 4 constrains only the object type; line 9's SQ_SUCCEEDED check runs after the writes). Absent one-statement fix: sq_reservestack(_thread(o), nparams + 3); before line 6.

Sink: first unbounded write into the target thread's fixed-size stack, executed unconditionally on the OT_THREAD path; no sq_reservestack/capacity check precedes it, so even this write can overflow when the thread's stack is already near capacity (top+1 >= capacity). Same failure set and absent fix as the loop sink; primary CWE CWE-787, heap-buffer-overflow write of an attacker-influenced value.

assumptions: SQVM::Push compiles to _stack[_top++] = o with no bounds check and no stack growth (upstream sqvm.cpp).
sq_move(dest, src, idx) = dest->Push(stack_get(src, idx)).
A thread's stack is a fixed-size buffer allocated at creation (SQVM::Init does _stack.resize(stacksize); base_newthread sizes it as 2*closure_stacksize+2).
nparams = sq_gettop(v) is bounded only by the source VM's stack, which is routinely much larger than a small thread's capacity.
limitations: The thread stack's numeric capacity is not literally declared inside the fragment; it is fixed at thread creation (unshown, structural). The finding rests on the in-fragment unbounded count (nparams) feeding unchecked writes (OOB-ONLY EXTRA), and matches the documented upstream CVE-2022-30292 fix (added sq_reservestack(_thread(o), nparams + 3)).
Post-overflow behavior inside sq_call (line 9) is downstream corruption caused by the overflow, not an independent second finding.
No NULL-deref or injection sinks were identified in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment contains no dangerous operation that admits an unconstrained value. The visual-selection state is validated by the early return `if (rex.reg_buf != curbuf || VIsual.lnum == 0) return FALSE;`, the match line is range-gated by `if (lnum < top.lnum || lnum > bot.lnum) return FALSE;`, and every column check is fail-closed (`return FALSE` on mismatch). No memory write, indexing, string, or interpretive sink exists with a shown in-fragment failure producer.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for any invalid-visual-position flow: it excludes the degenerate state VIsual.lnum==0 (and foreign regex buffers) before visual positions are consumed at lines 21/27 and passed to getvvcol/win_linetabsize. BREAK test: identity — it constrains the same VIsual object later read into top/bot, with no intervening modification; boundary — it excludes exactly 0 and admits only 1-based buffer lines; degenerate — 0/NULL/MAXCOL sentinels are excluded or handled at line 66; reach — unconditional early return executes on every path before the first use. This guard survives the BREAK test, so the position-consumption flows are fully constrained.

evidence.snippet:
if (lnum < top.lnum || lnum > bot.lnum)
	return FALSE;
evidence.reason: Range gate that fully bounds the match line computed at line 47 to the visual span [top.lnum, bot.lnum] before either mode branch consumes positions (lines 53-69). Fail-closed: any out-of-range value returns FALSE. BREAK test: identity (lnum is not modified between the guard and its uses), boundary (admits exactly the visual range, rejects below/above), degenerate (zeroed saved visual positions force lnum==0 to pass, after which only comparisons remain with no memory sink), reach (unconditional on every path to the mode branches). Survives the BREAK test.

assumptions: curwin and rex.reg_win are valid window pointers with no NULL-producing branch shown in the fragment (line 6), so the wp dereferences have no in-fragment NULL witness.
rex.line is the engine's NUL-terminated line buffer, so a non-negative length passed to win_linetabsize (line 68) cannot overrun it within the fragment's shown semantics.
limitations: A NULL-deref of wp was demoted: rex.reg_win/curwin are framework-provided pointers and no shown statement can make them NULL.

An OOB read inside getvvcol/win_linetabsize was demoted: the fragment shows no capacity expression for wp's buffer, and a failing argument (an out-of-window line) has no in-fragment producer; capacity-evidence rule not satisfied.
A negative (rex.input - rex.line) at lines 53/68 has no shown in-fragment producer; the callee's behavior on such a length is not attributable from the fragment.

The inactive-path positions curbuf->b_visual.vi_start/vi_end are never validated against line 1 in this fragment; even a zeroed saved visual state would be fail-closed at line 48, and downstream operations are comparisons only, so no confirmed finding was derived.

verdict.summary: Each in-fragment dangerous operation on ccline.cmdbuff is bounded at its exact point of use: the K_LEFT read is preceded on every path by the entry check `ccline.cmdpos == 0` (line 566) and the same-expression term `ccline.cmdpos > 0` (line 576); the K_RIGHT read is capped by `ccline.cmdpos >= ccline.cmdlen` (line 544) with the NUL-at-cmdlen slot shown at line 492; the Ctrl_U copy runs only while `i < ccline.cmdlen` (line 489); and the Ex-mode read requires `ccline.cmdpos > 0` (line 394). No injection, NULL-deref with an in-fragment NULL producer, or un-checked-status-then-use path exists, so no witness survives the BLOCK test.

evidence.reason: K_LEFT word-skip read (failure set: cmdpos-1 < 0). Reverse protection scan finds guards on every reaching path: line 566 `if (ccline.cmdpos == 0) goto cmdline_not_changed;` excludes 0 on entry, and the access is the last term of the while-expression whose first term is line 576 `while (ccline.cmdpos > 0` — evaluated with the current value immediately before the use (identity: same int variable, no intervening modification; reach: re-tested each iteration; degenerate: cmdpos==0 exits both at 566 and via the 576 term; boundary: admitted cmdpos in [1, cmdlen] maps to index in [0, cmdlen-1], failure set {cmdpos <= 0} has empty intersection). BREAK test passed; resolution PRESENT.

K_RIGHT word-skip read (failure set: index > capacity). Line 544 `if (ccline.cmdpos >= ccline.cmdlen) break;` is re-checked at the top of every do-while iteration, so the body (and the post-body read) start from cmdpos < cmdlen; cmdpos advances by the character length, and mb_ptr2len's NUL-cap semantics keep it <= cmdlen, i.e. the largest read index is the NUL slot that line 492 (`ccline.cmdbuff[ccline.cmdlen] = NUL;`) establishes in-fragment. No shown producer creates cmdpos > cmdlen, so no witness passes the BLOCK test. BREAK boundary test passed; resolution PRESENT (capacity of the NUL slot is the only unshown invariant, recorded in notes).

Ctrl_U tail-shift copy (failure set: i or j outside [0, newlen-1]/[0, oldlen-1]). The loop runs only while line 489 `while (i < ccline.cmdlen)`; write index i in [0, newlen-1] and read index j = cmdpos_old + i <= oldlen-1 are both in-bounds because every shown mutator keeps cmdpos <= cmdlen (566/576, 544/551-554, 695, 704). Degenerate cmdpos == oldlen gives zero iterations (cmdlen becomes 0) without underflow. Resolution PRESENT; the subsequent NUL write at line 492 is to the same NUL slot convention.

Ex-mode backslash read (failure set: index < 0). Guards 393-394, `ccline.cmdpos == ccline.cmdlen` and `ccline.cmdpos > 0`, are earlier terms of the same &&-chain and constrain the same value at the same precision immediately before the use, so read index cmdpos-1 lies in [0, cmdlen-1]. BREAK (identity/boundary/degenerate/reach) passes; resolution PRESENT.

assumptions: ccline.cmdbuff is a NUL-terminated buffer with capacity >= cmdlen+1, evidenced in-fragment by line 492 writing NUL at index cmdlen; growth/reallocation happens only inside unshown callees (put_on_cmdline, init_ccline).

verdict.summary: qtm_decompress performs an out-of-bounds heap write on the LZ match-copy path: match_length bytes are copied to &window[window_posn] without bounding match_length against the remaining window space (qtm->window_size - window_posn). On the wrap branch, the only guard (j > window_size) constrains the source wrap distance j, not the destination extent, and the else-branch clamp is unreachable there; window_posn += match_length then also advances state past the window end.

evidence.reason: Match-copy sink writes i=match_length bytes at rundest=&window[window_posn]. Window capacity is qtm->window_size (last valid index window_size-1, per L102 '&window[qtm->window_size - j]' and L113 clamp). With window_posn=window_size-2 (driven by literals via L59), selector 4 (L67) gives match_length=3 and attacker-chosen sym/extra yield match_offset=window_size (L66): j=match_offset-window_posn=2 passes L98 (2 > window_size is false), j<i splits the copy, L105 writes 2 in-bounds bytes, then L108 writes window[window_size], 1 byte beyond the allocation. Guard L98 bounds only j (wrong-object drift); L112-113 clamp runs only on the else path and is unreachable here. Absent fix: 'if (match_length > (int)(qtm->window_size - window_posn)) return qtm->error = CL_EFORMAT;' before the copy. Heap OOB write, CWE-787.

Independent literal-write sink: after an else-branch match, L116 'window_posn += match_length' advances by the unclamped match_length even though L112-113 clamps only the local copy count, so window_posn can exceed window_size (the L135 wrap reset fires only on exact equality). If frame_end (L46-48) is still larger, the L51 loop re-enters and this literal write indexes window[window_posn] past the window_size-element window; L120 also forms an OOB pointer. Absent fix: same one-statement bound on match_length against qtm->window_size - window_posn before the state advance. CWE-787.

assumptions: The window object's capacity is qtm->window_size entries, established in-fragment by L98, L102, L113, and L135 (indices into window are valid only for 0..window_size-1).

The compressed bitstream is attacker-controlled; QTM_GET_SYMBOL/QTM_READ_BITS and the model tables (position_base, extra_bits, length_base, length_extra) are unshown, so sym/extra/match_offset/match_length retain their full attacker-derived ranges.
The outer loop (L37) and frame logic permit multiple frames, so window_posn can be driven to window_size-2 within a frame that spans the window boundary.
limitations: Bounds of the model tables (position_base, extra_bits, length_base, length_extra) and the internals of QTM_GET_SYMBOL/QTM_READ_BITS/QTM_RESTORE_BITS/QTM_STORE_BITS are not shown; the BLOCK-test witness requires the attacker-chosen match_offset=window_size to be realizable by position_base, which the fragment never constrains (confidence 0.8, not higher).

The L131 'do { QTM_READ_BITS(i,8); } while (i != 0xFF);' re-align loop could fail to terminate on truncated input, but QTM_READ_BITS error semantics are unshown, so it is recorded as a limitation rather than a finding.
Membership of this fragment in the vulnerable/fixed pair was not used; the verdict rests solely on the ABSENT guard at the match-copy sink and the surviving witness.

verdict.summary: The fragment bounds the only attacker-influenced index and length before any dangerous operation: fs_parse's status is fully checked (L9, L30), the Opt_name size is constrained to [1, MAX_CGROUP_ROOT_NAMELEN-1] by L65/L67, and the string-read loop L70 admits only indices below that checked size. The only residual concern (signed char c passed to isalnum) has no in-fragment demonstrable failure, and the param->string buffer capacity is an external API contract, so no witness survives the BLOCK test.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective guard for the Opt_name string read: it executes on every path to the loop (straight-line within case Opt_name, before the loop) and constrains the same unmodified param->size consumed by the loop, excluding every size > MAX_CGROUP_ROOT_NAMELEN - 1 (admitted set [1, 63]). BREAK test: identity PASS (no assignment between L67 and L70), boundary PASS (loop index i < param->size so max index = 62 < size <= 63, and the fs_parameter string contract provides a buffer of at least size bytes), degenerate PASS (0 excluded by L65, 1 admitted safely), reach PASS. A huge-size read witness is blocked here.

Loop bound over the attacker-controlled but pre-checked param->size: admits indices [0, param->size-1] with param->size in [1, 63], so the read at L71 never exceeds the string value's length; the loop terminates and has no count-1/i-1 underflow because L65 guarantees size >= 1 on this path.

Degenerate-input guard: excludes size == 0 before the validation loop, so the loop cannot execute zero times against an empty name nor pass a zero length to reads; complements the upper-bound guard at L67.

Return-status handling for fs_parse: after the -ENOPARAM path (L9) handles the one sentinel, this clause returns every other negative status, so no error status is discarded or treated as success; the switch is only reached with a valid non-negative table index.

assumptions: fs_parameter string contract: for a string-valued parameter, param->string points to a NUL-terminated buffer of at least param->size bytes (kernel builds it with kmemdup_nul of the user-supplied length), and fs_parse enforces fs_value_is_string/!param->string for string-table entries such as Opt_name, so param->string is non-NULL and holds the bytes read at L71.
param->key is NUL-terminated (VFS supplies the key from the fsconfig syscall), making strcmp and the '%s' uses in invalfc safe.
for_each_subsys iterates the fixed small CGROUP_SUBSYS_COUNT, so the int shift `1 << i` at L25 stays within defined range; no attacker-controlled value drives i.
limitations: The backing-buffer capacity of param->string is not declared anywhere in this fragment; any OOB-over-param->string claim therefore lacks in-fragment capacity evidence and is demoted — the read index is nonetheless capped at size-1 by the shown guards.

`char c = param->string[i]` can hold a negative value (byte >= 0x80) when passed to isalnum(c) at L72. This is UB per the C standard if the ctype callee does not cast, but isalnum's body is unshown, no standard implementation (kernel __isctype casts to unsigned char; glibc's table covers -128..255) has a named failing outcome, and no in-fragment dereference/capacity demonstrates harm — demoted to a defensive-hardening concern, not a finding.

Downstream consumers of fc->source, ctx->release_agent, and ctx->name (e.g., later strscpy of a name of up to 63 chars plus NUL into MAX_CGROUP_ROOT_NAMELEN storage) are outside the fragment; the shown stores are pointer transfers with ownership correctly NULLed, and any overflow there is not demonstrable here.

MAX_CGROUP_ROOT_NAMELEN's literal value is not defined in the fragment; the safety of the in-fragment reads depends only on the loop using the checked param->size itself, not on that constant's value.

verdict.summary: The only OOB-capable access, the my_strcasecmp read at dl->str + dl->length - so_ext_len, is fully protected by the short-circuit guard `dl->length < so_ext_len ||` (line 4): it executes only when dl->length >= so_ext_len, giving offset >= 0, and length values 0..so_ext_len-1 (the exact unsigned-underflow range) never reach the sink. The memcpy/strcpy writes into the buffer allocated at line 8 (dl->length + so_ext_len + 1) fit exactly. No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained failing value.

evidence.snippet:
if (dl->length < so_ext_len ||
      my_strcasecmp(&my_charset_latin1, dl->str + dl->length - so_ext_len,
                    SO_EXT))
evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement: the first operand `dl->length < so_ext_len` (line 4) short-circuits the `||`, so the my_strcasecmp sink (lines 5-6) is reached only when dl->length >= so_ext_len. The OOB-read failure set of the unsigned subtraction `dl->length - so_ext_len` is exactly {dl->length < so_ext_len}; the guard's admitted set ({length >= so_ext_len}) has empty intersection with it, and nothing between the guard and the operand evaluation modifies dl->length. BREAK test passes: identity (same value/precision), boundary (admitted minimum so_ext_len gives offset 0), degenerate (0..so_ext_len-1 all skip the read), and reach (short-circuit evaluation is on every path to the sink).

assumptions: LEX_STRING contract: dl->str points to a NUL-terminated buffer holding exactly dl->length bytes (capacity >= length+1), which bounds the strcasecmp read starting at offset dl->length - so_ext_len.
so_ext_len = sizeof(SO_EXT) - 1 is a fixed compile-time constant (3 for ".so").
limitations: alloc_root returning NULL and being dereferenced at lines 9-10 is a theoretical NULL deref, but the NULL producer is an environmental OOM failure with no attacker-controlled value path shown inside the fragment; treated as a limitation, not the pair discriminator.

A wrap of `dl->length + so_ext_len + 1` (line 8) would require dl->length near SIZE_MAX/UINT_MAX with a matching huge dl->str, which no shown statement can produce; no in-fragment capacity/type evidence establishes it.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in Node::RunForwardTypeInference: the index ix is copied from edge->src_output() (line 17) with no non-debug constraint, and the only guard before node_t.args(ix) (line 45) is a DCHECK at line 41 that is compiled out under NDEBUG. evidence.reason: node_t.args(ix) is read at line 45 with capacity node_t.args_size() shown at lines 41/43. ix is int, sourced from input_idx[i] (line 9) which is assigned edge->src_output() at line 17 with no shown constraint; the only guard, DCHECK(ix < node_t.args_size()) at line 41, is compiled out in normal builds and cannot exclude the admitting value ix == node_t.args_size(). The absent fix is an unconditional check (e.g., if (ix < node_t.args_size())) before args(ix). This is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) from an unconstrained entry-point/graph-derived value reaching the protobuf repeated-field accessor.

assumptions: node_t.args_size() shown at lines 41 and 43 establishes the capacity of the repeated field accessed by args(ix).
DCHECK is compiled out under NDEBUG and is therefore not an executing protective statement.
edge->src_output() and edge->dst_input() are graph-provided values with no visible invariant bounding them.
limitations: input_nodes.at(i) at line 16 is bounds-checked (throws rather than writing out of bounds) and is not a memory-safety finding.
input_nodes[i] at line 36 is bounded by the loop condition i < input_nodes.size() and is safe.
No NULL-deref candidate: fwd_type_fn is null-checked at line 4 and input_nodes null entries cause an early return at lines 24-30.
Signed-overflow on i for input_types.size() > INT_MAX was not treated as a finding because the fragment shows no producer for such a size.

verdict.summary: node_map_->GetNode(node.input(1)) can return nullptr for a dangling second input (a name-keyed lookup whose standard semantics return NULL on a missing key), and the fragment dereferences it immediately at IsReallyConstant(*new_shape) with no non-NULL check, also at new_shape->DebugString() and EvaluateNode(*new_shape,...). evidence.reason: node.input(1) is entry-point graph data constrained only by the line-6 input_size >= 2 check, which validates the index, not the referent; GetNode is a map lookup that returns nullptr when the name is absent, and no shown statement between line 11 and line 12 assigns, initializes, or checks new_shape. The dereference *new_shape constructs the reference argument and crashes on NULL before IsReallyConstant runs. The absent fix is a null check, e.g. 'if (new_shape == nullptr) return errors::Internal(...);' inserted after line 11. Primary CWE-476: null pointer dereference of a possibly-NULL lookup result.

assumptions: node_map_ is a node-name-to-NodeDef map whose GetNode returns nullptr for an absent name (standard lookup semantics, TensorFlow's documented behavior).
node is derived from an untrusted GraphDef so its input names need not refer to existing nodes.
limitations: No downstream exploitation (beyond crash/DoS of the optimizer) is assessed; the same NULL witness also reaches new_shape->DebugString() at line 14 and EvaluateNode at line 24, but line 12 is the first dereference on every path.
If an enclosing graph-validation stage not shown in the fragment guaranteed referential integrity, GetNode would not return NULL; no such invariant is visible in the shown code and none is assumed.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations in the fragment are guarded. Protected NULL-deref sink: left_item is NULL only when the iterator is empty, and that exact state is returned from at line 21 before this line is reached; guard `if (!left_item)` (line 20) admits only non-NULL left_item, so no NULL witness survives.

Protected NULL-deref sink: same guard at lines 20-21, left_item is never reassigned between the guard and this second-loop use (lines 23-43 modify only `item`, clones, and `eq`), so the same non-NULL admitted set applies.

assumptions: `Item_equal_fields_iterator::operator++()` returns NULL at end of iteration, giving loop termination and non-NULL `item` inside each loop body (conditions at lines 12 and 40).
`build_clone()` and placement `new (thd->mem_root)` may return NULL and `equalities->push_back()` may report failure; all such results are checked before/at use (lines 29, 34, 47, 54).
`get_const()` is nullable and its result is used only inside the `if (right_item)` gate (line 23).

Bodies of `get_const()`, the field iterator, `build_clone()`, and `Item_func_eq` are not shown but are only exercised through guarded sites; no failure behavior is attributed beyond their standard semantics.
Membership in the vulnerable/fixed pair is not inferable from code appearance and was not used; the verdict follows solely from the Phase 4 PRESENT resolutions and BREAK-test results.

verdict.summary: scm_mkdir converts the optional mode via scm_to_uint, a checked conversion that raises on negative or out-of-range input, and fully checks mkdir's return status (if (rv != 0) SCM_SYSERROR). No inventory item resolves ABSENT with a surviving witness: there is no in-fragment memory sink, capacity expression, wrap derivation, NULL producer, or injection sink; the only residual concern (unmasked special permission bits) has no shown failure mechanism and is at most defensive hardening.

evidence.reason: DECISIVE PRESENT guard for the mkdir status sink: rv is the int return of mkdir (line 15); POSIX standard semantics give mkdir a failure set of exactly nonzero (-1). The guard executes unconditionally on the only path to the read, constrains the same rv with no intervening modification, and excludes the full failure set. BREAK test: identity OK, boundary OK, degenerate OK, reach OK. No later use of rv exists, so no unchecked-status or discard-then-success path remains.

PRESENT constraint on the only entry-point value reaching mkdir's mode parameter: scm_to_uint is a checked Guile conversion with standard semantics of raising out-of-range for negative values and values above UINT_MAX, so c_mode's residual range is {0777} ∪ [0, UINT_MAX] — no negative or wrapping value can be produced in-fragment; the later mode_t assignment only truncates high bits that mkdir does not interpret. No capacity, pointer, or NULL failure set exists for this value, so the operation is not dangerous.

assumptions: SCM_DEFINE's "1, 1, 0" declares mode optional, and SCM_UNBNDP (mode) at line 13 correctly selects the 0777 default when the argument is omitted.
scm_to_uint follows Guile's standard checked-conversion semantics: it raises an exception on negative or out-of-range input and never returns an unchecked value.
STRING_SYSCALL is the unshown macro converting path into the NUL-terminated c_path used at line 15; no protection or failure is credited from its unshown expansion.
limitations: Demoted candidate: c_mode's high bits (e.g., S_ISGID/S_ISVTX) reach mkdir without an explicit mask (e.g., & 0777). This is not a confirmed failure: the fragment's own documentation contracts that mode is applied as specified, no in-fragment capacity/wrap/NULL/memory/injection mechanism exists, and any harm would depend on unshown environment (group ownership and downstream consumers).
mode_t truncation on platforms where mode_t is narrower than unsigned int only discards high bits that mkdir does not consume; no memory or logic failure is derivable from the shown code.

Nothing inside STRING_SYSCALL is shown, so path-handling behavior (conversion, allocation, lifetime of c_path) could not be audited; no in-fragment producer of a NULL or oversized c_path exists to support a finding.

verdict.summary: The first selection loop assigns left_item= item; (line 14) before evaluating the checker predicate (line 15), so an item that the checker rejects is still admitted: the reject outcome (continue) only skips later iterations and never retracts the assignment. When all iterated items fail the checker, the loop exhausts with left_item holding the last rejected (non-NULL) item; the NULL guard at line 20 does not exclude it, and inside the if (right_item) branch it is consumed at line 26 (left_item->build_clone) to push down an equality. The absent one-statement fix is to assign left_item only after the checker accepts the item (as the second loop correctly does at lines 52-53).

evidence.reason: Sink consumes left_item, whose residual range after line 14 (left_item= item;) includes items rejected by the checker at line 15: the checker run is ordered after the assignment and its continue outcome never undoes it, so on the all-rejected/exhaustion path left_item is the last rejected item. The only guard on the path, if (!left_item) return false; (lines 20-21), excludes NULL only (identity-limited: it constrains NULL-ness, not validity), and guard if (right_item) (line 23) admits the branch for a non-NULL get_const() result, neither of which blocks the rejected value. Absent fix: move the left_item assignment below the checker test (mirroring the correct checker-then-use order at lines 52-53), so only checker-accepted items are selected. Mechanism: validation challenge is evaluated after the value is admitted, so the guarded security decision admits a superset of the intended set (CWE-697).

assumptions: right_item = get_const() (line 9) may be non-NULL; the if (right_item) branch at line 23 demonstrates that path in-fragment.
checker, when non-NULL, is a validation predicate whose false result means 'do not push this item'; a NULL checker admits all items and is not itself a failure.
Item_equal_fields_iterator it++ returns NULL exactly at end of the field list, exhausting the iterator for subsequent reads.
The field list is the only producer of item values in the first loop; no shown statement guarantees any item passes the checker or bounds the list size.
limitations: No memory-safety finding: NULL derefs of left_item and right_item (lines 26, 28, 45, 55) are guarded by if (!left_item) return false; (20-21) and if (right_item) (23); item derefs in loop 2 (52, 56) are guaranteed non-NULL by the loop condition.

The surviving witness requires the internal precondition that every iterated item fails checker while right_item is non-NULL; no shown statement excludes this configuration, but its downstream impact (incorrect pushdown/query semantics vs memory corruption) depends on unshown consumers.

The second-loop use of left_item at line 55 was audited and excluded as an independent sink: it is reachable only after the first loop broke on a checker-passing item, or not at all (exhausted iterator).
Status handling of build_clone failures (lines 29-30, 57-58), eq allocation and equalities->push_back (lines 34-35, 64-65) is complete and was not flagged.

The only prior guard, `if (input_tensor.index() < 0) break;` (lines 20-23), constrains the TensorId index (control dependencies), not map membership, so a regular input whose node is absent from the map still reaches line 25 where `*input_node` dereferences NULL. The absent one-statement fix is `if (input_node == nullptr) return ...;` between lines 24 and 25. The NULL witness survives the BLOCK test: no shown statement on the path excludes it.
