assumptions: node_map_->GetNode has standard map-lookup semantics: it returns nullptr for a name not present in the map (no shown check or invariant guarantees membership).
node.input() strings are externally supplied graph data consumed by this fragment.
limitations: total_inputs_size (size_t) accumulation at line 52 can wrap, but its only consumer is the unshown CreateNodeDef; no in-fragment failure of that callee is demonstrated, so it is not asserted as a finding.

new Tensor(raw_val.dtype(), raw_val.tensor_shape()) at line 44 performs an attacker-shaped allocation with no shown cap; a crash would occur inside an unshown constructor path, so it is demoted to a robustness note.
The early `break` on a control dependency at lines 20-23 skips later inputs for EvaluateNode; any concrete failure would occur in the unshown EvaluateNode body, so it remains a limitation.

verdict.summary: In the FLX_FRAME_TYPE path, the chunk size field read from the stream is only upper-bounded by avail (line 105); a crafted size smaller than FlxFrameChunkSize makes flxfh.size - FlxFrameChunkSize wrap to a huge gsize, gst_adapter_take returns NULL (precondition nbytes <= available violated), and chunk is dereferenced unchecked (lines 113-114), causing a NULL-pointer crash. Additionally, flxdec->size * 4 (line 124) wraps in 32-bit arithmetic for large unvalidated width/height, allocating an undersized output buffer consumed by flx_colorspace_convert.

evidence.reason: flxfh.size is stream-controlled (memcpy line 98) and the only guard, `if (avail < flxfh.size)` (line 105), admits every size <= avail, including sizes below FlxFrameChunkSize when avail >= FlxFrameChunkSize (line 90, e.g. flxfh.size=2, avail=6). The subtraction `flxfh.size - FlxFrameChunkSize` (line 112) then wraps to a huge gsize; gst_adapter_take's documented precondition nbytes <= available is violated, so it returns NULL, and chunk is dereferenced at lines 113-114 with no NULL check (CWE-476, root cause CWE-191). The absent one-statement fix is a lower-bound check `if (flxfh.size < FlxFrameChunkSize) goto need_more_data;` placed before the take; the BLOCK test finds no shown statement excluding this witness.

width/height from the header (lines 36-37, 78) are unvalidated; size = width*height fits in guint (max 4294836225) but `flxdec->size * 4` wraps in 32-bit unsigned for size >= 2^30 (e.g. 32768 x 32768 -> wrapped size 0). The undersized buffer (capacity = wrapped expression at line 124) is mapped and passed as map.data to flx_colorspace_convert (lines 138-141), whose converter was built from the same width/height (lines 67-69), yielding a write of width*height*4 bytes into a smaller buffer (CWE-190, CWE-787). No guard caps width, height, or size on any path; the absent fix is a bounds check on the product before the allocation.

assumptions: FlxFrameChunkSize is a small positive constant (struct/header size), so flxfh.size values in [0, FlxFrameChunkSize-1] are representable by the stream-derived chunk-size field.
gst_adapter_take(adapter, nbytes) returns NULL when nbytes exceeds the bytes currently available, per GStreamer's documented precondition (nbytes==0 also returns NULL).
width/height are 16-bit header values (<= 65535 each), making width*height fit in guint while width*height*4 can wrap.
gst_adapter_map returns a valid pointer to at least the requested bytes when avail >= requested size (true at lines 18/90).
limitations: The definitions of FlxFrameChunk/FlxHeader and the numeric value of FlxFrameChunkSize are not in the shown lines; they follow the standard FLX format.

The heap overflow from the wrapped size*4 materializes inside the unshown flx_colorspace_convert body; the in-fragment confirmed failure is the 32-bit wrap at line 124 feeding an undersized buffer to that call.
A size==0 chunk on the default path (gst_adapter_flush of 0 bytes, line 154) causes non-termination/livelock — same missing lower-bound check, not counted as a separate finding.
Huge g_malloc calls (lines 81-82, up to ~4.3 GB) may abort on constrained systems (resource exhaustion); not counted as a separate finding.
The pair's single-statement difference cannot be identified from this fragment; both the flxfh.size lower-bound check and the width/height bounds check are absent here.

verdict.summary: pax_decode_header reads the sparse-map entry count from the archive into sparse_map_size with only a TYPE_MAXIMUM(size_t) bound and no SIZE_MAX/sizeof check before xcalloc; the multiplication sparse_map_size * sizeof(*sparse_map) can wrap, allocating an undersized buffer that the loop then fills sparse_map_size times via sparse_add_map, causing a heap out-of-bounds write (and unbounded allocation/iteration) from a crafted archive.

evidence.reason: sparse_map_size is attacker-controlled (decode_num at line 46 admits any value up to TYPE_MAXIMUM(size_t), assigned unmodified at line 52) and reaches the allocation-size computation at lines 53-54 with no overflow/bound check. For sparse_map_size > SIZE_MAX/sizeof(*sparse_map) the product wraps (CWE-190), producing an undersized heap allocation that the loop at line 56/append at line 76 then overfills with sparse_map_size entries -> heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The absent one-statement fix is a 'TYPE_MAXIMUM (size_t) / sizeof (*file->stat_info->sparse_map) < sparse_map_size' reject-and-return check immediately before xcalloc; every guard on the path (COPY_BUF check at line 18, decode_num check at line 46) is passed by the witness (a large valid decimal).

The loop iterates exactly sparse_map_size times (0..SIZE_MAX) with no shown cap, each iteration appending one entry via sparse_add_map (line 76) into a buffer sized only by the unguarded multiplication at lines 53-54; when that size computation wraps, these writes exceed the allocated capacity, and the same attacker-controlled count drives unbounded allocation and iteration.

assumptions: decode_num returns success with u in [0, TYPE_MAXIMUM(size_t)] on the checked path (name-implied semantics of numeric decode with an upper-bound argument), so sparse_map_size can be as large as SIZE_MAX.

struct sp_array has at least one member (shown assignments sp.offset = u and sp.numbytes = u at lines 67/75), so sizeof(*file->stat_info->sparse_map) >= 1, making values near SIZE_MAX overflow the size multiplication.
Capacity evidence for the OOB claim is the shown allocation-size computation itself (lines 53-54) per the capacity-evidence rule.
limitations: sizeof(struct sp_array) is not declared in the fragment, so the exact wrap threshold is not quoted; the overflow requires element size >= 1 and sparse_map_size exceeding SIZE_MAX/sizeof, and the fragment's decode_num boundary admits such values.

If the linked calloc/xcalloc implementation internally rejects nmemb*size overflow (e.g., glibc calloc returning NULL), the OOB-write path degrades to a guaranteed abort/unbounded-resource failure; the fragment shows no protective statement at this site, and unshown callee internals are not credited as guards in either direction.
The dumped_size arithmetic (line 80) and any behavior of the unshown sparse_add_map body beyond appending one entry per call were not treated as independent findings.
No NULL-deref finding: all find_next_block() results are checked at lines 28 and 42.

verdict.summary: In the macro-expansion path (CTO_UpLow/CTO_None), substitution arguments are copied into the fixed-size tmpFile.line buffer with no MAXSTRING bound check, while the sibling definition-copy path carries that check (L157). A crafted table file whose macro definition fills linelen up to MAXSTRING and whose call supplies a non-empty argument makes the loop at L169-170 write at and beyond index MAXSTRING, overflowing the buffer (stack OOB write).

evidence.reason: arg.length originates from a table-file macro-argument token (L130), i.e. entry-point input with no shown minimum; tmpFile.line's usable extent is MAXSTRING as demonstrated by the fragment's own guard `tmpFile.linelen >= MAXSTRING` at L157 (which fires only before a definition-char write, permitting the transition MAXSTRING-1 -> MAXSTRING). The L169 loop admits j in [0, arg.length-1], so writes reach index linelen+arg.length-1 >= MAXSTRING when linelen == MAXSTRING and arg.length >= 2, and no statement on the L166-L170 path bounds linelen or arg.length. The missing one-statement fix is a bound check before the copy, e.g. `if (tmpFile.linelen + arg.length >= MAXSTRING) { compileError(...); return 0; }`, equivalent to the guard already present on the definition path at L157. This unguarded write past the line buffer's MAXSTRING extent is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

assumptions: tmpFile.line is a fixed-size buffer whose usable extent is MAXSTRING, shown in-fragment by the guard `tmpFile.linelen >= MAXSTRING` (L157) and the error message naming MAXSTRING (L158-161).
Macro arguments read by getToken at L130 are entry-point (table-file) content; a non-empty argument has length >= 1, and getToken can deliver lengths up to MAXSTRING.

Reaching the vulnerable copy requires m->substitution_count >= 1 with a substitution position inside definition_length; this is the normal, name-implied meaning of a macro with parameters, and no shown statement contradicts it.
limitations: L168 `arguments[m->substitutions[2 * subst + 1] - 1]` could be an OOB read if compileMacro emits an out-of-range substitution index, but compileMacro's body is unshown and no in-fragment constraint or producer demonstrates such a value.

L127-128 `malloc(m->argument_count * sizeof(CharsString))` is unchecked, but argument_count is determined by the macro definition's declared parameters (each costing input bytes), so NULL/failure is not attacker-drivable in a demonstrable way.

Discarded statuses of getCharacters/getRuleCharsText/getRuleDotsPattern at L232-235 and L283-286 could leave CharsString fields uninitialized on failure, but whether the callee leaves them untouched is unshown; the uninitialized-use chain was demoted.
Unchecked malloc of `char *s` in the emphasis-class handlers is a NULL-deref candidate only on small-allocation failure, which the fragment cannot drive.
CTO_SeqAfterExpression copies ruleChars into seqAfterExpression with no shown capacity; the target capacity is not established in-fragment, so it was demoted under the capacity-evidence rule.

The memcpy sinks at L262/L313 are bounded by the two 13841-element _lou_pattern_compile caps and the `if (!len) goto` checks (max len 27683 < 27720 allocation); the ruleArea target capacity is unshown but no in-fragment derivation exceeds it.

verdict.summary: The only unit-freeing operation, un->exclude_level() (line 20), is protected: the list pointer is captured by next_unit= un->next_unit() (line 19) BEFORE the freeing call, and if (next_unit) continue; break; (lines 21-23) ensures the loop increment at line 6 never evaluates un->next_unit() on the freed unit (non-NULL next_unit short-circuits the ternary; NULL exits the loop). All other sinks (NULL checks at lines 11, 60, 86, 89 and return-status checks at lines 56, 76) are present and cover their failure sets, so no witness survives the BLOCK test.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the only use-after-free candidate. exclude_level() (line 20) frees un, but the pointer consumed by the loop increment (line 6) is saved at line 19 BEFORE the free; lines 21-23 then force either continue with the saved non-NULL next_unit (so line 6's ternary takes the next_unit arm and un->next_unit() is never evaluated) or break (so line 6 never runs at all). BREAK test: identity holds (same pointer, no intervening modification; line 9's reset runs after the increment), boundary N/A, degenerate case next_unit==NULL exits via break, and line 21-23 lies on every path out of line 20. No witness survives the BLOCK test, and every other inventoried sink (NULL checks at lines 11/60/86/89, status checks at 56/76) resolves PRESENT, so the fragment is not vulnerable.

assumptions: exclude_level() unlinks and frees the current SELECT_LEX_UNIT only; the pre-saved next-unit node remains a valid list element (standard semantics, no in-fragment statement contradicts this).
first_inner_unit()/next_unit()/first_select()/next_select() return NULL at list end, which the loop conditions at lines 5 and 46 test.
Framework members un->thd, un->thd->lex, inner_join->thd, and inner_join->select_lex have no NULL producer visible inside the fragment.
limitations: A UAF witness that assumes exclude_level() also frees subsequent units or that the linked list is already corrupted requires non-standard callee behavior with no shown statement, so it is rejected by the BLOCK test.

The second status check (if (res) return TRUE;, line 104) is redundant dead code since a non-zero res returns at line 77 and res is not reassigned between lines 77 and 104; this is a code-quality observation, not a status-handling flaw because the status is checked at line 76.
No OOB candidate exists: the fragment performs no array/container indexing, no copies, and no arithmetic on sizes; capacity evidence is therefore not applicable.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is guarded in-fragment: the uint32 multiply at L32 is bounded by the 2GB check at L26 (max product <= 2147483647, no wrap, lossless uint32 cast), the L34 allocation is NULL-checked at L35, the inline memcpys at L40/L58 write exactly the calloc'd capacity and read within the 8-byte tdir_offset union under L39/L57, and the file reads at L47/L65 are sized to the buffer with err checks at L48/L66. No sink resolves ABSENT with a surviving witness.

evidence.reason: uint32 multiply cannot wrap: the L26 guard `if ((uint64)(2147483647/typesize)<target_count64) return(TIFFReadDirEntryErrSizesan);` runs on every path before L31 and admits only target_count64 <= floor(2147483647/typesize), so after the lossless L31 cast `datasize = (*count)*typesize <= 2147483647 < UINT32_MAX`, fitting uint32 and (tmsize_t) at L47/L65; the L34 allocation of *count*typesize equals datasize.

Write is exact-fit into the _TIFFCheckMalloc buffer whose capacity is *count*typesize = datasize (L34/L32), and the L39 `datasize<=4` branch bound keeps the source read within the 8-byte tdir_offset union; BREAK test passes at the boundary (datasize==4 exactly uses the 4-byte toff_long).
BigTIFF inline copy is exact-fit (datasize == calloc'd capacity) and L57 `datasize<=8` caps the source read at the full 8-byte union size; no admitted value exceeds the buffer or the source object.

The read transfers exactly datasize bytes, matching the datasize-capacity buffer, and L48 `if (err!=TIFFReadDirEntryErrOk) { _TIFFfree(data); return(err); }` fully handles a failed/short read before the buffer is consumed; datasize <= 2147483647 fits the signed (tmsize_t) parameter. The BigTIFF twin at L65 is protected identically by L66.

assumptions: TIFFDirEntry.tdir_offset is a union of at least 8 bytes (the fragment accesses toff_long at L44 and toff_long8 at L62), so reading <= 8 bytes from it stays in-object.
TIFFDataWidth returns a small positive width (1/2/4/8) for known types and 0 otherwise; L14 excludes the 0 case, so typesize is a nonzero divisor at L26.
_TIFFCheckMalloc has calloc semantics (allocates count*typesize bytes, NULL on failure), and L35 checks the result before any use.
TIFFReadDirEntryData either transfers the requested cc bytes or returns a non-Ok error, and every non-Ok outcome is handled at L48/L66 before data is used.
limitations: desttypesize (uint32, L2) has no shown call site and no in-fragment producer of 0; if a hypothetical caller passed 0, the division at L28 `(uint64)(2147483647/desttypesize)` would divide by zero, but per provenance rules an unconstrained parameter domain alone is not a finding.
The assert at L33 is not credited (compiled out under NDEBUG), but datasize>0 is independently derived from L14 (target_count64>0 and typesize>0) before any allocation/copy.
Caller-side contract violations (NULL direntry or tif, maxcount mis-use) are not shown and are out of scope.
The offset value passed to TIFFReadDirEntryData is attacker-influenced, but out-of-file reads are rejected by that function's err return, which the fragment checks at L48/L66.

verdict.summary: ELF parser mmaps the file (capacity st.st_size, line 23) but never validates header offsets/counts against that size: attacker-controlled e_shoff/e_shstrndx reach an out-of-bounds read at shdr[e_shstrndx] (line 178), section-name offsets reach an unbounded strlen (line 254), and uninitialized dynstr/dynamic are used as section-table indices (line 345) when the file omits the .dynamic/.dynstr sections.

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125): elf_map's capacity is st.st_size (line 23); e_shoff (line 176) and e_shstrndx are entry-point file fields admitted with no constraint, so a small ELF32 file with large e_shoff/e_shstrndx dereferences elf_map + e_shoff + e_shstrndx*sizeof(Elf32_Shdr) far beyond the mapping. No guard on any reaching path bounds them (reverse scan: only the mmap/MAP_FAILED check at 24 and MODE==ELFCLASS32 at 30). Absent one-statement fix: validate e_shoff + (e_shstrndx+1)*sizeof(Elf32_Shdr) <= st.st_size before this line. Witness survives the BLOCK test; no protective statement exists to run the BREAK test.

OOB read (CWE-125): name is produced at line 183 as elf_map + shstrtab.sh_offset + shdr[i].sh_name with unvalidated attacker-controlled offsets, then consumed by strlen without proving the pointer lies within the st.st_size-byte mapping (line 23). The guard itself constrains string length, not pointer placement (wrong-object drift), and performs the same unchecked scan. Absent fix: a bounds check shstrtab.sh_offset + shdr[i].sh_name < st.st_size before computing/reading name.

Uninitialized use (CWE-457) feeding OOB access: dynamic/dynstr are declared at lines 330-331 and only assigned inside the 333-341 loop when a section name strcmp matches; a file with no '.dynamic'/'.dynstr' section leaves them indeterminate, and this line then indexes shdr[dynamic] at an arbitrary offset. Attacker-supplied sh_size (line 346) also drives the unbounded dyn[i] loop at line 350. Absent fix: initialize dynamic = dynstr = -1 and check they were set (or validate shdr[dynamic].sh_offset/size against st.st_size) before use.

assumptions: The file contents are entry-point input: every ELF header field (e_shoff, e_shstrndx, e_shnum, e_phnum, sh_offset, sh_name, sh_size, d_un.d_val) is attacker-controllable.
The mmap region's capacity is st.st_size by line 23; accesses beyond it are the failure boundary (faulting or reading past mapped data).
A file can validly contain no section named '.dynamic'/'.dynstr', leaving lines 330-331 uninitialized (status flags assign only on strcmp match, lines 335-340).
limitations: The strcpy write at line 255 is demoted: it is gated by strlen(name) > 15 (line 254) and writes into bytes 9..14 of a buffer whose first 16 bytes were already read, so the confirmed failure is the preceding unchecked strlen read, not the write.
flag2str_sh/flag2str writes into flag[4] (lines 257-258, 310-311) and PRINT_* macro behavior cannot be verified because their bodies are unshown.
The 64-bit twin (MODE == ELFCLASS64) repeats the same unbounded patterns; it is not counted as an additional independent finding.

The sum/offset arithmetic in a malformed file may also fault inside the mapped page region; the verdict rests on the confirmed dereferences at lines 178/254/345 which are provably past the st.st_size boundary.

verdict.summary: SSL_new(ctx) result is passed to SSL_set_options and later OpenSSL calls without a NULL check (NULL dereference on allocation failure), and SSL_connect's failure status 0 is admitted by the 'rc < 0' guard and treated as success via isssl = true.

evidence.reason: ssl is assigned SSL_new(ctx) at line 87; SSL_new's documented semantics return NULL on failure. The fragment contains no NULL check between line 87 and this first dereferencing use at line 88 (nor before SSL_set_fd/SSL_set_tlsext_host_name/SSL_connect), and the only adjacent guard, 'if (ctx == NULL)' at line 14, constrains ctx, not ssl (wrong-object drift). The absent one-statement fix is 'if (ssl == NULL) { SSL_CTX_free(ctx); ctx = NULL; return -1; }' after line 87; the NULL witness survives the BLOCK test because no shown statement excludes it on the path to line 88. Primary CWE-476 (NULL pointer dereference of an unchecked allocation result).

SSL_connect (line 100) returns 0 or negative on handshake failure and 1 on success; the guard 'rc < 0' excludes only negatives, admitting the failure value rc == 0. On that admitted path the fragment proceeds to set isssl = true (line 115) and return 0 (line 117), consuming the failed session as an established SSL connection. The absent one-statement fix is 'if (rc <= 0)' (or 'rc != 1'); the rc == 0 witness survives the BLOCK test with no intervening check. Secondary CWE-754 (failure status entered into a success path).

assumptions: ctx is non-NULL when SSL_new is reached because line 14 and fail-closed returns at lines 23-51 precede it.
OpenSSL standard semantics: SSL_new returns NULL on failure; SSL_connect returns 1 on success and 0 or negative on error.
limitations: The NULL-deref witness requires an SSL_new allocation failure (resource exhaustion), so it is a robustness/DoS-oriented trigger rather than a directly attacker-shaped input.

hostname and certificate_path are not shown to be attacker-controlled at a dangerous sink; their uses here (literal-format logging, path argument to SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations) were not confirmed as findings.
SSL_set_fd(ssl, this->getFD()) with getFD() == -1 was not treated as a fence because no shown producer/consumer chain demonstrates harm.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation carries a protective statement. The only wrap-sensitive sink, len -= POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE on the decrypt path (line 84), is preceded on every reaching path by the guard "if (len < POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE) return 0;" (lines 82-83), which admits only len >= 16 and excludes the underflow set [0,15]; all copy/read lengths are bounded by arg equality/range checks (arg==EVP_AEAD_TLS1_AAD_LEN, arg in [1,16], arg==12) and allocation results are NULL-checked. No surviving witness.

evidence.reason: Decisive sink: the unsigned len (declared line 74, derived from TLS AAD bytes, range 0..65535) is decremented by POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE on the decrypt path. Guard at lines 82-83 (if (len < POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE) return 0;) executes on every path to the subtraction at line 84 inside the !ctx->encrypt branch, admitting only [16,65535] and excluding [0,15], so no modulo-2^32 wraparound is possible. BREAK test passes: identity (same len, no intervening modification), boundary (min admitted 16 vs failure boundary 15), degenerate (0 and 15 are early-returned, 65535 -> 65519), reach (unconditional before line 84). Resolves PRESENT with excluded set [0,15].

Copy length is the constant EVP_AEAD_TLS1_AAD_LEN (13), admitted only when the line 71-72 guard (arg != EVP_AEAD_TLS1_AAD_LEN -> return 0) passes with arg == 13; the destination tls_aad has at least POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE (16) bytes, established in-fragment by the line 22 memset(actx->tls_aad, 0, POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE), so 13 <= 16 and no OOB. Resolves PRESENT.

arg is bounded by the line 65 guard (arg <= 0 || arg > POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE || !ctx->encrypt -> return 0) to [1,16], matching the 16-byte source actx->tag; the destination is the caller-supplied tag buffer of arg bytes per the EVP control contract, and no in-fragment NULL producer for ptr exists. Resolves PRESENT.

assumptions: POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE == 16, EVP_AEAD_TLS1_AAD_LEN == 13, CHACHA_CTR_SIZE == 16 (OpenSSL constants for this code); the tls_aad capacity of 16 is corroborated in-fragment by memset(actx->tls_aad, 0, POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE) at line 22.
arg in EVP_CIPHER_CTX_ctrl calls is the caller-supplied buffer/parameter length, so the arg equality/range guards tie each copy length to that argument.
limitations: NULL dereference of ptr in EVP_CTRL_AEAD_SET_IV_FIXED, EVP_CTRL_AEAD_GET_TAG, EVP_CTRL_AEAD_TLS1_AAD, and of dst in EVP_CTRL_COPY would require a NULL produced by an unshown caller; no in-fragment NULL producer exists, so these are demoted.

actx is dereferenced without a NULL check in the non-INIT/non-COPY cases, but no shown statement can make it NULL on those paths (the NULL handling at lines 8-10 is confined to the INIT case); demoted.
The downstream consumption of actx->tls_payload_length and the encrypt-direction len in the TLS record layer is outside the fragment and was not analyzed.
GET_TAG before any tag is set would copy zalloc-zeroed tag bytes; no uninitialized read and no shown disclosure path.
Confidence capped at 0.75 because safety rests on several guards across independent case branches rather than a single monolithic check.

verdict.summary: No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained failing value inside the fragment. The `data->task` dereference (line 13) is guarded by `data &&` (excludes data==NULL), and `connection_attempt_remove`/`enumerator_next_async` (lines 39-40) are guarded by `if (data)` (lines 37-43), both surviving the BREAK test. The dereferences at lines 31-32 and 48-49 have no surviving NULL witness: the fragment's only NULL producer (line 55) is always preceded by synchronous `g_cancellable_cancel` (line 54), so a NULL-data callback is cancelled and routed through `else g_clear_error` (line 35), never reaching those derefs; a NULL from the unshown task-completion teardown or a success-after-cancel race is not derivable from the shown statements.

evidence.reason: PRESENT protective statement for the dereference of `data` (`data->task`): the `data &&` conjunct excludes the NULL value from the dereference. BREAK test: identity — the same local `data` (copied at line 6) is consumed with no intervening modification; boundary — data==NULL is excluded, every admitted value is deref-safe; degenerate — a NULL `data` skips the deref and does not take this return path; reach — the check executes before the deref on every path. PASS.

PRESENT protective statement for `enumerator_next_async (data)` (line 40) and for `connection_attempt_remove (attempt)` (line 39), which consumes `attempt->data`: the `if (data)` branch excludes data==NULL on the error path. BREAK test: identity — local `data` equals `attempt->data` here (no shown modification between line 6 and line 37); boundary/degenerate — NULL flows to `connection_attempt_unref` instead; reach — executes on every error-branch path before these calls. PASS.

Routing guard that keeps the in-fragment NULL producer (line 55) away from the `data->connectable`/`data->last_error` dereferences (lines 31-32): because line 54 synchronously cancels before line 55 NULLs, every attempt that reaches this callback with data==NULL has a cancelled cancellable, so this `if` takes the `else` (line 35) and the derefs at lines 31-32 are not executed. No in-fragment producer yields (data==NULL, cancellable==uncancelled); the witness is BLOCKed before line 31.

The only NULL-producing statement in the fragment (line 55) is always paired with a synchronous cancellation (line 54); standard GLib semantics make `g_cancellable_is_cancelled` TRUE immediately afterward. Consequently sibling attempts whose `data` is NULL are routed through the `else` paths (lines 35 and 42-43) and never reach the dereferences at lines 31-32 or 48-49 in any path shown by the fragment.

assumptions: `g_cancellable_cancel` sets the cancellable's flag synchronously, so `g_cancellable_is_cancelled` returns TRUE immediately afterward (standard GLib semantics).
Entries in `connection_attempts` retain an independent reference for their in-flight async callback, so the unrefs at lines 56 and 60 are balanced (ref accounting beyond the shown statements).

After a successful `g_socket_connection_connect_finish` (line 26), `attempt->socket` and `attempt->connection` are non-NULL, so the steals at lines 48-49 and later uses of `data->socket`/`data->connection` are valid.
limitations: The comment on line 12 documents an unshown task-completion teardown that can set `attempt->data = NULL`; if that teardown ever runs without cancelling the attempt's cancellable, a NULL `data` could reach the dereferences at lines 31-32 or 48-49. That teardown is outside the fragment, so it is not a confirmed in-fragment finding.

A race in which a sibling attempt's connect completes successfully before its cancellation and its callback runs after the success loop (lines 51-57) NULLs its data, with `g_socket_connection_connect_finish` still returning TRUE, would dereference NULL at lines 48-49. The required concurrent-attempt interleaving is not displayed in the fragment.

verdict.summary: An unauthenticated caller can send a JSON body whose 'scheme_type' field is a non-string value (e.g. a number). The check at line 16 only tests key presence, so the right operand of || is evaluated and o_strcmp receives the NULL returned by json_string_value() for a non-string, dereferencing NULL inside the strcmp-equivalent and crashing the callback (DoS).

evidence.reason: The attacker-controlled JSON body (line 3) supplies 'scheme_type'; line 14 and line 15 pass for {"username":"x","password":"y","scheme_type":123}. The only guard at the sink, line 16's `json_object_get(j_param, "scheme_type") == NULL`, excludes only absence, so for a present non-string value the || evaluates the RHS and json_object_get's value reaches json_string_value, which returns NULL for non-strings, which is then passed to o_strcmp (strcmp semantics) causing a NULL pointer dereference. The absent one-statement fix is a json_is_string(json_object_get(j_param, "scheme_type")) check (or NULL check on the json_string_value result) before the o_strcmp call; the witness survives the BLOCK test with no shown statement blocking it, giving CWE-476.

assumptions: JSON body from ulfius_get_json_body_request is attacker-controlled when non-NULL (line 3, 14).
jansson semantics: json_string_value returns NULL for non-string values; json_string_length returns 0 for NULL/non-string.
o_strcmp has strcmp-like semantics on its arguments.
expires[129] with strftime size 128 leaves room for the NUL terminator.
limitations: NULL session_uid passed into get_users_for_session (line 49-50) and user_session_update/ulfius_add_cookie_to_response is not confirmable because those callee bodies are unshown.
json_string_value(json_object_get(j_result, "username")) at lines 117/122 depends on unshown auth_check_identify_scheme output type, so it is demoted rather than a finding.
Format strings in y_log_message are literals with %s arguments; no injection sink confirmed.

verdict.summary: spell_suggest() copies the remainder of the bad word into the fixed-size stack buffer wcopy (MAXWLEN + 2) without bounding the copy size: vim_strncpy(wcopy + stp->st_wordlen, sug.su_badptr + stp->st_orglen, sug.su_badlen - stp->st_orglen) is guarded only by sug.su_badlen > stp->st_orglen, which bounds nothing relative to wcopy's capacity. The bad-word length originates from a visual selection capped only at the line length (lines 40-50), not at MAXWLEN, so a long bad word causes a stack-buffer overflow (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: Stack-buffer overflow: wcopy is declared char_u wcopy[MAXWLEN + 2] (line 5), so the maximum valid index is MAXWLEN+1. The copy at lines 139-141 writes (sug.su_badlen - stp->st_orglen) + 1 bytes starting at wcopy + stp->st_wordlen, needing stp->st_wordlen + sug.su_badlen - stp->st_orglen <= MAXWLEN+1. The only guard, line 138 (sug.su_badlen > stp->st_orglen), admits st_orglen < su_badlen but leaves su_badlen, st_orglen, and st_wordlen unbounded relative to MAXWLEN. su_badlen is derived from badlen, which the visual-selection branch (lines 40-50) caps only at the line remainder (line 50), never at MAXWLEN; a selection longer than MAXWLEN+2 (e.g., 50 chars with MAXWLEN=40) yields a copy of 49+ bytes into a 42-byte stack buffer. The absent one-statement fix is a clamp of su_badlen to MAXWLEN (or of the copy length to MAXWLEN - stp->st_wordlen) before the copy; a witness (long visual selection -> large su_badlen -> guard 138 passes for any st_orglen < su_badlen -> write past wcopy) survives the BLOCK test with no blocking shown statement.

assumptions: vim_strncpy copies at most the named maxlen characters and always appends NUL, so it writes up to maxlen+1 bytes (standard Vim semantics).
wcopy is a stack-local array; its in-fragment capacity is MAXWLEN + 2 (line 5).
spell_find_suggest (line 92) fills su_badlen as the bad-text length corresponding to the passed badlen per standard name-implied semantics; it receives the fragment-produced badlen.
st_orglen < su_badlen (the guard-passing case) is the documented normal case for partial replacement (comment lines 135-136).
limitations: The magnitude of su_badlen relies on the unshown callee propagating badlen without an internal MAXWLEN cap; such an unshown cap is neither shown nor credited per the evidence rules.

The replacement-branch allocation/STRCAT chain (lines 219-225) shows the same class of unconstrained suggestion fields (st_orglen versus remaining line length), but its witness additionally needs st_orglen to exceed the remaining line; demoted.

The STRLEN(line) - curwin->w_cursor.col expression (line 50) is size_t arithmetic and could underflow if the cursor column exceeded the line length, but no in-fragment producer of such a column value is shown.
The %. *s reads of sug.su_badptr rely on line NUL termination and were not treated as independent findings.
Membership in the vulnerable/fixed pair was not used as evidence; the verdict follows from the absent bound at the wcopy sink.

verdict.summary: The unsigned int *count parameter is never constrained, and the allocation-size arithmetic (*count + auth_count) at line 15 wraps mod 2^32 for *count near UINT_MAX, yielding a small t_malloc buffer; memset(tab, 0, *count * sizeof(*tab)) then writes ~*count elements into it (heap overflow) and tab += *count walks the pointer out of bounds. A bound check such as if (*count > UINT_MAX - auth_count) return NULL; before the allocation is absent.

evidence.reason: Heap buffer overflow (CWE-787): *count has residual range [0, UINT_MAX] because no shown statement constrains it (no-caller-assumptions rule). With *count = UINT_MAX, the capacity expression (*count + auth_count) * sizeof(*tab) at line 15 wraps (unsigned int addition) to about (auth_count-1) entries, but this memset writes UINT_MAX * sizeof(*tab) bytes (~103 GB) into that small allocation. No guard on *count exists anywhere before the write; the absent one-statement fix is an upper bound/validation on *count, e.g. if (*count > UINT_MAX - auth_count) return NULL;

Integer overflow in allocation sizing (CWE-190): *count (unsigned int, unconstrained by the fragment) plus auth_count (unsigned int) wraps for *count >= UINT_MAX - auth_count + 1, producing an undersized allocation that is then overrun by the memset at line 16 and the tab += *count advance at line 17. The capacity itself is the quoted line-15 product, so the in-fragment derivation exceeds the in-fragment capacity; no guard constrains *count.

assumptions: auth_count = N_ELEMENTS(auth_request_var_expand_static_tab) is a non-zero constant, and the memcpy at lines 20-21 copies exactly auth_count entries into the auth_count-entry static region.
t_malloc follows Dovecot data-stack semantics (never returns NULL), so no NULL check on its result is required.
sizeof(*tab) > 0; its exact magnitude only scales the overflow size.
limitations: auth_request->user has no shown NULL producer; its unconditional use (lines 23-24, 26, 74, 79) implies a non-NULL invariant, so a NULL-user crash cannot be confirmed from the fragment.

The inner pointers auth_request->userdb->userdb (line 42) and auth_request->passdb->passdb (line 45) have no shown NULL producer, so the outer-pointer ternaries (lines 41, 44) cannot be extended to a confirmed NULL-deref finding.
The tab[0..33] writes require auth_count >= 34, but the value of auth_count is not shown; OOB there is not demonstrable in either direction.
Whether *count can be driven to ~UINT_MAX by a real caller is outside the fragment; the finding rests on the unconstrained residual range per the no-caller-assumptions rule.

verdict.summary: Every consumed status or nullable pointer in BuildXlaCompilationCache is protected by an in-fragment check: the metadata pointer is null-tested before dereference (line 4), platform/client StatusOr results are early-returned on failure before ValueOrDie() (lines 13, 50), and the registration out-param is only dereferenced after GetCompilationDevice succeeds (lines 54-58). The partially-checked compiler_for_platform status is never consumed, and the unguarded framework accessor dereferences have no in-fragment NULL producer.

assumptions: device->tensorflow_cpu_worker_threads() and flr->config_proto() return valid non-null pointers; no in-fragment statement can make them NULL.
XlaOpRegistry::GetCompilationDevice sets the registration out-parameter when it returns true (standard boolean out-param contract).
xla_device_metadata() is a const-ref getter whose value cannot change between the check at line 4 and the dereferences at lines 6-7.
limitations: The compiler_for_platform status is handled only for error::NOT_FOUND (lines 30-35); other error codes fall through, but the failed result is never consumed in the fragment, so this is a robustness/fail-open concern without a confirmed harmful consumer.

verdict.summary: The parser maps attacker-controlled file bytes (mmap length st.st_size at line 23) and dereferences unvalidated ELF header/section fields (e_shoff/e_shnum/e_phoff/e_phnum/e_shstrndx, shstrtab.sh_offset, sh_name, sh_size) against that region; the only bounds guard, validated_offset at line 184, covers just the first section loop's name string, leaving OOB reads at lines 178, 270, 326 and an uninitialized-use at line 349 that indexes shdr with an unset 'dynamic'.

Absent one-statement fix: add the same validated_offset(name, elf_map, elf_map + st.st_size) check before this printf. Primary CWE-125 (OOB read).

dynamic is declared uninitialized (line 335) and assigned only when a section name equals '.dynamic' (lines 342-344); because section names are attacker-controlled, omitting that name leaves dynamic uninitialized and it is consumed here as an index into shdr without any initializer or sentinel check, also producing an unguarded OOB read against the st.st_size-byte mapping (line 23). Absent fix: initialize dynamic = -1 and test it (plus bound shdr[dynamic].sh_offset against st.st_size) before use. Secondary CWE-457 (uninitialized use).

e_shoff (line 176) and e_shstrndx are untrusted header fields; the read at line 178 is at elf_map + e_shoff + e_shstrndx*sizeof(Elf32_Shdr) with no bound versus st.st_size, e.g., e_shoff=0x1000, e_shstrndx=0, small file, reads past elf_map+st.st_size. No guard exists on the path (only the MAP_FAILED check at line 24). Absent fix: validate e_shoff + e_shnum*sizeof(Elf32_Shdr) <= st.st_size before dereferencing shdr. CWE-125 (OOB read).

assumptions: ELF header/section/dynamic fields are read from the mmap'd file bytes, so their values are attacker-controlled (entry-point data via the file path argument, including st.st_size from fstat).
validated_offset semantics are name-implied: it returns nonzero when name is outside [base, end), and its use at line 184 treats nonzero as an error return.
limitations: The 64-bit ELFCLASS64 mirror (from line 1141) duplicates every sink; only the ELFCLASS32 instances are cited.

verdict.summary: xQueueGenericCreate computes the queue storage size with an unsigned multiplication of caller-supplied uxQueueLength and uxItemSize; the only overflow guard is a configASSERT that does not execute in a normal build, so a wrapped xQueueSizeInBytes feeds pvPortMalloc and creates an undersized queue storage while the queue advertises full capacity, enabling subsequent heap overrun (CWE-190 root, allocation-size corruption).

evidence.snippet: xQueueSizeInBytes = ( size_t ) ( uxQueueLength * uxItemSize ); /*lint !e961 MISRA exception as the casts are only redundant for some ports. */
evidence.reason: uxQueueLength and uxItemSize retain their full unsigned UBaseType_t domain in the analyzed configuration: lines 9 and 17 are configASSERT assertions and, per the do-not-credit rule, do not execute as constraints in a normal build. The product therefore wraps (e.g., 0x10001 * 0x10001 = 0x100020001 wraps to 0x20001 on 32-bit types), and the wrapped value becomes xQueueSizeInBytes which sizes the allocation at line 28 and the queue's advertised capacity at line 46. The absent one-statement fix is a runtime overflow check (e.g., `if( ( uxItemSize != 0 ) && ( uxQueueLength != ( xQueueSizeInBytes / uxItemSize ) ) ) return NULL;`) executed before the allocation; without it, an undersized queue storage is created, and later item writes assumed to have uxQueueLength * uxItemSize bytes overflow it (CWE-190 primary, allocation-size corruption).

evidence.snippet: pxNewQueue = ( Queue_t * ) pvPortMalloc( sizeof( Queue_t ) + xQueueSizeInBytes ); /*lint !e9087 !e9079 see comment above. */
evidence.reason: The allocation is sized from xQueueSizeInBytes, whose wrapped value is admitted at line 14 because the single guard (configASSERT at line 17) is an assertion that does not execute in the analyzed configuration. The line-30 NULL check constrains only allocation failure (different failure set), not the size, and pvPortMalloc succeeds on the undersized request, so the wrapped size reaches this allocation-sized-from-input sink unblocked. The BLOCK test confirms no shown runtime statement excludes the witness; the absent fix is the runtime overflow/early-return check.

assumptions: UBaseType_t is an unsigned base type of finite width (16/32/64-bit), so two full-domain values can make uxQueueLength * uxItemSize exceed the type width and wrap.
The analyzed configuration is a normal/release build in which configASSERT does not execute (assert-class macro); the do-not-credit rule applies, so lines 9 and 17 provide no runtime constraint.
pvPortMalloc follows standard malloc-like semantics: it returns a non-NULL block for the (wrapped) small request, which the line-30 NULL check does not reject.
limitations: The actual overflowing storage write would occur in queue send/receive paths or inside the unshown prvInitialiseNewQueue's later use of pucQueueStorage, which are outside this fragment; the in-fragment confirmed failure is the wrapped size reaching the allocation-sized-from-input operation.
If a port compiles configASSERT as an active abort-on-failure statement, the overflow path terminates at line 17 instead; that configuration is outside the analyzed normal build.
The NULL-deref candidate on pxNewQueue is fully handled by the line-30 check and is not part of this finding.

verdict.summary: Topic::publish shows no confirmed vulnerability from the fragment alone. segment[0] is guarded by segment.length()==1, and both wildcard-child dereferences are NULL-guarded; all guards pass the BREAK test. The two strongest candidates are demoted: triggeredTopics[numTriggeredTopics++] cannot exceed the implied 64 entries via any shown producer (initial value/drain reset unshown, capacity not declared in-fragment), and topic.substr(start, stop - start) keeps start <= topic.size() on every shown path (a danger would require an unshown initial caller passing start > size).

assumptions: topic and message are caller-supplied std::string_view values; the shown loop/recursion keep substr position start <= topic.size() (start = found-slash-position + 1; slash positions are at most size-1).
topic is a finite, non-empty string with a slash-capable content; std::string_view::find returns a position >= the search offset or npos.
iterator is non-NULL in the initial call, and map children values are non-NULL Topic* pointers (no shown producer of NULL).
triggeredTopics has capacity 64, implied only by the literal in numTriggeredTopics == 64 (no in-fragment declaration/allocation).
numTriggeredTopics initial value is <= 64 and drain() resets it to 0 (both unshown); under these the shown ==64 guard keeps the counter <= 64.
limitations: Out-of-bounds write at triggeredTopics[numTriggeredTopics++] (L30, L59) would require numTriggeredTopics > 64 at a registration site or capacity < 64; no shown statement can produce that from a <=64 start, and the array capacity is not established by any verbatim in-fragment declaration/allocation — the ==64 vs >=64 comparison is a hardening concern (CWE-787) that cannot be confirmed from the shown code.

topic.substr(start, stop - start) (L6) could fault only if start > topic.size(); every shown producer (loop increment L4, recursion argument L37) keeps start <= size, so a dangerous value would require an unshown initial caller violating the implied contract — out of scope.
A NULL iterator at L50 or NULL map values would require an unshown caller or unshown map contents; no NULL producer exists in the fragment.
iterator->messages[messageId] (L21, L50) uses messageId and the messages container whose type and bounds are undisclosed; no in-fragment evidence of an out-of-range write.
drain() itself is not shown; non-resetting behavior was not assumed and cannot be verified, which is why the triggeredTopics overflow stays demoted.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected by in-fragment validation: splits are constrained to [0, input_data_size] (lines 22, 26-27, 34) before being used as indices into input_data, the ngrams output is allocated at line 73 from the same cumulative count that the generation loop (lines 76-105) reproduces exactly, and ngrams_splits writes (lines 52, 57, 66) stay within the splits-shaped allocation. All status returns are guarded by OP_REQUIRES_OK. No vulnerable or absent guard resolves to ABSENT with a surviving witness.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for sink (A), line 77 `&input_data[splits_vec(i)]`. Combined with line 22 (first split == 0) and line 26 (non-decreasing), every split admitted is in [0, input_data_size]; the maximum admitted index input_data_size is only a one-past-end address formed for zero-length batches where CreateNgrams receives num_ngrams == 0 (line 83) or the preserve branch continues (lines 95-97). The guard survives the BREAK test: same value at sink, boundary [0, size] exactly matches capacity, no degenerate negative value passes line 26, and the validation executes on every non-empty path because line 47 returns when splits_vec.size() == 0.

Decisive protective statement for sink (B), ngrams output writes at lines 80/102. The buffer is sized by the exact cumulative ngram count computed in the first loop (lines 58-67, including the preserve_short bump at 63-65), and the second loop (lines 76-105) reproduces the identical per-batch count (width loop 79-85 plus preserve bump 91-104 with the zero-length skip at 95-97), so the final output_start_idx never exceeds the allocation; last write index is capacity - 1. BREAK test passes on identity, boundary, degenerate (num_ngrams >= 0), and reach.

assumptions: SPLITS_TYPE is a signed integer type (int32/int64) so the comparisons at lines 26-27 are meaningful and enforce [0, input_data_size].
get_num_ngrams(length, width) follows standard n-gram counting: non-negative, and 0 when length == 0 or width > length.
CreateNgrams writes exactly num_ngrams output entries and performs no data dereference when num_ngrams == 0.
OP_REQUIRES_OK on context->input and allocate_output aborts Compute on failure, so data and output pointers are non-null at every use.
All split values are validated before use because line 47 returns whenever splits_vec.size() == 0, and lines 20-38 run otherwise.
limitations: pad_width_ (line 101) is not validated in the fragment; a negative pad_width_ could make ngram_width <= 0, but the only consumer is the unshown CreateNgrams with a fixed num_ngrams of 1 and a buffer slot already reserved by the first-loop bump, so no in-fragment dangerous operation is demonstrated.
Truncation of data->flat<tstring>().size() (int64) into int at line 18 could misbehave only for tensors with > 2^31 elements, which is not realizable as a demonstrated witness.
Integer overflow of cumulative ngram counts (line 66) would require impossible buffer sizes and was not treated as a candidate.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation with an establishable failure set is guarded: match copies/advances are bounded by the line 92 check (window_posn + match_length <= window_size), and the window-wrap source index is bounded by the line 103 check (j = match_offset - window_posn <= window_size, with j >= 1 on that branch), so runsrc stays within the window. Both guards survive the BREAK test (identity, boundary, degenerate, reach); remaining OOB candidates (literal write via frame_end, table indexing, out_bytes truncation) cannot be proven from the shown code and are recorded as limitations.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the window-wrap source at line 107: on the branch match_offset > window_posn (line 100), j = match_offset - window_posn >= 1 (line 102); the guard admits j in [1, window_size] and excludes j >= window_size+1, so runsrc = &window[window_size - j] is always in [0, window_size-1]. The failure value (j > window_size, which would make window_size - j wrap to a huge unsigned index and read out of bounds) is excluded by the strict '>' operator. BREAK: identity (j unchanged between 102 and 107), boundary (admitted max j = window_size -> index 0; failure at j = window_size+1 excluded), degenerate (j >= 1 always on this branch), reach (guard is on the only path to line 107).

Decisive protective statement for all match copy sinks (lines 110, 113, 119) and the window_posn advance (line 121): it admits window_posn + match_length <= window_size, so every match write ends at index <= window_size-1 and reads stay inside the window. The failure set (sum >= window_size + 1) is excluded by the strict '>' check. BREAK: identity (match_length copied to i at line 98 and only reduced afterward; window_posn unchanged until line 121), boundary (admitted equality exactly fills the window; failure starts one past), degenerate (match_length >= 3, no negative lengths), reach (every match path after the switch converges on line 92 before any copy).

assumptions: The window object's extent is qtm->window_size elements: line 92 caps matches against it, line 107 indexes window[window_size - j], line 140 compares window_posn == qtm->window_size, and line 125 takes &window[window_posn] with window_posn <= window_size (one-past-end is legal and not dereferenced).
match_length is always >= 3: selector 4/5 set it to 3/4 and selector 6 adds non-negative length_base[sym] + extra + 5.
out_bytes is non-negative and nonzero whenever the decode writes happen (lines 12 and 25).
limitations: The line 59 literal write (window[window_posn++]) has no explicit window bound; proving an out-of-bounds index requires frame_end > window_size, which depends on the unshown numeric value of QTM_FRAME_SIZE (lines 47-48) and the unshown window allocation/capacity, so no witness can be derived from the fragment alone.

Indexing of qtm->position_base, qtm->extra_bits, and qtm->length_extra (lines 65, 72, 79, 83, 84) uses symbol values from unshown macro expansions; array capacities and model ranges are not visible, so these OOB candidates are unevaluable.

The final flush casts out_bytes to int (line 158); a value above INT_MAX (not excluded by any shown check) would truncate, but reaching that flush with such a value requires the line 37 loop to terminate with buffered >= out_bytes, which the window-size-bounded buffer cannot satisfy — treated as a non-termination/truncation limitation, not a demonstrated in-fragment failure.

QTM_GET_SYMBOL / QTM_READ_BITS / QTM_RESTORE_BITS / QTM_REMOVE_BITS / QTM_STORE_BITS bodies are not shown; their internal buffer-end behavior is not credited as protection and no failure is attributed to them.
Possible non-termination for an unbounded out_bytes (outer loop line 37) cannot be shown destivable because the bit-stream exhaustion path lives inside the unshown macros.

verdict.summary: Header-derived width and height are cast-checked and strictly bounded (1 <= w,h < 2^27, int64 product < 2^29) before any size arithmetic, so decode.channels*width*sizeof(...) row sizes and the new uint16[height*width*decode.channels] allocation count stay at or below 2^31-4 with decode.channels <= 4 under PNG color-type semantics, below the int32 wrap boundary; allocation-failure status is handled fail-closed before output is used, and no dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement. It excludes cast-loss (int64 comparison), non-positive, >= 2^27, and >= 2^29 values, leaving width,height in [1,2^27-1] and width*height <= 2^29-1. Every later int size expression consumes these same const values with no intervening modification: decode.channels*width*sizeof(uint8) at line 63 admits at most 2^29-4, the uint16 row bytes at lines 70/81 at most 2^30-8, and new uint16[height*width*decode.channels] at line 77 at most 2^31-4 (<= INT_MAX = 2^31-1, margin 3), assuming decode.channels is 1..4 per the successful png::CommonInitDecode call's standard PNG color-type semantics. The guard executes on every reaching path before each sink and survives the BREAK identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach tests.

assumptions: decode.width and decode.height are png_uint_32 values filled by CommonInitDecode; lines 18-20 reject unsigned-to-int cast loss via the static_cast<int64_t> comparisons, non-positive values, values >= 2^27, and int64 width*height products >= 2^29.

A successful png::CommonInitDecode (line 5) implies a valid IHDR whose color type yields decode.channels in [1,4] (PNG component-count semantics), which the 'few bits to spare' comment at lines 10-13 is designed around; this is the only non-textual invariant used.
OP_REQUIRES and OP_REQUIRES_OK abort kernel execution on a failed condition (fail-closed), so after line 56 status is OK and output is non-NULL before any dereference at lines 62/69/80/92.
allocate_output dimensions express int64 sizes; the maximum admitted element count 2^31 fits int64 without overflow.
limitations: A decode.channels value > 4 reaching line 77 would require non-standard behavior from the unshown CommonInitDecode body; per the callee standard-semantics rule this witness is blocked, so it is not a confirmed vulnerability.
The maximum legal DT_FLOAT image (~2^31 uint16 elements, about 4.3 GB buffer) is a bounded resource-usage concern, not memory unsafety; bad_alloc handling is outside the fragment.
The DecodeBmp/DecodeAndCropJpeg dead-branch rejections and decode-context teardown on rejected paths are robustness/leak concerns, not verified memory-safety findings.
No caller or init-site for op_type_, data_type_, or channels_ is shown; only the fragment-shown usage was analyzed.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected: the only pointer dereference (local->local = 1) is reachable only after find_site_by_name returns success with an early return on failure, and the only memory write is a size-bounded snprintf whose bound is below the capacity shown by its own sizeof expression.

evidence.reason: Protects sink line 31 (local->local = 1). The lookup's failure set (site not found, and any NULL local produced by an unshown callee path) is excluded on every reaching path: L25 requires DAEMON+nonempty site, then L26-29 aborts with -EINVAL whenever find_site_by_name does not return truthy, and no statement between the check and the deref modifies local. BREAK test passes (identity: same variable, no intervening write; boundary: N/A; degenerate: not-found/empty site hits the early return; reach: guard executes on all paths).

Safe sink: snprintf caps the write at sizeof(cl.lockfile)-1 bytes, so the maximum payload (sizeof-2 characters plus terminating NUL) stays strictly inside the array capacity evidenced by the named sizeof in the same call; the format string is a literal (no format-string injection). booth_conf->name %s is demoted to limitations because no NULL producer for it appears in the fragment.

assumptions: cl.lockfile is a char array whose capacity is given by sizeof(cl.lockfile), which appears in the same statement (L44).
find_site_by_name(cl.site, &local, 1) has the standard name-implied semantics of a lookup with an out-parameter: a truthy return means the found site was written to *local on this call.
limitations: booth_conf->name could in principle be NULL and reach %s at L45, but the fragment shows no assignment or path that ever makes it NULL; a NULL supplied only by an unshown producer is not an in-fragment finding.
The discarded return of find_myself (L33) is a deliberate ignore documented by the L24 comment and has no consumer in the fragment, so no status-handling flaw is demonstrable on-path.
No capacity declaration for cl.lockfile or definition of find_site_by_name/find_myself is shown; conclusions rely only on the sizeof expression and the standard call-site semantics stated above.

verdict.summary: Every nullable handshake handle is null-guarded before consumption: clientParams is rejected by the throw at lines 51-55 before the dereference at line 56, and handshakeReadHeaderCipher is excluded from the codec setter by the unconditional CHECK at line 71; the remaining member-pointer dereferences (serverHandshakeLayer, readCodec) have no in-fragment NULL producer.

assumptions: folly CHECK is an unconditional runtime check (not an NDEBUG-compiled assert or DCHECK), so CHECK(handshakeReadHeaderCipher) at line 71 executes on every path into the block at lines 70-75.
conn.serverHandshakeLayer and conn.readCodec have no NULL producer anywhere in the fragment; their non-nullness is an object/caller invariant.
The Fizz-layer getters may return null cipher/params handles; each result is guarded before reaching a consumer (lines 18, 25, 28, 31, 35, 51, 58, 70, 71).
limitations: Callee bodies (setHandshakeHeaderCipher, processClientInitialParams, updatePacingOnKeyEstablished) are unshown; no failing argument reaches them because every nullable input on those paths is guarded in the fragment.
A NULL readCodec or serverHandshakeLayer dereference would require a NULL producer that the fragment does not show, so those candidates stay demoted to assumptions.
A CHECK-abort DoS (CWE-617) would require a shown producer driving handshakeReadHeaderCipher to null while handshakeReadCipher is non-null; no such producer is visible, so it is not confirmed.

verdict.summary: parse_query advances p to start+name_part_len (line 23) and then copies 4 bytes (type at line 26, dnsclass at line 31) with no check that p+4 <= max. An attacker-controlled DNS name that ends within 0-3 bytes of the buffer end makes the pj_memcpy calls read past the valid packet region (out-of-bounds read).

evidence.reason: p = start + name_part_len (line 23) is derived from the attacker-controlled name length parsed by get_name_len (line 10) and no shown statement verifies p + 2 <= max; with a well-formed name of encoded length max-start-1, p = max-1 and this 2-byte copy reads 1 byte past the packet region bounded by max. The absent one-statement fix is a tail bounds check such as 'if (p + 4 > max) return ...;' inserted before line 26. Primary CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read).

Deciding sink: after p += 2 (line 28) this read covers [start+name_part_len+2, start+name_part_len+4); with name_part_len = max-start-2 the type copy stays in-bounds but this copy reads bytes max and max+1, fully outside the [pkt, max) region shown as the parse limit by the get_name_len/get_name calls (lines 10, 19). No guard on any reaching path excludes the witness; the same absent 'p + 4 <= max' fix would neutralize it. Primary CWE-125.

assumptions: max is the end-of-valid-data bound for the DNS packet, as shown by both parser calls passing max as the scan limit (lines 10 and 19).
get_name_len/get_name return PJ_SUCCESS for a well-formed name that occupies nearly the entire remaining packet region, so the status checks at lines 11 and 20 do not exclude the failing values.
limitations: The numeric size of the packet buffer is not declared in this fragment; the OOB claim is anchored to the in-fragment bound max rather than a declared array length.
A name_part_len exceeding max-start would make the overflow larger, but that would require non-standard parser behavior, so it is not relied on.
The *parsed_len = (int)(p - start) store is bounded by packet size and is not treated as a finding.

verdict.summary: Every entry-point value that reaches a dangerous operation is validated or status-checked within the fragment. epsilon is constrained to strictly positive before reaching the QuantileStreamResource constructor (line 10 excludes zero, the failure the fragment names, plus negatives, NaN, and -inf); both tensor pointers are only dereferenced after OP_REQUIRES_OK aborts on failure; and the CreateResource status is fail-closed for every outcome except the intentionally allowed ALREADY_EXISTS. The only unvalidated value, num_streams, reaches an unshown constructor whose failure behavior cannot be demonstrated from the fragment alone, so it is a hardening note rather than a confirmed finding.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the epsilon argument consumed by the constructor sink at lines 17-18. epsilon is a float read from the entry-point tensor (line 8); strict '>' excludes the entire named failure set {0, -0.0, negatives, NaN, -inf} and admits only (0, +inf). BREAK test: identity holds (same variable, same float precision, no modification between line 10 and line 18); boundary 0 is rejected by the strict operator; degenerate values 0/-0.0/NaN/-inf all fail the comparison and abort Compute; reach holds because the code is straight-line and every path to the constructor passes through lines 9-11.

The CreateResource status (line 19) is not discarded and is compared for all outcomes: every !ok status except ALREADY_EXISTS triggers OP_REQUIRES(context, false, status) and fails closed. The single pass-through outcome, ALREADY_EXISTS, is the comment-documented intended behavior (lines 2-3: only create one if none exists; the new resource is unref'd), so it is not a fail-open flaw and no status-handling candidate survives.

assumptions: On success of OP_REQUIRES_OK (lines 7, 14), epsilon_t and num_streams_t are valid non-NULL tensors; on failure Compute returns and no later line executes.
ALREADY_EXISTS pass-through at lines 20-22 is the intended resource-already-exists outcome per the fragment's own comment (lines 2-3).
new QuantileStreamResource does not return NULL (it throws on allocation failure), so no NULL check applies to result.
limitations: num_streams (line 15) is an unvalidated int64_t from an entry-point tensor; any harmful consequence of a negative, zero, or huge value would occur inside the unshown QuantileStreamResource constructor, and neither standard callee semantics nor in-fragment arithmetic demonstrates a failure — demoted to a hardening/robustness note.
Positive-but-extreme epsilon values (+inf, denormals) pass line 10; no in-fragment consumer demonstrates a failure for these admitted values.
max_elements_ is an unshown class member; its provenance, bounds, and any failure it could induce are not established within the fragment.
Tensor shape/dtype validation and resource-handle validity are performed by the framework outside the fragment; non-scalar tensors of wrong rank/type are not evaluated here.

verdict.summary: The loop at lines 14-16 indexes tuple[i] and calls ctx->set_output(i, ...) only for i in [0, tuple.size()-1] (line 14), and line 10 enforces tuple.size() == ctx->num_outputs() on every path reaching the loop. Therefore every index is within the tuple's own size and within the valid output range [0, num_outputs), and the discarded buf->Get return has no shown in-fragment failure path that can reach a dangerous operation. Both decisive protective statements survive the BREAK test, so no ABSENT dangerous operation exists.

assumptions: OP_REQUIRES with a false condition aborts Compute, so line 15 is unreachable unless tuple.size() == (size_t)ctx->num_outputs() (line 10).
Buffer::Tuple is an indexable container whose own size() is its extent, so tuple[i] with i < tuple.size() is in-bounds.
ctx->set_output accepts output indices in [0, num_outputs).
limitations: buf->Get's body is not shown; its discarded return is a status-handling candidate, but the fragment displays no failure path, assigns no NULL, and any size inconsistency it could produce is rejected by the line 10 equality check before the sink.
A hypothetical failure of buf->Get that still yields a tuple whose size equals num_outputs and contains bad tensors is not demonstrable from the shown code.
ctx->num_outputs() is treated as a non-negative framework-provided count; a negative value would require an out-of-scope producer not shown in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The component count m_ucCount (UBYTE, file-derived) is used as the loop bound for every component loop over fixed 4-element stack arrays (line[4], lp[4], a[4], b[4], c[4], d[4], d1..d3[4]) and is restrained only by a debug assert(m_ucCount < 4) at line 26. In a release build that assert never executes, so m_ucCount values 5..255 drive cx past capacity and perform an out-of-bounds stack write at line[cx] = CurrentLine(cx) (and lp[cx] = line[cx]->m_pData, a[cx], etc.). The missing one-statement fix is a runtime bound check (e.g., if (m_ucCount >= 4) return false;) before the line[4] fill loop.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds write: m_ucCount (UBYTE, domain 0..255) has no executing constraint in the fragment — line 26 assert(m_ucCount < 4) is debug-only and does not execute under NDEBUG — so the loop at line 30 (for(cx = 0;cx < m_ucCount;cx++)) admits cx up to 255 against the 4-element capacity declared at line 6 (struct Line *line[4];). For m_ucCount = 5, cx = 4 writes past line[4] on the stack (CWE-787). The absent fix is a runtime component-count bound (e.g., if (m_ucCount >= 4) return false;) placed before line 30; the BLOCK test passes because no shown executing statement excludes m_ucCount >= 5.

Same unvalidated m_ucCount (line 26 assert only) drives the loop at line 40 with cx up to 255 against the 4-element capacity declared at line 37 (LONG *lp[4];); m_ucCount = 5 yields cx = 4, an out-of-bounds stack write to lp[4] and a dereference of the already out-of-bounds line[cx] entry (CWE-787). The absent fix is the same runtime bound check on m_ucCount before the loop; the BLOCK test passes since no executing guard on the path excludes the witness.

assumptions: m_ucCount is a file-derived scan/component-count field (protocol header data) whose full UBYTE domain 0..255 remains after the only shown constraint, a debug assert, is discarded.
The arrays line[4] (line 6), lp[4] (line 37), and a[4], b[4], c[4], d[4], d1[4], d2[4], d3[4] (lines 48-49) are stack locals with capacity 4, so any index cx >= 4 is out of bounds.
assert() at lines 12 and 26 is compiled out under NDEBUG in normal builds and carries no protective effect, per the do-not-credit rule.
limitations: m_lJ[m_lRunIndex[0]] (line 101) was demoted because the capacity of m_lJ and the admissible range of m_lRunIndex[0] are not shown in the fragment.
The line-buffer writes *lp[cx]++ (lines 75, 109, 152) cannot be quantified independently of m_ucCount because the capacity of line[cx]->m_pData is not shown in the fragment.

A zero-width input (length == 0 at line 36) would make the inner do..while(--length) at line 155 non-terminating, but a producer of width 0 (the header parser) is outside the fragment, so that witness was demoted.
Negative lines would require m_ulRemaining[0] > INT_MAX at line 4, which no shown statement can produce.
DecodeRun at line 66 is analyzed only through its call-site argument (length), assuming it returns a run bounded by length; its exact failure behavior is not shown.

verdict.summary: Both 2-byte packet reads (lines 30 and 35) are fully constrained by the line-26 check `if (p + 4 > max) return PJLIB_UTIL_EDNSINSIZE;`, whose admitted set (p + 4 <= max) exactly covers the 4-byte span consumed by the two pj_memcpy calls; the guard executes on every reaching path before the reads and survives the BREAK test. No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained failing value.

assumptions: max points one past the last accessible byte of the packet region delimited by the start/max parameters, per the function's API contract.
p is not reassigned between the guard at line 26 and the first memcpy; it advances by 2 after the first 2-byte read, keeping the second read inside the same guarded span (p_orig+4 <= max).
pj_pool_alloc follows pjlib pool-allocator semantics (the documented NULL-returning variant is pj_pool_safe_alloc), so an unchecked allocation result is not an in-fragment NULL producer.
get_name_len's standard semantics return non-negative DNS name lengths; no shown producer can drive name_len to INT_MAX.
limitations: An int overflow of name_len+4 at line 15 would require a name_len near INT_MAX, which the fragment cannot produce (DNS name length is bounded by the callee's standard semantics).
A negative name_part_len that would move p before start is not producible from the shown code; get_name_len's standard semantics return non-negative lengths.
Bodies of get_name_len/get_name are unshown; any failure behavior inside them is not attributable to the fragment, and both return a checked status (lines 11, 20) before their results are consumed.
An unchecked pj_pool_alloc result followed by a get_name write would matter only if the allocator could return NULL, which contradicts the pool allocator's standard semantics.

verdict.summary: Both entry-point inputs consumed by the resource constructor are validated before use: epsilon is constrained to strictly positive (excluding zero, negatives, and NaN), and num_streams is constrained to non-negative. The CreateResource status is checked on every failing path other than the intentional ALREADY_EXISTS create-if-absent case. No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value within the fragment.

evidence.reason: Protective statement for the only downstream consumer of epsilon (constructor call at line 21). Admitted set after the check is (0, +inf); the failure set {0, negatives, NaN} is fully excluded (0.0f and -0.0f both fail '> 0'). BREAK test: identity holds (no modification between line 8 read and line 21 use), boundary 0 is outside the admitted set, degenerate values (INT_MIN-equivalent floats, NaN) are rejected, and the single reaching path executes the check. Resolves PRESENT.

Protective statement for num_streams before it reaches the constructor call at line 21. Admitted set is [0, INT64_MAX]; the failure set [-2^63, -1] (negative values that would convert to a huge size_t in a sized container) is fully excluded. verdict.summary: In xQueueGenericCreate, xQueueSizeInBytes is computed as ( size_t )( uxQueueLength * uxItemSize ), so the product is truncated at UBaseType_t width before conversion to size_t; an oversized product wraps to a small value that under-sizes the pvPortMalloc allocation at line 31 while the unmodified uxQueueLength and uxItemSize are recorded via prvInitialiseNewQueue at line 49, yielding queue storage too small for its declared capacity (CVE-2018-16601 class, integer overflow leading to heap mis-sizing/overflow). The only guards present are configASSERT checks, which are assert-class and compiled out by default, hence not protective.

evidence.snippet: xQueueSizeInBytes = ( size_t ) ( uxQueueLength * uxItemSize ); /*lint !e961 MISRA exception as the casts are only redundant for some ports. */
evidence.reason: CWE-190: both operands are UBaseType_t with full declared domain (line 9 configASSERT is assert-class/non-creditable and only excludes 0; uxItemSize is unconstrained), so the product is computed at UBaseType_t width and wraps before the size_t cast. Witness: 0x10001 * 0x10001 = 0x100020001 truncated to 0x00020001 (131073) on 32-bit UBaseType_t; that wrapped value is consumed by the shown allocation pxNewQueue = ( Queue_t * ) pvPortMalloc( sizeof( Queue_t ) + xQueueSizeInBytes ) at line 31 while the full factors are passed to prvInitialiseNewQueue at line 49, creating ~128 KiB of storage for a queue declaring ~4.3 GiB of item capacity. The configASSERT checks at lines 9, 17, and 20 do not protect: they are assert-class (compiled out when configASSERT is unset, the default) and lines 17/20 execute after the wrapping arithmetic, so the truncated value still reaches the allocation. Absent one-statement fix: xQueueSizeInBytes = ( size_t ) uxQueueLength * uxItemSize; (multiply at size_t width) or a creditable runtime bound check on both operands before the multiplication.

assumptions: UBaseType_t is the arithmetic width of the line 14 product (typical 16/32-bit port type); the cast to size_t happens after the wrap, which is the CVE-2018-16601 mechanism.
configASSERT defaults to an empty macro when not defined by the application, and per the analysis rules assert-class checks never count as protective statements.
limitations: The literal heap overrun occurs in unshown queue send/initialization code after the queue is used; the in-fragment demonstrated failure is the truncated size feeding the line 31 allocation together with the unmodified capacity factors recorded at line 49.
The addition-overflow configASSERT at line 20 is likewise assert-only; it would not change the verdict and is not needed for it.

The literal heap overrun occurs in unshown queue send code after the queue is used; the in-fragment demonstrated failure is the truncated size feeding the shown allocation while the full factors are recorded.

uxQueueLength/uxItemSize have no shown call site; attacker control is the standard FreeRTOS threat model for this API, but the wrap-and-undersized-allocation path itself is demonstrated wholly within the fragment.

verdict.summary: pooling_ratio_[i] is an op-attribute (user-config) value with no positive lower bound in the shown code: the only guard, input_size[i] >= pooling_ratio_[i], admits 0 and negative ratios, and the DCHECK_GT on output_size is compiled out under NDEBUG. A pooling ratio of 0 reaches the integer division input_size[i] / pooling_ratio_[i] and causes divide-by-zero (SIGFPE/UB); negative ratios additionally produce negative output sizes consumed by TensorShape and the Eigen maps.

evidence.reason: The divisor pooling_ratio_[i] is entry-point user-config data; its residual range after the only shown guard (line 19 'context, input_size[i] >= pooling_ratio_[i]') still includes 0 and negative values because tensor dims are >= 0, so the guard's admitted set intersects the sink's failure set {0}. The witness pooling_ratio_[i] == 0 with any input dim >= 0 passes line 19 and reaches this division unchanged (guard identity OK, boundary insufficient), and line 31's DCHECK_GT(output_size[i], 0) is debug-only and does not execute in normal builds. The absent one-statement fix is an added validation such as OP_REQUIRES(context, pooling_ratio_[i] > 0, ...) in the dimension loop; the primary mechanism is division by zero (CWE-369), with negative-ratio output_size (lines 48-49, 67-68) as a downstream consequence.

assumptions: Tensor dim_size() values are non-negative (Tensor semantics, line 16).
GeneratePoolingSequence (lines 39-42) follows its standard semantics of returning output_size+1 cumulative entries, which bounds the sequence loops (lines 77, 81, 94, 102).
OP_REQUIRES_OK aborts Compute() on allocation failure, making the output-tensor derefs (lines 71-74, 114-115) safe on that path.
limitations: height_cum_seq.size() - 1 (line 94) unsigned underflow would require GeneratePoolingSequence to return an empty vector, which the unshown callee cannot be shown to produce; demoted.
int64 col-offset arithmetic overflow (lines 104, 113) needs per-dimension sizes near 2^31, not derivable as a practical in-fragment witness; demoted.
Out-of-bounds col() access from a negative output_size is a downstream consequence of the same missing pooling_ratio_ > 0 validation, not an independently confirmed second sink.

verdict.summary: MulConvPushDown dereferences node_map_->GetNode() results without NULL checks. An attacker-controlled GraphDef Mul node whose input names a node absent from the NodeMap makes GetNode return NULL, and IsReallyConstant(*mul_left_child) (and the conv children derefs) crash on it; a NULL check after each GetNode is missing.

A Mul node with two non-control inputs whose input(0) references a missing node yields GetNode() == nullptr, admitted by every guard in execution order, and dereferenced here (CWE-476 NULL dereference).
