verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected: kzalloc/vzalloc results are NULL-checked before use (L8-9, L17-18, L32-33), and the only pointer-driven sink (args.head->next at L52/L55) is guarded on every reaching path by `if (args.head)` at L51, which excludes the sole failure value (NULL). No unconstrained entry-point value reaches an unprotected operation in the fragment.

evidence.reason: This list-append sink resolves PRESENT. The reaching path is fully gated by `if (args.head)` (L51), whose admitted set is exactly head != NULL, excluding the only failure value (NULL dereference of args.head at L52/L55). The while-condition (L52) keeps each L53 reassignment non-NULL, so no intervening statement can restore NULL (guard-identity audit: no drift; BREAK test passes on identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach). The allocation sinks L11/L20/L35/L36 are likewise PRESENT via L8-9, L17-18, and L32-33.

assumptions: When args.head is non-NULL it points into a valid, acyclic vidtv_encoder list, so the L52-53 walk terminates and L55 writes to an initialized node (cycle production is not shown in the fragment).
e->name may be NULL after kstrdup (L14); the fragment never dereferences it, and kfree(NULL) is valid, so no in-fragment failure exists.
e->src_buf/e->src_buf_sz (L25-26) are stored but have no consuming sink (copy/index) within this fragment.
limitations: L63 `kfree(e->encoder_buf)` frees vzalloc()'d memory with kfree (allocator mismatch, CWE-762 class), but this cleanup is reachable only when the internal `kzalloc(priv_sz)` at L31 fails (OOM); no entry-point value drives it, so it is a robustness concern, not a reachable attacker-triggerable finding.
A circular args.head list would make the L52 loop non-terminate, but no cycle-producing call site is shown in the fragment.
kstrdup failure leaves e->name NULL; not dereferenced in the fragment (would only matter at an unshown caller).

verdict.summary: sctp_make_strreset_req truncates the computed lengths to __u16 (lines 6/12/13), so for stream_num=65535 the chunk allocated at line 15 has outlen+inlen=20 bytes while sctp_addto_chunk at lines 29/40 appends stream_len up to 65534 bytes, causing a heap buffer overflow write; no bound, validation, or wider-type fix is present.

evidence.reason: stream_num has full __u16 domain 0..65535 with no in-fragment constraint; at line 6, 2*65535=131070 truncates to stream_len=65534; lines 12-13 truncate outlen to 14 and inlen to 6, so line 15 sizes the chunk at only outlen+inlen=20 bytes; guard `if (outlen)` (line 19) admits outlen=14 and guard `if (stream_len)` (line 28) admits 65534, and neither bounds the append length against the remaining capacity (wrong-object drift / nonzero-only check). Sinking 65534 bytes into a 20-byte chunk is a heap overflow write (CWE-787); absent fix: reject stream_num such that stream_num*sizeof(__u16) exceeds __u16 range (or compute lengths in a wider type without 16-bit truncation before sizing the chunk).

Independent sink on the in-request path: same truncated stream_len=65534 appended into the same 20-byte chunk after `if (inlen)` (line 32) admits inlen=6 and `if (stream_len)` (line 39) admits 65534; overflow continues the CWE-787 write, root-caused by the __u16 wrapping of the computed sizes (CWE-190) on lines 6/12/13.

assumptions: sctp_make_reconf(asoc, outlen + inlen) creates a chunk whose payload capacity is the shown length argument (capacity evidence at line 15).
sctp_addto_chunk appends its named length to the end of the chunk payload (name-implied semantics).
__u16 assignments wrap mod 65536 per the declared type.
limitations: No call site for stream_num/out/in is shown; reaching this in production requires an upstream caller to supply these values (e.g., setsockopt-derived parameters) — the in-fragment arithmetic failure is fully derivable from the declared domains regardless.
Bodies of sctp_make_reconf/sctp_addto_chunk are unshown; analysis uses the shown arguments and standard chunk-append semantics, not any hypothetical internal clamping.
NULL-deref of retval is not a finding: lines 16-17 guard it before any use.

verdict.summary: The only dereference of ImageBuf (line 21) is guarded by the immediately preceding bound check `if (bx * lprn->nBw + x >= bpl) break;` (line 20), which excludes every in-row offset >= bpl on every iteration; the guard constrains the same expression consumed by the sink, survives the BREAK test, and no other sink resolves ABSENT.

evidence.reason: PRESENT protective statement for the read `p[x]` at line 21: the guard admits only offsets bx*nBw + x < bpl and excludes the failure set bx*nBw + x >= bpl that would spill past the current scan line or buffer end. BREAK test passes: identity (same bx*nBw+x expression composes the index, no intervening write), boundary (admitted maximum bpl-1 is the last valid byte of the row), degenerate (evaluated before the first read and every iteration), reach (executes on every path to the sink).

assumptions: bpl, nBh, nBw, and BlockLine are positive device-driver fields set during device init (visible only as reads at lines 5, 6, 9, 13, 14, 20).

ImageBuf is allocated by the device with at least the rows that the caller's r/h range accesses; its byte capacity is not shown in the fragment, so row-level bounds are treated as a device invariant, not an in-fragment capacity.
limitations: Row-level OOB (y0+y beyond ImageBuf's height) cannot be confirmed: no verbatim in-fragment capacity expression for ImageBuf exists (capacity-evidence rule).

Negative y0 from `(r + h - bh) % maxY` (line 11) when an unshown caller passes r+h < bh, and integer overflow in `bx * lprn->nBw` for caller-supplied near-INT_MAX bx, have no in-fragment producer; demoted under the internal-helper rule.
Division by zero at line 11 requires maxY == 0, i.e., a device initialization with BlockLine < nBh, which no shown statement demonstrates; demoted.
The line-20 check is the documented guard for Ghostscript bug 701785; its protection is per in-row offset only, which is the failure set the shown capacity (bpl) can establish.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in ga_concat_shorten_esc: the inner loop advances s by the stale byte length of the first matched character (clen), so when a later byte sequence decodes to the same code point with a shorter byte length (e.g., a lone UTF-8 continuation byte after a 2-byte character in U+0080..U+00BF), s skips past the string's sole NUL terminator and the next evaluation of `*s` reads past the end of the string.

evidence.reason: `str` is a NUL-terminated byte string with no shown length or encoding validation (residual range: arbitrary byte sequences); its readable extent ends at the first NUL, as defined by the fragment's own `*p != NUL` (line 16) and `*s != NUL` bounds. At line 25 `s += clen;` advances `s` by the stale first-character length (clen from line 21) instead of the matched character's own byte length; with str = {0xC2,0xA0,0xA0,0x00}, mb_cptr2char_adv (line 20) yields c=0xA0 and clen=2, the lone continuation byte at p+2 decodes (standard Vim semantics: invalid lead decodes to its own byte, length 1) to 0xA0 == c, so `s += clen` moves s to p+4 and the next evaluation of line 22 reads `*s`/`mb_ptr2char(s)` one byte past the NUL at p+3. The only candidate guard, `*s != NUL`, is the sink's own read at the corrupted position (guard-identity failure), and the absent fix is an actual-length advance (e.g., `s += mb_ptr2len(s)`) or an end bound before the dereference. CWE-125.

assumptions: str is consumed as a NUL-terminated C string whose legitimate readable extent ends at the first NUL, evidenced by the fragment's own `*p != NUL` and `*s != NUL` loop bounds (lines 16 and 22).
mb_cptr2char_adv and mb_ptr2char follow standard Vim multibyte semantics: they never read past a NUL, and invalid UTF-8 lead/continuation bytes decode to the byte value with byte length 1.
limitations: The demonstrated OOB read requires a variable-width runtime encoding such as UTF-8; the fragment imposes no encoding constraint, and the witness is therefore environment-dependent.
gap has no NULL producer inside the fragment, so a NULL-gap dereference is not asserted.
same_len int overflow and unbounded looping on OOB memory are secondary consequences of the same faulty advance and are not asserted independently.

verdict.summary: ReadMATImageV4 reads the local 'status' before any initialization when the file fails the early header checks (first 32-bit word > 9999, nonzero Type digits, invalid imagf, or an empty file), and consumes partially filled pixel buffers as fully populated after a truncated row read, both being attacker-triggerable uninitialized-use flaws.

evidence.reason: 'status' (declared at lines 21-22 without initializer) is first assigned only at line 115 'status=SetImageExtent(...)'; the early-exit paths -- empty file skipping the 'while' body (line 49) and the breaks at lines 56, 62, 64, and 82 -- reach line 240 with 'status' still uninitialized. An attacker file whose first 32-bit little-endian word exceeds 9999 (the vast majority of 4-byte values) triggers 'if ((ldblk > 9999) || (ldblk < 0)) break;' (line 55-56), then line 240 reads the uninitialized stack value and bases the DestroyImageList/GetFirstImageInList control decision on it (CWE-457). Reverse protection scan finds no initializer or assigning statement on any of these paths; the absent one-statement fix is initializing 'status' (e.g., 'status=MagickFalse;') at declaration or before the loop.

The row read at line 163 requests depth/8*image->columns bytes, and ReadBlob's name-implied semantics return the count actually read: a truncated row yields count in 0..(depth/8*columns)-1, all admitted by the only guard 'if (count == -1) break;' (line 164). ImportQuantumPixels then consumes the full per-row extent from 'pixels' even though only 'count' bytes were filled; at y=0 the buffer was freshly allocated by SetQuantumDepth (line 154), so the tail is uninitialized heap and flows into the decoded image (CWE-908/CWE-457). The guard constrains 'count', not the buffer fill consumed by the sink (wrong-object drift), admits exactly the failing short values, and fails the BREAK test; the absent fix is a length-equality check 'if (count != (ssize_t)(depth/8*image->columns)) break;'.

Independent complex-part sink: the second read (line 190, 'count=ReadBlob(image,depth/8*image->columns,(char *) pixels);') is guarded only by 'count == -1' (line 191), which admits positive short counts from a truncated file; InsertComplexDoubleRow (or InsertComplexFloatRow at line 196) then interprets the full depth/8*columns-byte buffer, including the unfilled/uninitialized tail, as 'columns' doubles/floats. Same absent fix (length-equality break) as the real-part sink; CWE-908/CWE-457.

assumptions: size_t/ssize_t are 64-bit, so image->columns and image->rows (from unsigned int header fields 1..0xFFFFFFFF) and depth/8*image->columns (max 8*0xFFFFFFFF) do not overflow.
ReadBlob returns the number of bytes actually read, so a truncated row yields a non-negative count below the requested length (per its name-implied semantics and the shown arguments).
ImportQuantumPixels/InsertComplex*Row consume the whole row buffer (depth/8*columns bytes) regardless of the preceding read count, per the name-implied semantics of those calls.
limitations: A heap out-of-bounds write into 'pixels' is not claimed because the buffer capacity from GetQuantumPixels/SetQuantumDepth is not shown in the fragment (CWE-787 demoted per capacity-evidence rule).

A NULL 'pixels' resulting from discarded SetQuantumFormat/SetQuantumDepth/SetQuantumEndian statuses (lines 153-155) is not claimed: the failure path producing a NULL buffer lies inside unshown callees and no in-fragment NULL producer or documented NULL-on-failure return is shown for those calls.
The ping-mode SeekBlob with 32-bit-wrapping HDR.nCols*ldblk (line 109) is not a finding: the wrapped offset is positive and the seek result is discarded; no memory-safety sink is shown.
The (int) cast of image->columns at line 173 truncates huge dimensions to a non-positive width, which makes FixSignedValues a no-op rather than an out-of-bounds access.

verdict.summary: No dangerous operation admits a value whose failure is demonstrable from the fragment: the silence fills are bounded by the shown guards' lower-bound semantics and the buffer capacity, field signedness, and any producer of buffer_used/period_ptr exceeding period_bytes are not shown in the fragment; the pad write is bounded by the modulo-complement plus the if (size > 0) check, and all ioctl/status returns are checked.

evidence.reason: S3 pad-write sink resolves PRESENT: the guard at line 54 ('if (size > 0)') combined with the modulo/complement arithmetic at lines 53-55 constrains the admitted count to [1, period_size-1]; the excluded set is {0} and all values >= period_size, so the size reaching snd_pcm_lib_write is fully bounded and survives the BREAK test (identity, boundary, degenerate, reach).

S4 status-handling sink is PRESENT: the DRAIN ioctl return value is checked with 'if (err < 0) return err' (lines 74-75) on every path, so no failing status is consumed as success; the error path returns to the caller rather than continuing.

S1 silence fill is classified non-dangerous as demonstrated: the guard at line 26 admits buffer_used >= 1 with no upper bound, so it would not neutralize a period_bytes - buffer_used underflow, but that failure cannot be established from the fragment because the capacity of runtime->oss.buffer and the declared signedness of period_bytes/buffer_used are not shown, and no shown statement can make buffer_used exceed period_bytes; the OOB/underflow candidate is demoted per the capacity-evidence and declared-type rules.

assumptions: substream->runtime is non-NULL whenever substream != NULL since no NULL producer for runtime is shown in the fragment.
snd_pcm_kernel_ioctl and the make_ready helpers report failure via a negative return, which the fragment checks before each continued use.
runtime->oss.buffer, if it were sized in the larger program, would need an explicit in-fragment capacity to support an OOB claim; none is present.
limitations: A period_bytes - buffer_used (line 30) or period_bytes - period_ptr (line 41) unsigned-wrap underflow feeding the silence fills is not confirmable: the operands' types are not declared in the fragment, no capacity for runtime->oss.buffer appears, and no producer of buffer_used/period_ptr > period_bytes is shown; the witness fails the BLOCK test, so it is demoted.

Division/modulo hazards (width == 0 at lines 30/44, period_size == 0 at line 53) have no in-fragment producer since the format/width derivation and parameter validation are unshown; they are noted, not findings.
The return values of snd_pcm_lib_write/snd_pcm_lib_writev are discarded, but this is a best-effort silence-pad operation with a bounded count and no shown security-relevant consumer.
Membership of this fragment in the vulnerable/fixed pair was not used as evidence; the verdict rests solely on the BLOCK/BREAK tests applied to the shown statements.

verdict.summary: In the CONFIGURE_FILE_USE_NODE/EUID path, the config-file loop copies an item into big_buffer (capacity big_buffer_size, shown as the size argument at line 10) without bounding its length, then sprintf() writes the euid/node suffix into suffix = filename + Ustrlen(filename); with an item near big_buffer_size-1 characters the ~279-byte write overruns big_buffer (CWE-787). Independently, expand_string(host_number_string) is passed unchecked to Ustrtol at line 391, so an expansion failure (NULL per the fragment's own sibling checks at lines 236/250/310) dereferences NULL (CWE-476).

evidence.reason: filename length L is unconstrained except by the string_nextinlist copy cap at lines 10-11 (L can be big_buffer_size-1); suffix (line 16) is big_buffer+L and sprintf writes up to ~279 bytes (dot + %ld up to 20 digits + dot + %.256s), so the write end L+279 exceeds the capacity big_buffer_size established by the line-10 size argument; no length or remaining-space check exists on any path to this sink. The absent one-statement fix is a bound of L plus the appended suffix against big_buffer_size before the call (or a bounded snprintf with big_buffer_size-(suffix-big_buffer)); primary mechanism is an out-of-bounds memory write (CWE-787).

Same unguarded pattern as line 25: suffix = filename+Ustrlen(filename) (line 16) and L is bounded only by the line-10 copy cap; sprintf writes up to ~258 bytes (1 dot + 256 chars + NUL) past the filename end, overflowing big_buffer when L is within ~257 bytes of big_buffer_size; no protective length check exists (CWE-787).

Same unguarded pattern as lines 25/30: suffix points at big_buffer+L with L admitted up to big_buffer_size-1 by the line-10 copy cap; the %ld write (up to ~22 bytes with NUL) exceeds big_buffer when L+22 > big_buffer_size; no bounds check precedes it (CWE-787).

s = expand_string(host_number_string) at line 390 can be NULL on expansion failure (standard semantics, corroborated by the fragment's own NULL checks after expand_string at lines 236, 250 and 310), and no NULL check exists between line 390 and this use; the guard at line 387 constrains only host_number_string (wrong-object drift, guard-identity class 2), so s==NULL reaches Ustrtol/strtol and is dereferenced (CWE-476). The absent one-statement fix is an 'if (s == NULL)' PANIC_DIE after line 390, mirroring lines 235-238.

assumptions: big_buffer's capacity is big_buffer_size, evidenced in-fragment by the consuming call string_nextinlist(&list,&sep,big_buffer,big_buffer_size) at lines 10-11.

The analyzed build configuration has CONFIGURE_FILE_USE_NODE and CONFIGURE_FILE_USE_EUID defined so that lines 25, 30 and 41 are compiled; the #else branch (line 57) is the default configuration without these sinks.
uname() succeeds on the reaching path (line 22), which is the normal OS-level result and is not excluded by any shown statement.
LOG_PANIC_DIE log_write terminates, which is relied on to keep config_file non-NULL at fileno(config_file) (line 90).
limitations: The line-25/30/41 overflow requires a config-file-list item at least ~big_buffer_size-280 characters; the list is root/CLI-supplied in the trusted path, but the fragment shows no length constraint, so the residual range is treated as unconstrained per the analysis rules.
expand_string returning NULL requires a failing expansion (e.g., undefined variable or lookup failure) of host_number_string; with a successful expansion the NULL-deref sink is not reached.
Owner/group/mode checks (lines 94-105), getpwuid and parse_extract_address NULL checks, and the log_file_path '%' validation were audited and contain no admitted failing value.

Demoted candidates: fileno(config_file) depends on PANIC_DIE semantics of log_write; t[1]/Ustrchr(t+2,'%') at lines 263-267 cannot read past the terminating NUL due to short-circuit evaluation and start-at-NUL behavior.

verdict.summary: In parse_rtcp_bye, the BYE reason length byte at pkt[8] (range 0..255, attacker-controlled) is copied to reason.slen bounded only by the destination buffer size; pj_memcpy then reads reason.slen bytes from pkt+9 while the only size guard (size > 8) merely verifies byte 8 is present. A 9-byte packet carrying reason length >= 1 reads past the packet's valid size bytes, an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: The source read copies reason.slen bytes from pkt+9. reason.slen is derived at lines 9-10 as PJ_MIN(sizeof(sess->stat.peer_sdes_buf_), *((pj_uint8_t*)pkt+8)); the length byte is entry-point data with residual range 0..255 and no shown minimum, and the only path guard, 'if (size > 8)' (line 8), admits size == 9, leaving size - 9 = 0 valid bytes at offset 9. A witness of size == 9 with pkt[8] == 1 yields reason.slen == 1 (destination capacity >= 1), so the memcpy reads 1 byte past the packet; the PJ_MIN constrains the destination write only and exhibits wrong-bound drift for the source read. Absent fix: bound the length by the remaining packet size, e.g., PJ_MIN(..., size - 9) or check 'if (size < 9 + reason.slen)'. Mechanism: attacker-controlled length byte causes an out-of-bounds read from a network packet buffer (CWE-125).

assumptions: pkt contains exactly size accessible bytes, as demonstrated by the fragment's own size-bounded reads at pkt+8 and pkt+9.
sess->stat.peer_sdes_buf_ is a positive-capacity string buffer (capacity >= 1), needed so pkt[8] == 1 yields reason.slen == 1.
limitations: If the packet buffer is embedded in a larger allocation, the over-read may not cross an unmapped page, but it still reads outside the fragment's established size bound (undefined behavior and potential disclosure).
The destination write itself is safely capped by PJ_MIN(sizeof(peer_sdes_buf_), ...) and is not part of the finding.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in ReadMATImageV4 is either protected by a statement that survives the BREAK test or has no demonstrable in-fragment failure set. The entry-derived ldblk is bounded to 0..9999 at line 55 before the ping-mode SeekBlob product (line 109) can be formed, nameLen is capped at 0xFFFF at line 83 before the skip loop, column/row extents are validated for nonzero values (line 103) and by the checked SetImageExtent status (lines 115-117) before pixel-cache access, and the quantum/cache/image pointers are NULL-checked (121-122, 168-169, 207-208). No witness survives the BLOCK test; short reads and the ignored SetQuantum* statuses are robustness concerns whose memory impact depends on unshown callee internals.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the SeekBlob sink at line 109: it excludes ldblk>9999 and ldblk<0, leaving residual 0..9999; the shown divisions (57-60) and Type[3]/Type[2] checks further reduce it to the M digit 0..9, so after line 108 the product HDR.nCols*ldblk ≤ 18*(2^32-1) ≈ 7.7e10 fits signed long/MagickOffsetType with no overflow. BREAK test passes: same variable at same precision, no intervening write, boundary below capacity, executes on every path before the sink.

Decisive protective statement for the entry-driven name-skip loop at line 85: it excludes nameLen>0xFFFF, so the loop admits at most 65535 byte reads (index i ≤ 65534) and terminates; the EOF break at lines 94-99 covers truncated names. BREAK test passes: identity (same variable), boundary (< 65536), degenerate (nameLen=0 → zero iterations), reach (on every path before the loop).

Decisive protective statement for the pixel-cache region sink at line 166 and the row loops (158, 185): entry-derived HDR.nRows/nCols are constrained to 1..2^32-1, and SetImageExtent (115, status checked 116-117) bounds the extent, so QueueAuthenticPixels(...,0,rows-y-1,columns,1,...) with y in 0..rows-1 stays in-bounds; the result is NULL-checked at 168-169. BREAK test passes: identity, boundary, degenerate (zero extents returned), reach on every path.

assumptions: long/MagickOffsetType are 64-bit, making the 18*(2^32-1) seek product overflow-proof; on a 32-bit long build the line 55 guard still keeps the operands small enough that any modular wrap is a benign forward/backward mis-seek re-validated by the per-header checks (55, 81, 83, 103).
Image extent validity is enforced by the checked SetImageExtent call (lines 115-117), which is the shown allocation/bound gate for the pixel cache.
depth/8*image->columns (lines 163, 190) is at most 2^35 with size_t arithmetic; no in-fragment wrapping is shown.
limitations: Row-read short counts (count in 0..requested-1, lines 164/191 only reject -1) let ImportQuantumPixels consume partially-read/stale pixels, but pixels' capacity is not shown in-fragment (GetQuantumPixels is an unshown accessor) and no shown arithmetic exceeds a shown capacity, so this is a robustness concern, not a confirmed CWE-125/457 in the fragment.

SetQuantumFormat/Depth/Endian statuses (153-155) are overwritten/discarded; any undersized-buffer consequence of their OOM failure would originate inside unshown callee bodies, which the fragment does not display, so it cannot be confirmed (CWE-754 candidate demoted).

GetQuantumPixels (157), FixSignedValues (173), and InsertComplexDoubleRow/InsertComplexFloatRow (194/196) have unshown bodies; no NULL producer and no capacity/index arithmetic is demonstrated in-fragment, so those candidates were demoted per the capacity-evidence and NULL-producer rules.

Ping-mode SeekBlob (109) ignores its return value; a failed seek only mispositions the parser, and every subsequent object header is re-validated by the shown checks, so no memory-safety consequence is demonstrated in-fragment.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation whose object capacity is shown in the fragment is guarded: pattern-decode writes are capped by `if (row >= 64) break;` (admitted rows 0..63 give max byte offset 10239 < capacity 10240 from line 249) plus `chn = pi&31` (0..31); packed-buffer reads are bounded by `size` against the `size+5` allocation; and the loadModuleSample status is checked before continued use. Accesses whose target capacities are not shown in the fragment (header->ord, module->smp/instr/phead) have no derivable failure set, so no confirmed vulnerability exists.

evidence.reason: Protective statement resolving the pattern slot-write sink at lines 327-341: it excludes row >= 64; the only row increment (line 308) is immediately followed by this guard, so every reaching path carries row in 0..63. Max admitted offset 63*32*5 + 31*5 + 4 = 10239 < capacity 64*32*5 = 10240 (line 249), and chn is separately masked to 0..31 at line 320. BREAK test passed on identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach.
Channel-index bound: `pi&31` admits chn in 0..31, matching the 32-slot row layout of the 10240-byte pattern buffer; with row capped at 63 the highest written byte is 10239, inside capacity.
Return-status check for module->loadModuleSample (line 385): every non-MP_OK outcome returns before any further use of the sample data on that path, so no unchecked status consumption remains.

assumptions: pattern buffer capacity is 64*32*5 = 10240 bytes as shown at line 249.
packed buffer capacity is size+5 (line 285) with size from a 16-bit readWord (<= 65535) reduced by 2 at lines 279-283.
safeRead bounds its reads to the named [index, size) range per its name-implied semantics.
readWord/readByte/readDword return 16/8/32-bit unsigned values from the file stream.
limitations: Capacity of header->ord is not shown in the fragment, so the copy at line 83 (`header->ord[j++] = orders[i]`) has no derivable failure set and cannot be resolved as an OOB candidate.

Capacities of module->smp, module->instr, and module->phead are not shown, so smp[s], instr[i], and phead[i] accesses (lines 139-202, 233, 274-383, 396, 359) are demoted; the file-driven counts (insnum/patnum up to 65535) would need the matching array bounds confirmed elsewhere.
Unchecked return values of f.read/f.readWords (truncated-file behavior) are not shown producing a failing value inside the fragment, so no status-handling finding is confirmed.
strcpy at line 408 copies a fixed 17-byte literal; the tracker field capacity is not shown but the content is constant and not attacker-influenced.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous write in print_media_desc is preceded on all reaching paths by a protective statement: the top-level length check (L9) covers the media/transport memcpys, the per-format remaining-space check (L28) covers each fmt copy, the >=2 check (L37) covers the CRLF write, and the <0 status checks (L47/L56/L65) gate the subprinter results before p is advanced. Candidates that depend on unshown field widths or callee behavior fail the BLOCK test.

evidence.reason: Protective statement for the L14 media memcpy (and L25 transport memcpy). Capacity buf[0,len) is fixed at L4 ('char *end = buf+len;'). The guard excludes {len < media.slen+transport.slen+36}; after it passes, the media copy occupying buf[2, 2+media.slen) satisfies 2+media.slen <= media.slen+transport.slen+36 <= len, and the fixed prefix before the transport copy leaves the 36-byte slack. BREAK test: identity (same slen values, no intervening modification), boundary, degenerate (zero slens), and reach (executes before any write on every path) all pass.

Protective statement for the L29-L30 fmt writes (' ' plus pj_memcpy of fmt[i].slen bytes = slen+1 bytes). The guard admits only end-p >= slen+1, so the last written byte is at p+slen <= (end-p)-1+p = end-1; it excludes {end-p <= fmt[i].slen}, which would be exactly the overflow set. BREAK test: identity (same p, end, slen at use), boundary (admitted set starts one past the failure boundary), degenerate (slen==0 requires end-p >= 1; end-p==0 returns -1 in the else), and reach (per-iteration, before the write) all pass.

Protective statement for the CRLF writes at L38-L39 (2 bytes). Guard excludes {end-p < 2}; with end-p >= 2 the writes end at end-1, inside capacity. BREAK test passes on identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach.

Return-status check for print_connection_info (same pattern at L56 for print_bandw and L65 for print_attr). p += printed executes only when printed >= 0, i.e., the subprinter reported a non-negative byte count under its documented size-bounded contract; the <0 failure set causes an early return before any pointer advance. BREAK test passes on the call-result value with no intervening modification; L45 additionally NULL-checks m->conn before the call.

assumptions: Output capacity established at L4: writes are bounded by the interval [buf, buf+len).

The guard constrains the exact value consumed (no intervening modification) and executes unconditionally on every path to the memcpy; degenerate sizes (size=9 -> 0-byte copy; byte=255 with small packet -> slen=size-9) remain in bounds.

assumptions: size is an unsigned size type (pj_size_t), so size-9 cannot underflow on the size > 8 path.

PJ_LOG passing pj_size_t reason.slen to the '%.*s' precision (expected int) is a minor type-mismatch robustness point, not a vulnerability given the literal format and the small bounded value.

verdict.summary: The directory-entry name area is sized to SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1 bytes and the on-disk size field is rejected with `if(dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN)` before the name read (dire->size + 1 bytes) and the NUL write (index dire->size + 1), so every admitted value stays within the 257-byte name capacity. Guard identity holds (same dire->size, no intervening modification), boundary does not coincide with failure, degenerate size=0 is safe, and the guard executes on every path reaching the sink (both swap and non-swap branches pass through it).

Protective statement bounding the inner entry loop (line 68 while(dir_count--)) to at most SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT (256) iterations, so directory-entry processing cannot loop unboundedly on corrupted dirh.count; each entry is read into the fixed 262-byte buffer with res-checked read_directory_data calls.

SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT is 256, bounding the inner dir_count loop.

limitations: read_inode's result is dereferenced at lines 25-32 without a NULL check, but no in-fragment producer can make it NULL (its body is unshown and its standard semantics is allocate-or-abort), so no NULL-deref witness is derivable from the fragment alone.

verdict.summary: virtbt_rx_handle dereferences skb->data and pulls one byte without any skb->len check. A zero-length virtio RX packet reaches an out-of-payload read at line 5, the failed skb_pull status at line 6 is discarded, and the malformed skb is then forwarded to hci_recv_frame at line 14.

evidence.reason: skb->data is dereferenced with no shown bound on skb->len; the fragment's own consuming call skb_pull(skb, 1) at line 6 establishes the 1-byte minimum that is never enforced, so the entry-point packet's residual range still includes len == 0. No guard exists on the reaching path (reverse scan from line 5 finds no early return or length check), skb_pull's NULL result at line 6 is discarded, and the same skb is consumed at line 14, so the witness len == 0 survives the BLOCK test. The absent fix is a length guard (if (skb->len < 1) { kfree_skb(skb); return; }) before line 5; the read of one byte beyond skb->len is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) feeding garbage pkt_type into the HCI dispatch.

The skb arrives from the virtio RX path as a device-controlled network packet, so its length is entry-point input with no shown minimum.
limitations: hci_recv_frame's body is unshown; the downstream effect of a zero-length/garbage-typed skb is not demonstrated in-fragment, though the failed-pull status discard and continued consumption at line 14 are shown.

With len == 0 the single read at line 5 falls in the skb headroom (within the allocation), so the confirmed in-fragment failure is an out-of-payload read and unchecked skb_pull failure, not an allocation-boundary overrun by itself.
The missing switch default leaks skbs for unmatched garbage pkt_type values; treated as a robustness/resource concern, not an independent memory-safety finding.

verdict.summary: The fragment contains no dangerous operation with an in-fragment producer for its failure set. verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is guarded. The directory-name consumption (read at L77-78, NUL write at L82) is preceded by the guard at L72 excluding dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN, and the line-5 buffer provides SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1 bytes of name capacity, so the maximum admitted read length (256) and NUL index (256) stay in bounds (capacity 257). Together with the L72 guard this resolves the name write PRESENT.

assumptions: SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN == 256 and SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT == 256, the comparator literals the guards test against, so the guards admit dire->size <= 255 and dir_count <= 256.
dire->name is a flexible-array member at the end of struct squashfs_dir_entry, making the name capacity in the L5 buffer exactly SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1.
read_directory_data returns FALSE only when it cannot supply the requested length and otherwise copies exactly that many bytes; its FALSE return is checked at L46, L64, and L79.
MEM_ERROR() is the conventional print-and-exit error macro, so the NULL checks at L19 and L95 divert control before any dereference.
limitations: The read_inode result at L16 is dereferenced at L24-L28, L31, and L40-L42 without a NULL check, but the fragment shows no NULL producer (callee body unshown, no named NULL-on-failure semantics), so NULL deref is not a confirmable finding.

verdict.summary: On the first realloc failure (i==0, result still NULL), the guard `if (!tmp && result)` at L8 is false, so `tmp` NULL is propagated to `result` at L16 and dereferenced at L17, a NULL-pointer write; absent fix is `if (!tmp)`. Guard L8 `if (!tmp && result)` admits this state (result is NULL, conjunction false), skipping the error branch; L16 assigns `result = tmp` (NULL) and L17 writes `result[0]`, a NULL-pointer dereference/write (CWE-476). The absent fix is `if (!tmp)` so the failure is handled regardless of `result`.

limitations: Both confirmed findings require a realloc failure (heap-pressure event), not a pure attacker-supplied value; the fragment nonetheless models and handles that outcome, so the paths are shown.

`dupstr(arg)` returning NULL would make `strtok(copy, delim)` the first-ever call with a NULL cursor (undefined behavior), but dupstr's body is unshown and this UB occurs inside the callee; recorded here rather than as a separate finding.

verdict.summary: One-byte out-of-bounds read of the client-supplied cipher-suite vector: the parity check `if (datalen % 2 != 0)` (line 78) is placed after the first loop (lines 13-39), which already reads `data[i + 1]` at lines 17 and 30. The parity guard `if (datalen % 2 != 0)` (line 78) constrains the same value but executes after this loop (check-then-use order inverted), so it protects nothing here. Absent one-statement fix: apply the even-length rejection before line 13 (or iterate with `i + 1 < datalen`). Mechanism: one-byte OOB read from a network-controlled buffer (CWE-125).

Same ABSENT guard as the line-30 sink: with odd attacker-chosen `datalen` and `data[datalen-1] == GNUTLS_RENEGO_PROTECTION_REQUEST_MAJOR` (and `sr != SR_DISABLED`, line 15), the last loop iteration reads `data[datalen]`, one byte past the `datalen`-byte extent established by the loop bound at line 13; the parity check at line 78 executes only after the loop. Same absent fix as named for line 30; CWE-125.

assumptions: `data` points to exactly `datalen` accessible bytes, per the fragment's own length parameter used as the loop bound at line 13 (`i < datalen`).
The 2-byte `session->security_parameters.cipher_suite` field matches the fixed 2-byte memset/memcpy sizes.

`cipher_suites` indexing (lines 97-108, 122-134) is bounded only by callee name-implied semantics (`_gnutls_supported_ciphersuites` writes at most the passed `sizeof(cipher_suites)`; `_gnutls_remove_unwanted_ciphersuites` returns a count <= its input); bodies are unshown, so no in-fragment derivation of an over-capacity count exists.

The c<4 bound only constrains the huff/free index, not the dp position.

Loop line 30 (`dp < data+len && (c = *dp++) < 4`) admits a final c-read at data[65534]/data[65532] with c<4, after which make_decoder_ref(&dp) is invoked with *bufp = data+65535/data+65533 and, per standard Huffman-table semantics, reads 16+ bytes, touching indices >= 65536 — beyond the data[0x10000] (65536-byte, line 5) capacity. Guards line 16 (0xffc4 passes) and line 30 (bounds only the array index c, not dp) do not exclude the witness. ushort len (line 4) is 16-bit unsigned; the int subtraction at line 15 wraps on truncation for L=0/1.

limitations: jh->huff[]/jh->free[] element counts and other struct jhead field capacities are not declared in the fragment, so the propagation writes at lines 43/45/46 (indices up to huff[5]) and the exact in-bounds status of the c<4 writes cannot be independently confirmed; they are not the basis of the verdict.

The exact byte count read by make_decoder_ref is unshown; the over-read size (1..16 bytes past index 65535) depends on that standard table-parse behavior, which is inferred from the call's name and role.
Return values of the fread calls (lines 10, 13, 17) are discarded; this can cause parsing of stale in-bounds bytes for short reads but produces no in-fragment memory-safety failure.
The SOS reads at lines 34-35 index at most 513, within the 65536-byte array; a missing minimum-length check there is a validation-only concern, not a confirmed memory error.

verdict.summary: The inner loop in find_match_text compares match_text against rex.line at offset col + len2 (line 15) and again in the composing-character check (line 26) with no bound relating col + len2 to the line's extent. The bodies of hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call and hw_atl_utils_fw_downld_dwords are unshown; they are analyzed only through the shown arguments and guards, so no additional failure is attributed to them.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in sixpack_close is protected: the NULL guard `if (!sp) return;` (lines 9-10) executes on the only path reaching each sp->... use and excludes the sole failing value (NULL); no other dangerous operation (indexing, copy, injection, allocation, discarded status) admits an unconstrained value within the fragment. verdict.summary: Off-by-one index validation in the IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_FD_FIXED path: the check `fd > ctx->nr_user_files` admits fd == ctx->nr_user_files, so a boundary (or, when the fixed-file table is empty, index 0) file-table slot is consumed by io_fixed_file_slot and the wrong-file cancellation proceeds instead of returning -EBADF. evidence.reason: Entry-point-controlled `fd` keeps its full int range until line 11; the guard `if (unlikely(fd > ctx->nr_user_files))` admits fd == ctx->nr_user_files, but `ctx->nr_user_files` (lines 11 and 13) is the capacity of the `ctx->file_table` fixed-file array indexed here (valid indices 0..nr_user_files-1). The required comparison is `>=`; with `>`, the equality case survives: for nr_user_files == 0 and fd == 0, array_index_nospec(0,0) returns 0 (index >= size is masked to 0), producing an OOB read at slot 0 of a zero-length table (CWE-787), and for non-zero tables slot 0 is wrongly consumed. Absent one-statement fix: `if (unlikely(fd >= ctx->nr_user_files)) return -EBADF;`. The mechanism is an off-by-one comparison at a security boundary (primary CWE-697), with CWE-787 as the degenerate manifestation.

The admitted boundary value fd == ctx->nr_user_files reaches this security-relevant consumer: __io_async_cancel executes with cd->file taken from fixed-file slot 0 instead of the branch returning -EBADF, so the wrong file's requests are cancelled — a wrong-comparison superset admission (CWE-697) at a security decision, caused by the line 11 operator being `>` rather than `>=`.

assumptions: ctx->nr_user_files, used at lines 11 and 13, is the entry count/capacity of ctx->file_table's fixed-file array indexed at line 14 (ties the size to the object by the shown consuming call).
array_index_nospec follows its standard kernel semantics: returns the index when index < size, otherwise masks to 0.
io_fixed_file_slot is a direct slot accessor with no shown internal bounds check.
limitations: The OOB read (CWE-787) requires the degenerate fixed-file table state nr_user_files == 0 with fd == 0; if an unshown caller guarantees nr_user_files >= 1 whenever IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_FD_FIXED is used, that manifestation is demoted, but the CWE-697 wrong-comparison finding (boundary value admitted into the fixed-file cancel path) remains.
NULL dereference of cd or cd->ctx is not a finding: no shown statement produces NULL for these pointers.
The downstream impact of cancelling fixed-file slot 0's requests depends on ring state not shown here; the confirmed failure is the premature admission of the boundary index itself.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in get_complex_object: when pyc->magic_int & 0xffff > 62061, the complex-number length is read via get_st32 into ut32 n1/n2 with no bound check. For n1=0xFFFFFFFF (st32 -1), malloc(n1+1) wraps to a 0-byte allocation (CWE-190), and rz_buf_read(buffer, s1, n1) then writes attacker-controlled file bytes past the allocation (CWE-787); s1[n1]='\0' repeats the OOB index write. The post-read size!=n1 check and malloc NULL checks do not constrain n1.

evidence.reason: n1 is attacker-controlled: line 16 'n1 = get_st32(buffer, &error);' (selected when line 13's magic branch is false) assigns a signed 32-bit value into ut32 n1, admitting the full unsigned domain including 0xFFFFFFFF. The allocation at line 23 'ut8 *s1 = malloc(n1 + 1);' computes n1+1 in ut32 arithmetic, wrapping to 0 for n1=0xFFFFFFFF, so s1 has 0 capacity. The check at line 24 'if (!s1)' admits the standard non-NULL malloc(0) outcome, and the short-read check at line 29 'if (size != n1)' executes only after this call has already written, so it protects nothing here. The absent fix is a bound/validation of n1 before malloc (e.g., reject n1 == 0xFFFFFFFF or clamp n1), which is not present. Primary mechanism: heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) driven by an undersized allocation from unsigned wrap (CWE-190).

Index write with attacker-controlled n1 (0..0xFFFFFFFF from get_st32 at line 16) into the line-23 allocation whose ut32 capacity is n1+1 mod 2^32 (0 for n1=0xFFFFFFFF). The preceding size!=n1 check (line 29) admits this case when the buffer supplies 0xFFFFFFFF bytes, and it cannot undo the same overflow already performed by rz_buf_read at line 28. No bound guard exists on n1; the absent one-statement fix is a length check on n1 before use.

Independent second sink with the identical unbounded flow: n2 comes from get_st32 at line 39 (ut32 domain, including 0xFFFFFFFF), malloc(n2+1) at line 44 wraps to 0 bytes, and this call writes attacker file bytes past s2. The line 50 'if (size != n2)' check is post-sink, and line 45 'if (!s2)' admits a non-NULL malloc(0). No bound/validation on n2 is present.

assumptions: n1/n2 are declared ut32, so malloc(n1 + 1)/malloc(n2 + 1) use unsigned 32-bit arithmetic; capacity is the verbatim expressions at lines 23 and 44 (0 bytes when the length is 0xFFFFFFFF).
get_st32 returns a signed 32-bit value; -1 converts to 0xFFFFFFFF in the ut32 locals at lines 16 and 39.
pyc->magic_int and buffer contents are entry-point (pyc file header/body); no shown validation prevents an attacker from taking the else branch at lines 15/38 with magic_int & 0xffff > 62061.
C11 permits malloc(0) to return a non-NULL pointer (glibc does), so the NULL checks at lines 24 and 45 need not trigger.
limitations: On allocators that return NULL for malloc(0), the check at line 24/45 would block this specific witness (implementation-defined outcome).
Reaching the s1[n1]='\0' write (line 34) alone requires the buffer to contain 0xFFFFFFFF bytes (~4GiB file), but the in-call overflow at rz_buf_read (line 28) occurs with just one readable byte.
Memory leaks when the second parse fails (lines 40-42: s1, ret not freed) or after malloc failure (lines 24-26, 45-47: s1/ret or s1 leaked) are robustness concerns, not memory-safety findings.

verdict.summary: The unvalidated entry-point __u16 stream_num is multiplied and summed in 16-bit arithmetic, wrapping stream_len/outlen so the reconfig chunk is reserved for only a few bytes while sctp_addto_chunk then appends sizeof(struct)+65534 bytes, overflowing the heap buffer.

evidence.reason: stream_num (line 3, full __u16 domain 0..65535, no shown bound) with value 65535 and out=1/in=0 makes stream_len = 65535*2 mod 65536 = 65534 (line 6) and outlen = (sizeof(outreq)+65534) mod 65536 = sizeof(outreq)-2, so the reservation SCTP_PAD4(outlen)+SCTP_PAD4(inlen) at line 15 is only <= sizeof(outreq)+2 bytes while this copy appends sizeof(outreq)+65534 bytes; guards `if (outlen)` (line 19) and `if (stream_len)` (line 28) admit the witness (14 and 65534) and do not bound magnitude, so the guard-identity/boundary checks fail and the heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) proceeds, rooted in the __u16 wrap (CWE-190). The absent one-statement fix is a stream_num upper-bound check (e.g. `if (stream_num > SCTP_MAX_STREAMS) return NULL;`) before the sizing arithmetic.

Parallel sink: with in=1 (and stream_num=65535), inlen = (sizeof(inreq)+65534) mod 65536 = sizeof(inreq)-2 (nonzero), PAD4 reserves <= sizeof(inreq)+2 bytes, and this copy appends sizeof(inreq)+65534 bytes, the same overflow after guards `if (inlen)` (line 32) and `if (stream_len)` (line 39), missing the same stream_num bound.

assumptions: sctp_make_reconf reserves a chunk whose payload area holds SCTP_PAD4(outlen)+SCTP_PAD4(inlen) bytes (line 15).
sctp_addto_chunk appends the named len bytes into the chunk's reserved data area (name-implied semantics for the 'add to chunk' API; the chunk's capacity is the reservation quoted at line 15).

The wrap arithmetic holds for any SCTP param struct size S >= 2: appended S+65534 always exceeds reserved PAD4(S-2) <= S+2, so the exact sizeof(outreq)/sizeof(inreq) values (e.g. 16/8 per RFC 6525) only shift the numbers, not the failure.
limitations: An OOB read or NULL dereference of stream_list itself is not claimed: its capacity and NULL-ness are established only by an unshown caller.
asoc NULL dereference is not claimed: no in-fragment NULL producer exists.

If sctp_addto_chunk were (contrary to its name-implied semantics) to grow the chunk instead of writing into the reservation, the failure would degrade to a wire-length/format inconsistency; that callee-internal behavior is unshown, which is why confidence is not higher.

A secondary issue is the long-to-int truncation of the ftell() file length before omAlloc, letting a very large edited file overflow the allocated buffer in myfread/body[len].

Witness EDITOR="vi; touch /tmp/pwned" contains a space, is admitted at line 49, reaches system() at line 58, and survives the BLOCK test with no shown statement excluding it. Absent fix: reject EDITOR values containing shell metacharacters or replace system(p) with an argv-based execvp launch. Primary CWE-78.

len comes from ftell(fp) at line 75 with no shown cap and reflects attacker-edited file content; the buffer was allocated as omAlloc((int)len+1) at line 79, truncating long to int. With len = 2^32+16 the allocation is 17 bytes while myfread writes len bytes, overflowing the heap (also body[len]='\0' at line 81 indexes past the 17-byte buffer). No guard on the path bounds len. Weakly confirmed secondary CWE-787 via CWE-195 truncation.

assumptions: EDITOR/VISUAL environment strings are entry-point, attacker-controllable inputs per the provenance rules.
The capacity of the command buffer at line 56 (strlen(editor)+strlen(filename)+2) exactly matches the "%s %s" payload plus NUL, so sprintf at line 57 is correctly sized.
File content after the user invokes the editor is attacker-influenced, making len at line 75 arbitrary large.
f is an int, so f=NULL at line 15 is benign and has no later use on its path.
limitations: The unchecked write() return at line 39 could leave a truncated file, but no in-fragment memory-safety consequence is shown.
The unchecked myfread() return at line 80 could leave uninitialized bytes, a robustness/information concern without a confirmed memory failure path in the fragment.
The CWE-787 witness requires an edited file of at least 2^32 bytes (e.g., a sparse file), an extreme boundary that caps confidence.
The execlp path at line 51 is non-dangerous because it invokes no shell interpreter.
editor allocated by omStrDup at line 24 is never freed (memory leak, not a security failure).

If an external caller were assumed to emit only spec-conformant 10-before-42 sequences, the -1 path would be unreachable, but the fragment itself shows no such constraint and line 17 directly produces the -1 value, so that assumption is rejected per the caller-independence rule.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in esp6_output_head is protected by an in-fragment guard that survives the BREAK test: the frag-array write (lines 55-56) is bounded by 'nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS' (lines 29-30) with the same index value re-read at line 53; the page-frag write is bounded by the skb_page_frag_refill status check (line 41) after sizing with ALIGN(tailen) (line 37); the tail append and trailer fill are bounded by 'tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)' (line 23) on the in-place path and by the checked skb_cow_data result (lines 78-80) on the cow path; the large-packet path is redirected by the allocsz cap (lines 18-20). No sink admits an unconstrained value, so the fragment is not vulnerable.

evidence.reason: Tail-append sink. On the in-place path the guard at line 23 'tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)' admits only tailen in [0, skb_tailroom]; the largest admitted positive value equals the tail capacity, which pskb_put/skb_put accept, and no statement between line 23 and line 86 modifies skb or tailen (guard-identity: no drift). On the cow path, skb_cow_data(skb, tailen, &trailer) at line 78 has its failure excluded by 'if (nfrags < 0) goto out;' (lines 79-80) and guarantees tailen bytes at the trailer tail on success. BREAK test (identity/boundary/degenerate/reach) passes; no surviving witness.

Frag-array write. The index nfrags is read from skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags at line 53, unchanged since the guard at lines 29-30 'skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS' which admits nr_frags in [0, MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1], the last valid entry of the MAX_SKB_FRAGS-entry frag array. The written length tailen is bounded by allocsize = ALIGN(tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) (line 37) with skb_page_frag_refill's success at line 41 guaranteeing at least allocsize bytes at pfrag->offset, and the allocsz cap at lines 18-20 bounds the frag-path size before entry. BREAK test passes; no admitted index or length exceeds the shown capacities.

assumptions: skb->data_len is the standard unsigned int sk_buff field and MAX_SKB_FRAGS is the skb_shared_info frag-array capacity (kernel-standard definitions).

skb_page_frag_refill(size) success guarantees at least size bytes available at pfrag->offset, and skb_cow_data(skb, len, &trailer) success guarantees len bytes at the trailer tail and sets *trailer non-NULL (named standard semantics).
pskb_put/skb_put accept a length exactly equal to the available tailroom (len == tailroom is in-bounds).
limitations: No in-fragment producer bounds or derives the magnitude of esp->tailen, skb->data_len, or nr_frags, so the line 18 addition-wrap candidate and any negative-tailen candidate lack a shown producer and are demoted.
NULL esp->esph or unset skb_transport_header at lines 76/82 has no in-fragment NULL producer, so those UB candidates are demoted.

Shell command injection (CWE-78): p is built at lines 57-58 as editor + " " + filename, where editor originates from getenv("EDITOR")/getenv("VISUAL") (lines 20-24), an entry-point environment string. The only guard, strchr(editor,' ')==NULL at line 50, merely routes space-containing editors to the system() branch; it does not exclude metacharacters, so the witness EDITOR="x; cmd" is admitted and system() at line 59 executes "cmd" via /bin/sh. The absent fix is sanitizing/quoting the editor string or invoking the editor with exec-family argument arrays instead of system().

assumptions: omStrDup allocates strlen(input)+1 bytes, giving the line-3 filename a 14-byte capacity (indices 0..13).
getpid() and getenv() results are treated as entry-point inputs per the fragment's own lack of constraints; any value in their declared domains must be considered.

The for loop at line 275 (i < pclrd->numlutents) executes at least once when numlutents >= 1 (attacker-controlled PCLR box value, no shown minimum), and guards at lines 240-241 and 246-247 bound cmptno/pcol only, never lutents, so a NULL lutents reaches the write lutents[0] = ... at line 276 on every path. Reverse scan from line 276 finds no excluding statement between 274 and 276. The absent one-statement fix is a NULL check on lutents after line 274 that jumps to error. This dereferences an unchecked allocation result (CWE-476).

assumptions: dec->numchans at line 233 equals cmapd->numchans when a CMAP box is present, giving the chantocmptlut allocation at lines 255-256 a capacity of cmapd->numchans entries.
jas_alloc2 can return NULL on failure, evidenced in-fragment by the checked call at lines 255-258.
limitations: dec->cdef dereference at line 268 (cdefd = &dec->cdef->data.cdef;) could be a NULL-pointer dereference when a CMAP/PCLR pair exists without a CDEF box, but the NULL value originates only in the unshown jp2_dec_create initializer, so no in-fragment NULL producer is demonstrated; demoted.

OOB reads of pclrd->lutdata (line 276), bpcc->bpcs (line 182), cmap ents and cdef ents are demoted because the arrays' capacities are not established by any in-fragment declaration or allocation; the box parser bodies are unshown.
Component indices taken from dec->chantocmptlut and passed to jas_image_setcmpttype (lines 302-324) are demoted for lack of an in-fragment capacity for the image component array.
dec->image->cmprof_ (line 211) is guarded only by assert(), which is debug-only and not credited, but the fragment shows no subsequent in-fragment consumption of the possibly-NULL value.

The deciding witness (NULL from allocation failure) requires an out-of-memory condition, an environment-dependent trigger rather than purely attacker-controlled input, which is reflected in the confidence band.

verdict.summary: In sctp_setsockopt_auth_key, the guard at line 30 rejects a NULL association only when sca_assoc_id is nonzero AND the socket is UDP-style. An attacker can reach sctp_auth_set_key with asoc == NULL (e.g., sca_assoc_id = 0, or a non-UDP-style socket), where the association key setter dereferences the NULL association, causing a kernel NULL pointer dereference. The missing one-statement fix is an unconditional `if (!asoc)` rejection.

evidence.reason: asoc is produced by sctp_id2assoc() at line 29, a lookup with standard NULL-on-failure semantics driven by the attacker-controlled sca_assoc_id field; no shown minimum excludes NULL. The only guard, line 30, admits NULL asoc whenever sca_assoc_id == 0 (UDP style) or the socket is not UDP-style, because its extra terms `authkey->sca_assoc_id && sctp_style(sk, UDP)` evaluate false on those paths. The NULL asoc is then passed to sctp_auth_set_key, whose name-implied semantics are to set the key on the given association, i.e., it dereferences it (confirmed failure class: NULL pointer dereference, CWE-476). The absent one-statement fix is `if (!asoc) { ret = -EINVAL; goto out; }` replacing the partial predicate at lines 30-32. Witness surviving the BLOCK test: UDP-style SCTP socket with sca_assoc_id = 0 and any keylength in 0..optlen-sizeof(struct sctp_authkey); producer (line 29) -> guard admitted (line 30) -> sink (line 35).

assumptions: sctp_id2assoc returns NULL when no association resolves for the given association id (standard lookup semantics of the named call).
The capacity of the authkey buffer is optlen, established by the kmalloc at line 15, and the flexible key array sca_key[0] therefore has optlen - sizeof(struct sctp_authkey) bytes available.
SCTP sockets for which setsockopt(SCTP_AUTH_KEY) is issued are created via normal non-privileged entry points, and sctp_style(sk, UDP) is a shown branch condition.
limitations: The actual NULL dereference executes inside the unshown callee sctp_auth_set_key; the fragment demonstrates the NULL argument reaching that call via the shown producer and guard-admitted path, but not the internal dereference instruction itself.
A negative optlen passes the signed/unsigned comparison at line 12 but is neutralized in-fragment by kmalloc failing (line 16) before any consumption, so it is not a finding.
The key-length OOB candidate is protected by line 24 (admitted keylength <= optlen - sizeof(struct sctp_authkey)) and was resolved PRESENT after the BREAK test; it does not contribute to the verdict.

evidence.reason: entryPath originates from the ZIP entry filename (line 8, attacker-controlled entry-point data) and its only shown constraints are isEmpty() (line 11, excludes "") and endsWithChar('/'|'\\') (line 16, excludes only trailing-slash paths); no shown statement rejects ".." or absolute prefixes. getChildFile resolves the relative path, so a filename "../pwn" (admitted by both guards, non-empty and without trailing slash) escapes targetDirectory and the result is written via FileOutputStream (line 51) or used in createDirectory/createSymbolicLink. The absent fix is a containment check such as "if (! targetFile.isAChildOf (targetDirectory)) return Result::fail(...)" before use; primary CWE-22 path traversal from unvalidated entry name to filesystem path construction/write.

originalFilePath is the raw, unvalidated stream content of the entry (lines 38-39), and targetFile is the same escape-unchecked path from line 14; a crafted entry can both place the link outside targetDirectory and choose an arbitrary link target, feeding the same missing containment/validation as the primary sink. Secondary sink sharing the CWE-22 root cause.

zei->entry.filename (lines 6/8) is ZIP archive entry data, i.e. attacker-controlled entry-point input, since no shown statement sanitizes or bounds it.
Status checks for stream open (line 21), overwrite/delete (lines 26-29), parent directory creation (line 33), and output open (line 48) are all present and correct.
limitations: entries.getUnchecked(index) is unchecked array access, but no in-fragment producer demonstrates an out-of-range index, so it is demoted, not a finding.
Symlink misuse escalation (writing through the created link in later extraction operations) happens outside this fragment; the shown symlink creation is covered by the path-escape finding.
Absolute-path entry names (e.g. "/etc/passwd") also reach line 14 unconstrained but are the same CWE-22 root cause, not a separate finding.

verdict.summary: In the non-AUTH path, the UTF-8 decoder is called with max_len = (size_t)(p - parser->end), a negative ptrdiff promoted to approximately SIZE_MAX because p < end, so the decoder can read past parser->end when a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence starts at or near the end of the command buffer.

evidence.reason: The buffer extent is established by the loop condition `while (p < parser->end)` (line 12), which admits p = end-1. Inside that admitted range, `p - parser->end` is negative, and the cast to `size_t` promotes it to approximately SIZE_MAX. `uni_utf8_get_char_n` reads up to the supplied max_len, so a trailing incomplete UTF-8 start byte causes it to read continuation bytes past `parser->end`, an out-of-bounds read. The reverse scan finds no guard constraining the length; the `nch < 0` check only runs after the call returns. The absent one-statement fix is `(size_t)(parser->end - p)`. Primary mechanism is an unbounded read size derived from a reversed pointer subtraction (CWE-125).

assumptions: parser->cur and parser->end delimit the accessible command-buffer bytes, as the fragment itself treats parser->end as the one-past-end boundary in the loop and in `if (p == parser->end)`.
The non-auth_response branch is reachable with attacker-controlled command-parameter bytes, since auth_response is parser state and no shown constraint forces it true.
limitations: The size of the backing allocation beyond parser->end is not shown; the overread length depends on the surrounding memory contents.
The oversized `state.poff` written at line 41 is only tracked, not consumed inside this fragment; any later misuse is outside the shown code.
A correct implementation of uni_utf8_get_char_n is assumed to respect max_len per its standard semantics; no non-standard callee behavior is relied on.

verdict.summary: In the interrupted-decode restart path, the body-first loop `do { *--tp = codep->value; ... } while (--occ);` (lines 42-45) is reached whenever `sp->dec_restart` is pending and `residue > occ`, with no `occ > 0` guard anywhere on the path. If the decode request supplies occ == 0 while a restart is pending, the first iteration writes one byte at op0-1 (before the output buffer) and the pre-decrement test leaves occ at -1, so the loop continues writing backward without bound. The absent one-statement fix is an `occ <= 0` early return (or equivalently a pre-test loop), e.g. `if (occ <= 0) return (0);` after the truncation check at lines 19-20.

evidence.reason: Sink: out-of-bounds write below the output buffer. occ0 (and so `long occ`, line 6) is unconstrained for positivity: the only guard before this point is the truncation equality at lines 19-20, which admits occ == 0 (0 maps to 0). With `sp->dec_restart != 0` (produced in-fragment at line 153 with occ >= 1), residue = codep->length - sp->dec_restart is >= 1, so the branch `if (residue > occ)` at line 30 is unconditionally true for occ == 0 and reaches this loop. The do-while at lines 42-45 is body-first: at occ == 0 it writes at tp = op + 0, i.e. *--tp targets op0-1 (one byte before the buffer), and `while (--occ)` then leaves occ at -1 (nonzero), so the loop keeps writing backward and never terminates. No shown statement excludes occ <= 0 on this path; the `while (occ > 0)` loop guard is at line 73, after the restart block, so it does not protect this sink. The missing protective statement is an `occ > 0`/`occ == 0` check (e.g. `if (occ <= 0) return (0);` after line 20) or a pre-test loop form. Primary CWE-787: the write index op0-1 lies outside the occ0-sized buffer whose start is op0.

assumptions: Buffer capacity for all output writes is tracked solely through `occ`/`occ0`; op0..op0+occ0-1 is the writable range.

The shown writers maintain 1 <= dec_restart < dec_codep->length (line 37: dec_restart += occ with occ < residue; line 153: dec_restart = occ with occ < codep->length), so residue at line 29 is always >= 1.

The LZW chain-length invariant (each entry's `length` equals its `next`-chain depth) holds via the in-fragment construction at lines 112 and 120, making the walks at lines 38-40 and 150-152 terminate within the table.
limitations: The occ == 0 witness requires the (unshown) decode caller to pass occ0 <= 0 while a restart is pending; the fragment itself shows no constraint excluding that value, which is why the sink is treated as admitting it.

The codetab indexing `sp->dec_codetab + code` (line 100) is only provably in-bounds using unshown constants (CSIZE/MAXCODE/BITS_MAX) and NextCode's standard bit-width semantics; with standard libtiff values (CSIZE=4096, BITS_MAX=12) it is safe, so this was not used as a finding.
NULL deref and chain-overrun variants of the table walks depend on corrupted chain state that the fragment's own construction prevents; they were not credited.
The raw-buffer accounting at lines 174-175 (rawcc after NextCode consumption) depends on NextCode's unshown body and was not assessed as a finding.

verdict.summary: In the non-AUTH UTF-8 path, the max-length argument to uni_utf8_get_char_n is (size_t)(p - parser->end): with p < parser->end this casts a negative ptrdiff_t to a huge size_t, so a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence split across the end of the input buffer causes an out-of-bounds read past parser->end (CWE-125, via signed-to-unsigned conversion CWE-195).

evidence.reason: Inside the loop guarded only by `p < parser->end` (line 13), the length operand `(size_t)(p - parser->end)` is the negation of the remaining readable bytes `parser->end - p` cast to size_t: since p < end always holds, p - parser->end is negative and wraps to roughly SIZE_MAX. The region valid at p is exactly `parser->end - p` bytes (line 13 establishes the buffer range [parser->cur, parser->end)), so uni_utf8_get_char_n, whose standard semantics read up to max_len bytes to validate a UTF-8 sequence, will read continuation bytes beyond parser->end whenever the attacker places a valid multi-byte leading byte (e.g. 0xC3) at p == parser->end - 1. No guard on any reaching path caps the length at end - p; the absent one-statement fix is (size_t)(parser->end - p). Witness survives the BLOCK test: p=end-1 and *p=0xC3 are admitted by line 13, reach line 19 unchanged, and no shown check blocks them.

assumptions: The command data region is [parser->cur, parser->end) as established by the loop condition `p < parser->end` (line 13); reads beyond parser->end are outside the fragment's declared buffer.
uni_utf8_get_char_n follows its name-implied semantics: it reads at most max_len bytes (and, for a valid leading byte, its continuation bytes) and returns the decoded length or a negative/zero error.
limitations: The downstream trim read `*(mp-1)` (line 56) could also go past parser->end if a multi-byte decode returns a length that advances p past end, but that is a secondary consequence of the same length bug and is not counted as an independent sink.
The exact allocation size of the buffer beyond parser->end is not shown; the OOB claim rests on the fragment's own declared input range [parser->cur, parser->end).
The AUTH branch (line 17) is unaffected because it dereferences only `*p` and never calls uni_utf8_get_char_n.

On the same admitted witness, 'target->len += add_len' (line 35) sets target->len to SIZE_MAX, and this NUL store writes at index SIZE_MAX, requiring capacity SIZE_MAX+1, which no size_t capacity (target->size) can represent or hold. realloc returns NULL on failure and simplestring_init_str initializes an empty string, per standard name-implied semantics.
limitations: The witness rests on the single exact boundary add_len == SIZE_MAX with target->len == 0, hence the capped confidence.
The line 2 dereference 'target->size' before the line 3 NULL test is a real check-order issue, but a NULL target requires an unshown caller, so it is not used as a finding.

verdict.summary: The CoRRE decoder trusts the server-supplied 32-bit nSubrects. The only bound, hdr.nSubrects*(4+BPP/8) > RFB_BUFFER_SIZE, is evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and wraps modulo 2^32, so a count such as 0x20000010 (BPP=32) is admitted and the loop then dereferences client->buffer far past its RFB_BUFFER_SIZE capacity — an out-of-bounds heap read enabled by the integer overflow.

evidence.reason: hdr.nSubrects is entry-point socket data (read at line 9, 32-bit swapped at line 12 via rfbClientSwap32IfLE) with residual domain 0..2^32-1. The sole guard, line 19, computes hdr.nSubrects*(4+BPP/8) in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic: with BPP=32 (multiplier 8), nSubrects=0x20000010 wraps the product to 128 <= RFB_BUFFER_SIZE, so the guard admits it and ReadFromRFBServer(client, client->buffer, 128) succeeds when the server sends 128 bytes. The line-24 loop then advances ptr by 8 bytes across ~536 million iterations, so the line-25 dereference reads past client->buffer, whose capacity is RFB_BUFFER_SIZE per the line-19 comparison — an OOB read (CWE-125) rooted in the wrapping bound arithmetic (CWE-190). BLOCK test: no shown statement excludes the witness; the guard admits the wrapped product, the read status is success, and no other constraint bounds nSubrects.

assumptions: nSubrects is a 32-bit unsigned field (protocol count), evidenced in-fragment by rfbClientSwap32IfLE; the product arithmetic therefore wraps modulo 2^32.
client->buffer capacity is RFB_BUFFER_SIZE, established by the in-fragment comparison at line 19.
The concrete witness assumes BPP=32 (BPP/8=4); equivalent witnesses exist for BPP=8 (multiplier 5, n=0x33333334) and BPP=16 (multiplier 6).
ReadFromRFBServer has standard semantics: it reads exactly the requested bytes and returns TRUE on success; the attacker-controlled server supplies those bytes.
limitations: If a build platform defined nSubrects as 64-bit, the product would not wrap and the guard would be effective there; the shown code only evidences a 32-bit width, so the 32-bit reading governs.
Framebuffer bounds for the GotFillRect calls (lines 17 and 32) are not shown in the fragment and are not assessed.

The exact numeric value of RFB_BUFFER_SIZE is not shown, but the witness's true consumption (~2^32 bytes) exceeds any plausible buffer size as well as 2^32-1, so the conclusion is independent of that value.
